Asterid.name: Asterid
Asterid.publicNotes:
Asterids are nymphs of the stars, serene guardians of clear night skies and isolated pockets of the natural world far from the smog and light pollution of mortal cities. They spend their nights sitting in open fields or standing at the crests of high mountains, their heads tilted back to silently watch the stars go by. The rapturous, dreamy expressions asterids wear during their nightly observations have inspired countless works of art on the themes of beauty and longing.

As asterids are bound to general locations rather than specific natural features, they often must rely on alliances and friendships with other kinds of nymphs to find shelter. During the day, asterids generally end up sleeping in the tree-homes of dryads, beneath naiad ponds, or in the courts of their queens. This, alongside the asterids' generally quiet and gentle demeanor, leads many other nymphs to be somewhat protective of them, especially the asterid queens.

Mortals looking to establish an observatory can ask for no better location than one beloved by an asterid, though they would do well to approach such an endeavor with care and diplomacy. Those who come to the nymph with deference and respect the sanctity of the surrounding natural beauty may earn themselves a quiet but attentive guardian, eager to share their knowledge in exchange for the ability to more closely observe their beloved stars. Those who mar the natural world with excess construction or, worst of all, drown out the stars with excess light provoke the asterid's wrath and find their endeavor cursed with misfortune, if not destroyed entirely by the fury of the nymph's protective friends.

action->Starlight Dependent.name: Starlight Dependent
action->Starlight Dependent.description: An asterid is mystically bonded to a single remote location with a good view of the open sky at night, most often a remote island, mountaintop, or open field. If they aren't in that location to see the sky at night on any given day, they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}, increasing the value by 1 for each night they miss, with the drained value increasing at sunrise each day. The drained value reduces by 1 only when they see the stars again. The asterid can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond to a new location.

action->Knowledge from the Stars.name: Knowledge from the Stars
action->Knowledge from the Stars.description:
Requirements It's currently night, and the asterid can see the sky

Effect The asterid looks to the stars for guidance and rolls a d20. Until the start of their next turn, they can use the result of their roll in place of making a check or saving throw. The asterid can't use Knowledge from the Stars again for 1 hour.

action->Starbeam.name: Starbeam
action->Starbeam.description: Effect The asterid launches a beam of starlight in a @Template[type:line|distance:120]. Creatures in the line take @Damage[5d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:26|basic] save). Creatures who fail their save also become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

action->Starshine.name: Starshine
action->Starshine.description: An asterid's hair and skin always glow with soft starlight, producing 10 feet of dim light and ranging along the same blue-to-red spectrum as natural stars. This is a magical effect that can be suppressed by magical darkness or covered by, for example, a cloak, but never goes out entirely unless the nymph is killed.

Asterid Queen.name: Asterid Queen
Asterid Queen.publicNotes:
Asterid queens reign over entire constellations and clusters of stars reflected in the seas. In practice, they rule mountain ranges, vast swaths of tundra at the Crown of the World, and remote islands far out to sea where the nights are long and dark. Their domains often (though not always) overlap with those of other nymph queens who sheltered the asterid when she was younger and still accumulating power. Asterid queens always remember their friends and return the favors owed with both powerful magic and the divinatory guidance of the stars.

spell->Falling Stars.name: Falling Stars
spell->Falling Stars.description:
Area 4 40-foot bursts

You reach into the skies and call down an array of falling stars that explode upon colliding with the ground. Choose for the falling stars to be airbursts (sonic), asteroids (fire), comets (cold), or plasma (electricity). The spell gains the trait of the falling star type you chose. The four stars' central 10-foot bursts can't overlap. Each falling star deals 6d10 bludgeoning damage to each creature in the @Template[burst|distance:10] at the center of its area of effect before exploding, dealing 14d6 energy damage of the type you chose to each creature in its @Template[burst|distance:40]. A creature in any of the areas attempts one basic Reflex save against the spell no matter how many overlapping explosions it's caught in and can take each type of damage only once.

Heightened (+1) The bludgeoning damage increases by 1d10, and the energy damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Foresight.name: Foresight
spell->Foresight.description:
You gain a sixth sense that warns you of danger that might befall the target of the spell. If you choose a creature other than yourself as the target, you create a psychic link through which you can inform the target of danger. This link is a mental effect. Due to the amount of information this spell requires you to process, you can't have more than one foresight spell in effect at a time. Casting foresight again ends the previous foresight. While foresight is in effect, the target gains a +2 status bonus to initiative rolls and isn't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} against @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} creatures or when flanked. In addition, you gain the following reaction: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.VOEWhPQfN3lvHivK]{Foresight}

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.X9Na6IK8FSPcTuoc]{Spell Effect: Foresight}

spell->Eclipse Burst.name: Eclipse Burst
spell->Eclipse Burst.description:
A globe of freezing darkness explodes in the area, dealing 8d10 cold damage to creatures in the area, plus an additional 8d4 void damage to living creatures. Each creature in the area must attempt a Reflex save.

If the globe overlaps with an area of magical light or affects a creature affected by magical light, eclipse burst attempts to counteract the light effect.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} by the darkness for an unlimited duration.

Heightened (+1) The cold damage increases by 1d10 and the void damage against the living increases by 1d4.

spell->Blanket of Stars.name: Blanket of Stars
spell->Blanket of Stars.description:
A flowing cloak of utter darkness drapes over you, filled with pinpricks of light like distant stars. It imparts the stillness of the cosmos to you, granting you a +2 status bonus to Stealth checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.XMcnh4cSI32tljXa]{Hide} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.VMozDqMMuK5kpoX4]{Sneak}.

While outside under a starry night sky, you're also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} as long as you remain still. When moving under a starry night sky, you're @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} instead.

Gazing too closely into the stars is disorienting. Any creature that ends its turn adjacent to you must attempt a Will save; this is a mental, visual effect.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} and dazzled until the end of its next turn.

action->(Nymph Queen) Tied to the Land.name: (Nymph Queen) Tied to the Land
action->(Nymph Queen) Tied to the Land.description:
An asterid queen is intrinsically tied to a vast, remote location with a clear view of the night sky, such as an isolated island or island chain, a mountain range, or an open plain far from the light pollution of civilization.

A nymph queen is intrinsically tied to a specific region. As long as the queen is healthy, the environment is exceptionally resilient, allowing the nymph queen to automatically attempt to counteract any spell that would harm the environment (such as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.7yWXx3qC4eFNHhxD]{Blight} ritual), using her spell DC with a counteract rank equal to the highest-rank druid spell she can cast.

When the nymph queen becomes physically or psychologically unhealthy, however, her warded region eventually becomes twisted or unhealthy as well. In that case, restoring the nymph queen swiftly heals the entire region.

action->(Nymph Queen) Nymph's Beauty.name: (Nymph Queen) Nymph's Beauty
action->(Nymph Queen) Nymph's Beauty.description: 30 feet. A creature who starts their turn in the aura must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:37] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

action->(Nymph Queen) Change Shape.name: (Nymph Queen) Change Shape
action->(Nymph Queen) Change Shape.description:
Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a more humanoid-looking version of their natural form.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

action->(Nymph Queen) Focus Beauty.name: (Nymph Queen) Focus Beauty
action->(Nymph Queen) Focus Beauty.description:
Requirements The target creature is affected by the asterid queen's nymph's beauty aura

Effect The target falls to its knees and is stunned for 1 hour.

action->Court of Night.name: Court of Night
action->Court of Night.description: The asterid queen opens an entrance to an extradimensional living space @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} within the shadows of the land to which she is bound. She can bring up to eight adjacent, willing creatures with her. This space can only be entered or exited at night, and only by the queen's will.

action->Crown of Stars.name: Crown of Stars
action->Crown of Stars.description: An asterid queen wears a brilliantly shining crown of stars that increases the effect of their natural starshine to 15 feet of bright light and 15 feet of dim light beyond that. The asterid queen can choose to remove her crown with a single Interact action, reducing the effect to that of starshine (as asterid) until the crown is returned to her head.

action->Knowledge from the Stars.name: Knowledge from the Stars
action->Knowledge from the Stars.description: Effect The asterid queen looks to the stars for guidance and rolls a d20. Until the start of their next turn, they can use the result of their roll in place of making a check or saving throw. The asterid can't use Knowledge from the Stars again for 1 hour.

action->Starbeam.name: Starbeam
action->Starbeam.description: Effect The asterid launches a beam of starlight in a @Template[type:line|distance:120]. Creatures in the line take @Damage[9d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:40|basic] save). Creatures who fail their save also become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

Bagman.name: Bagman
Bagman.publicNotes:
Stories abound of fey who steal away people, and many have a grain of truth. No fey embodies the fear in such tales quite like the bagman. These pale, greasy fey are gluttons who delight in eating sentient creatures. They capture their prey within bloody sacks, spiriting them away to murder the victim and devour everything but their fat. That, they save, rendering it into foul alchemical elixirs which they then gleefully sell to the unsuspecting settlement from which they kidnapped their victim.

Bagmen don't need to eat for sustenance, nor do they care for wealth—they merely enjoy spreading suffering. They're masters of disguise and often appear as traveling peddlers of medicinals, wearing deep cloaks and wide-brimmed hats, cruelly offering products to townsfolk crafted from missing loved ones.

consumable->Elixir of Restored Youth.name: Elixir of Restored Youth
consumable->Elixir of Restored Youth.description: Ten minutes after a living creature drinks this elixir, they transform into a young adult version of themself.
consumable->Elixir of Restored Youth.gmNote: The effect is merely cosmetic. After 1 hour in this form, the creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} until they get a full night's rest. The effects of this elixir last for 1 day. Only a bagman can create this elixir using fat extractor.

backpack->Bagman's Sack.name: Bagman's Sack
backpack->Bagman's Sack.description: A bagman's sack functions as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.jaEEvuQ32GjAa8jy]{Spacious Pouch (Type I)}, except that it can hold only sentient creatures or their remains. After it leaves the bagman's possession, it ejects its contents and becomes a mundane burlap sack. The bag has AC 20, 24 HP (BT 12), and can hold up to two Small creatures or one Medium creature; two Tiny creatures take up the same space as a Small creature. If a bagman's sack is lost or destroyed, they can craft a new one with a week's work.

action->A Simple Potion Peddler.name: A Simple Potion Peddler
action->A Simple Potion Peddler.description: A bagman needs only 1 minute (and no disguise kit) to assemble a convincing disguise to Impersonate a merchant and hide their fey qualities. They require the normal amount of time and a disguise kit to Impersonate as anything else or a specific individual.

action->Bagman's Sack.name: Bagman's Sack
action->Bagman's Sack.description: A bagman's sack functions as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.jaEEvuQ32GjAa8jy]{Spacious Pouch (Type I)}, except that it can hold only sentient creatures or their remains. After it leaves the bagman's possession, it ejects its contents and becomes a mundane burlap sack. The bag has AC 20, 24 HP (BT 12), and can hold up to two Small creatures or one Medium creature; two Tiny creatures take up the same space as a Small creature. If a bagman's sack is lost or destroyed, they can craft a new one with a week's work.

action->Elixir of Restored Youth.name: Elixir of Restored Youth
action->Elixir of Restored Youth.description: Ten minutes after a living creature drinks this elixir, they transform into a young adult version of themself, though the effect is merely cosmetic. After 1 hour in this form, the creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} until they get a full night's rest. The effects of this elixir last for 1 day. Only a bagman can create this elixir using fat extractor.

action->Bag Bludgeon.name: Bag Bludgeon
action->Bag Bludgeon.description:
Requirements The bagman has a creature in its sack

Effect The bagman makes a sack Strike against a creature in reach. If it hits, the target takes an additional @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]] damage; each creature in the sack also takes this bludgeoning damage.

action->Bag Prey.name: Bag Prey
action->Bag Prey.description:
Requirements The bagman has a Medium or smaller creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, is holding their bagman's sack, and their sack isn't full

Effect The bagman stuffs the creature into their sack. While stuffed in the sack, a creature is restrained and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}. If the creature [[/act escape dc=21]]{Escapes} or the sack becomes broken, the creature is ejected from the sack's mouth into a random space adjacent to the bagman.

action->Fat Extractor.name: Fat Extractor
action->Fat Extractor.description: A bagman can use the fat of sentient humanoids to create alchemical elixirs. They can create a single common elixir of 4th level or lower, or any elixir for which they have the formula, from a given creature's fat. This process takes 1 hour. Bagmen always know the formula for the elixir of restored youth.

Bannik.name: Bannik
Bannik.publicNotes:
The bannik is the spirit of the bathhouse—also called the sauna or banya—and resembles a wizened little person with wild hair and nails of pine or fir. While domovois consider themselves to be in charge of a home, banniks are the wisest and most respected of the household spirits. Traditionally, the third steaming of the bath belongs to the bannik and their guests (often other faerie creatures), and to interrupt it is a deadly danger.

House spirits are a collection of fey who live among peasants and poor rural folk. They hide themselves from mortal eyes—hence why they're so commonly called "spirits"—but their presence is always felt. Given suitable respect, these house fey take a decidedly parental interest in the mortals they live with, doing all manner of work around the household. They cook, they clean, they sweep, they chop wood, they care for animals, they tend the stove. If disrespected, however, they becomes a veritable plague of ill will.
Bannik.senses: tremorsense (imprecise) within their entire bound bath

spell->Read Omens.name: Read Omens
spell->Read Omens.description: You peek into the future. Choose a particular goal or activity you plan to engage in within 1 week, or an event you expect might happen within 1 week. You learn a cryptic clue or piece of advice that could help with the chosen event, often in the form of a rhyme or omen.

spell->Augury.name: Augury
spell->Augury.description:
You gain a vague glimpse of the future. During the casting of this spell, ask about the results of a particular course of action. The spell can predict results up to 30 minutes into the future and reveal the GM's best guess among the following outcomes: good, bad, mixed (the results will be a mix of good and bad), and nothing (there won't be particularly good or bad results).

The GM rolls a secret @Check[flat|dc:6|showDC:all|traits:secret]. On a failure, the result is always "nothing." This makes it impossible to tell whether a "nothing" result is accurate. If anyone asks about the same topic as the first casting of augury during an additional casting, the GM uses the secret roll result from the first casting. If circumstances change, though, it's possible to get a different result.

spell->Cleanse Affliction.name: Cleanse Affliction
spell->Cleanse Affliction.description:
Gentle restorative magic pushes back the effects of toxins and more complex maladies. Choose an affliction on the target, such as a curse, disease, or poison. If it has advanced past stage one, reduce the stage by one. This reduction can be applied only once to a given case of an affliction, with the case ending when it's completely cured. Although the reduction can't occur again, heightened versions of this spell attempt to counteract with each casting.

Heightened (3rd) Attempt to counteract the affliction if it is a disease or poison.

Heightened (4th) Attempt to counteract the affliction if it is a curse, disease, or poison.

spell->Sound Body.name: Sound Body
spell->Sound Body.description:
You send a surge of healing energy to restore the target's body. Attempt to counteract an effect of your choice imposing one of these conditions on the target: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened}. If you didn't counteract the effect, but you would have if its counteract rank were 2 lower, instead suppress the effect until the beginning of your next turn. The effect's duration doesn't elapse while it's suppressed.

This spell can't counteract or suppress curses, diseases, or conditions that are part of the target's normal state.

Heightened (4th) Add @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed} to the list of conditions.

Heightened (6th) As 4th rank, plus add @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dTwPJuKgBQCMxixg]{Petrified}.

Heightened (8th) As 4th rank, plus add petrified and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned}.

spell->Heal.name: Heal
spell->Heal.description:
You channel vital energy to heal the living or damage the undead. If the target is a willing living creature, you restore 1d8 Hit Points. If the target is undead, you deal that amount of vitality damage to it, and it gets a basic Fortitude save. The number of actions you spend when Casting this Spell determines its targets, range, area, and other parameters.

1 The spell has a range of touch.

2 (concentrate) The spell has a range of 30 feet. If you're healing a living creature, increase the Hit Points restored by 8.

3 (concentrate) You disperse vital energy in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. This targets all living and undead creatures in the burst.

Heightened (+1) The amount of healing or damage increases by 1d8, and the extra healing for the 2-action version increases by 8.

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

spell->Stabilize.name: Stabilize
spell->Stabilize.description: Life energy shuts death's door. The target loses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yZRUzMqrMmfLu0V1]{Dying} condition, though it remains @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} at 0 Hit Points.

action->Boil Alive.name: Boil Alive
action->Boil Alive.description:
Requirements The bannik is in their bound bath

Effect The bannik conjures a plume of superheated steam in a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] within 20 feet. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[6d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:22|basic] save). The bannik can't use Boil Alive again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Boil Alive]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Master of the Bath.name: Master of the Bath
action->Master of the Bath.description: A bannik's bathhouse never encounters random accidents, and any mortal that bathes there receives a +2 status bonus to Fortitude saves against disease for 1 week. An unfriendly bannik can invert their blessing—bathers take a –2 status penalty instead. A bannik must spend a week in a place before these benefits occur.

action->Shy.name: Shy
action->Shy.description: A bannik is naturally @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} while within sight of their bound bath. The bannik can become visible or even selectively visible—allowing only certain people to see them.

action->Tear Off Skin.name: Tear Off Skin
action->Tear Off Skin.description: The bannik makes two claw Strikes against the same target. If both hit and deal damage, the bannik pulls off the creature's skin. The target takes @Damage[1d4[persistent,bleed]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}; if either Strike was a critical success, the target takes @Damage[2d4[persistent,bleed]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} instead.

Baobhan Sith.name: Baobhan Sith
Baobhan Sith.publicNotes:
Undeath is rare in the fey realm of the First World, for that plane's infusion with the raw power of life makes undead uncomfortable at best. Yet a few fey have adopted the vile practices and habits of notorious undead while still being living themselves, as seen in the blood-drinking habits of the murderous baobhan sith.

A baobhan sith avoids confrontations when outnumbered, and although territorial, they won't reveal their true nature to larger groups. They prefer to drink blood from victims they find attractive, and they avoid drinking blood from animals and beasts entirely, as they consider such activities to be uncultured.

spell->Mind Reading (At will).name: Mind Reading (At will)
spell->Mind Reading (At will).description:
With a cursory mental touch, you attempt to read the target's mind. It must attempt a Will save. The target then becomes temporarily immune to your mind reading for 1 hour.

Critical Success The target perceives vague surface thoughts from you when you Cast the Spell.

Success You find out whether the target's Intelligence modifier is higher than, equal to, or lower than yours.

Failure You perceive vague surface thoughts from the target when you Cast the Spell, and you find out whether its Intelligence is higher than, equal to, or lower than yours.

Critical Failure As failure, and for the duration of the spell, you can Sustain the spell to detect the target's surface thoughts again. The target doesn't receive any additional saves.

action->Captivating Dance.name: Captivating Dance
action->Captivating Dance.description:
The baobhan sith sways rhythmically and Strides up to their Speed. Each creature within 30 feet of the baobhan sith at the end of their movement must attempt a @Check[will|dc:25] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Captivating Dance for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round and is temporarily immune to Captivating Dance for 24 hours.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated}, and it must spend at least 1 of its actions on each of its turns to move closer to the baobhan sith as expediently as possible, while avoiding obvious dangers. If the creature ends its movement or turn adjacent to the fey, it is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature must spend each of its actions moving closer to the baobhan sith, and if it ends its movement or turn adjacent to the fey, it is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} until the end of its next turn.

action->Change Shape.name: Change Shape
action->Change Shape.description:
The baobhan sith can transform into a large raven, with the effects from the bird option in the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.NzXpEzcZAjuDTZjK]{Aerial Form} spell.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

action->Drink Blood.name: Drink Blood
action->Drink Blood.description:
Requirements A bleeding creature is within the baobhan sith's reach

Effect The baobhan sith tries to Drink the Blood from the bleeding creature's wounds. The baobhan sith attempts an @Check[athletics|defense:fortitude] check against the victim's Fortitude DC. On a success, the victim becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} and the baobhan sith regains @Damage[10[healing]] HP, gaining any Hit Points in excess of their maximum Hit Points as temporary Hit Points.

Drinking Blood from a victim that's already drained doesn't restore any Hit Points to the baobhan sith but increases the victim's drained value by 1. A victim's drained condition decreases by 1 per week. A blood transfusion, which requires 10 minutes, a successful @Check[medicine|dc:20] check, and sufficient blood or a blood donor, reduces the drained value by 1.

Bogey.name: Bogey
Bogey.publicNotes:
A bogey typically hunts a single creature at a time, usually a small child or elderly person, methodically stalking and tormenting their prey. Often hiding under a bed, amid a dark attic space, or in a closet left slightly ajar, a bogey delights in the slow, methodical cultivation of fear in their victims until the time comes to reap their soul.

Bogeymen are stealers of innocence and devourers of souls. Few targets who survive an encounter with them remain untouched by repeated nightmares, feelings of paranoia, and newly realized phobias. Different names are given to bogeymen according to their varying sizes and degrees of power, which typically grow stronger and stronger as the monsters consume more and more souls.

Many bogeymen look like the mortal folk that they prey on, allowing them to often hide in plain sight.

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Message.name: Message
spell->Message.description:
You mouth words quietly, but instead of coming out of your mouth, they're transferred directly to the ears of the target. While others can't hear your words any better than if you normally mouthed them, the target can hear your words as if they were standing next to you. The target can give a brief response as a reaction, or as a free action on their next turn if they wish, but they must be able to see you and be within range to do so. If they respond, their response is delivered directly to your ear, just like the original message.

Heightened (3rd) The spell's range increases to 500 feet.

action->Devour Soul.name: Devour Soul
action->Devour Soul.description:
Requirements The bogey has killed a creature within the last round and is adjacent to its corpse

Effect The bogey consumes the creature's soul. The soul is utterly destroyed—nothing short of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similar magic can restore it to life, and only after the bogey has been slain. The bogey regains Hit Points equal to double the level of the consumed creature. After devouring three souls within a year, the bogey transforms into a bugaboo.

action->Surprise Attack.name: Surprise Attack
action->Surprise Attack.description: On the first round of combat, creatures that haven't acted yet are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the bogey.

Bogeyman.name: Bogeyman
Bogeyman.publicNotes:
These nocturnal stalkers tail their chosen quarry for days, even weeks at a time, ominously showing up in back alleys, shadowy street corners, and even in victims' own homes before going in for the kill. For unfathomable reasons, a bogeyman may spare a victim's life and instead kidnap them, absconding to a far-off location before returning years later with a fresh bogey in tow. The process of creating a new bogey is little understood by mortal occultists, as those who undergo it have little incentive to discuss the procedure and any who witness it become primary targets for the bogeymen who participated in it.

Bogeymen are stealers of innocence and devourers of souls. Few targets who survive an encounter with them remain untouched by repeated nightmares, feelings of paranoia, and newly realized phobias. Different names are given to bogeymen according to their varying sizes and degrees of power, which typically grow stronger and stronger as the monsters consume more and more souls.

Many bogeymen look like the mortal folk that they prey on, allowing them to often hide in plain sight.

spell->Truespeech (Constant).name: Truespeech (Constant)
spell->Truespeech (Constant).description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

spell->Nightmare.name: Nightmare
spell->Nightmare.description:
You send disturbing nightmares to your target. The next time the target falls asleep, it must attempt a Will save. If you know the target only by name and have never met them, the target gets a +4 circumstance bonus to the Will save.

Critical Success The target suffers no adverse effects and is temporarily immune for 1 week.

Success The target experiences the nightmares but suffers no adverse effects other than unpleasant memories.

Failure The target experiences the nightmares and awakens @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued}.

Critical Failure The target experiences the nightmares, awakens Fatigued, and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} until it is no longer Fatigued.

spell->Vapor Form.name: Vapor Form
spell->Vapor Form.description:
The target transforms into a vaporous state. In this state, the target is amorphous. It loses any item bonus to AC and all other effects and bonuses from armor, and it uses its proficiency modifier for unarmored defense. It gains resistance 8 to physical damage and is immune to precision damage. It can't cast spells, activate items, or use actions that have the attack or manipulate trait. It gains a fly Speed of 10 feet and can slip through tiny cracks. The target can Dismiss the spell.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.sILRkGTwoBywy0BU]{Spell Effect: Vapor Form}

spell->Vision of Death.name: Vision of Death
spell->Vision of Death.description:
You force the target to see a vision of its own death. It takes 8d6 mental damage with a Will save. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by this spell, its vision becomes reality and kills it instantly.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for as long as it's frightened.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Mind Reading.name: Mind Reading
spell->Mind Reading.description:
With a cursory mental touch, you attempt to read the target's mind. It must attempt a Will save. The target then becomes temporarily immune to your mind reading for 1 hour.

Critical Success The target perceives vague surface thoughts from you when you Cast the Spell.

Success You find out whether the target's Intelligence modifier is higher than, equal to, or lower than yours.

Failure You perceive vague surface thoughts from the target when you Cast the Spell, and you find out whether its Intelligence is higher than, equal to, or lower than yours.

Critical Failure As failure, and for the duration of the spell, you can Sustain the spell to detect the target's surface thoughts again. The target doesn't receive any additional saves.

spell->Invisibility.name: Invisibility
spell->Invisibility.description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Knock (At-Will).name: Knock (At-Will)
spell->Knock (At-Will).description:
You make the target easier to open. Knock grants a +4 status bonus to any creature that tries to open the target door, lock, or container with an Athletics or a Thievery check. You can attempt a Thievery check to open the target as part of casting knock, and you add your level even if you're untrained.

Knock counteracts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Azoh0BSoCASrA1lr]{Lock}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.OSapCU8heNHst21y]{Spell Effect: Knock}

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Message.description:
You mouth words quietly, but instead of coming out of your mouth, they're transferred directly to the ears of the target. While others can't hear your words any better than if you normally mouthed them, the target can hear your words as if they were standing next to you. The target can give a brief response as a reaction, or as a free action on their next turn if they wish, but they must be able to see you and be within range to do so. If they respond, their response is delivered directly to your ear, just like the original message.

Heightened (3rd) The spell's range increases to 500 feet.

action->Deepest Fear.name: Deepest Fear
action->Deepest Fear.description: 60 feet. A bogeyman's aura of terror manifests as a shifting haze of images that reflect the viewers' deepest fears. Whenever a creature ends its turn within the aura, it must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:28|options:area-effect,inflicts:frightened] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}. A creature's frightened condition (including from striking fear) does not reduce as long as the creature remains in the aura. If the creature succeeds at its saving throw, it becomes temporarily immune to the aura for 24 hours.

action->Devour Soul.name: Devour Soul
action->Devour Soul.description:
Requirements The bogeyman has killed a creature within the last round and is adjacent to its corpse

Effect The bogeyman consumes the creature's soul. The soul is utterly destroyed—nothing short of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similar magic can restore it to life, and only after the bogeyman has been slain. The bogey regains Hit Points equal to double the level of the consumed creature. After devouring 10 souls within a year, it increases its level by 1, and its statistics improve accordingly.

action->Mobility.name: Mobility
action->Mobility.description: When the bogeyman uses a Stride action to move half their Speed or less, that movement does not trigger reactions.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: The bogeyman deals 1d6 extra precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

action->Striking Fear.name: Striking Fear
action->Striking Fear.description:
If a bogeyman scores a critical hit with a claw Strike, the target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:29|options:inflicts:frightened,inflicts:fleeing] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

action->Surprise Attack.name: Surprise Attack
action->Surprise Attack.description: On the first round of combat, creatures that haven't acted yet are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the bogeyman.

Booted Tom.name: Booted Tom
Booted Tom.publicNotes:
"Don't kick that cat," an elder might warn a young child, "lest you rouse ol' Booted Tom." While most believe the legend of Booted Tom to be just that, a few mortals have received the shock of their lives when they heard a voice whisper, "Pssst, hey you!" and witnessed a feline emerge from the shadows, walking upright and clad in immaculate leather boots.

A booted tom, sometimes referred to in children's tales as a puss in boots, is a restless creature, a master manipulator who finds the maltreated and helps them out of all kinds of trouble, from arranged marriages to imprisonment by abusive caretakers. While the motives of these fey seem benevolent, as with many First World creatures, their methods vary wildly. Sometimes their aid is harmless, yet there's also a tale of an impoverished woman who wished to marry her sweetheart, but her beloved's aristocratic family forbade the match. Her booted tom saw to it that the entire snobby family suffered a series of fatal "accidents," leaving only her beloved alive, free to marry her.

Though the name "booted tom" would imply that such creatures are all male tomcats, in fact, this feline fey can be any gender. Booted toms change form the way mortals change socks. The only thing that remains consistent about their appearance is their very fine, always supple, leather boots.

spell->Drop Dead.name: Drop Dead
spell->Drop Dead.description:
Trigger A creature within range is hit by an attack from an enemy.

The target appears to fall down dead, though it actually turns @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. Its illusory corpse remains where it fell, complete with a believable fatal wound. This illusion looks and feels like a dead body. If the target's death seems absurd—for instance, a barbarian at full health appears to be slain by 2 damage—the GM can grant the attacker an immediate @Check[perception] check to disbelieve the illusion. If the target uses hostile actions, the spell ends. This ends the entire spell, so the illusory corpse disappears too.

Heightened (7th) The spell doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Illusory Scene.name: Illusory Scene
spell->Illusory Scene.description:
You craft an imaginary scene that includes up to 10 discrete creatures or objects of various sizes, all of which must be within the spell's area. These elements generate appropriate sounds and smells, and they feel right to the touch. Elements of an illusory scene are incapable of speech. Unlike with the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.f8SBoXiXQjlCKqly]{Illusory Creature} spell, creatures in your scene lack combat abilities and statistics. Your scene doesn't include changes to the environment around it, though you can place your scene within the illusory environment of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HBJPsonQnWcC3qdX]{Mirage} spell.

When you create the scene, you can choose to have it be static or follow a program. Though a static scene is stationary, it includes basic natural movement. For example, wind blowing on an illusory piece of paper would rustle it. A program can be up to 1 minute long and repeats when finished. For instance, you could create a scene of two orcs fighting each other, and the fight would go the same way for each repetition. If you create a loop, the two fighters end up in the same place at the start of the scene and at the end of it, but you can smooth the program so it's hard to tell when the loop ends and begins. Anyone observing the scene for more than a few minutes almost always notices it looping. You're unable to alter the program after you create the illusion.

Any creature that touches any part of the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. If they interact with a portion of the illusion, they disbelieve only that portion. They disbelieve the entire scene only on a critical success.

Heightened (6th) Creatures or objects in your scene can speak. You must speak the specific lines for each actor when creating your program. The spell disguises your voice for each actor.

Heightened (8th) As the 6th-rank version, and the duration is unlimited.

spell->Flicker.name: Flicker
spell->Flicker.description:
You flicker quickly between your current plane and another. You gain resistance 5 to all damage, except force. At the end of each of your turns, you automatically teleport 10 feet in a random direction, as determined by the GM. You can Sustain the spell to teleport in this way.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.ZlsuhS9J0S3PuvCO]{Spell Effect: Flicker}

Heightened (+2) The resistance increases by 3.

spell->Translocate.name: Translocate
spell->Translocate.description:
You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

spell->Enthrall.name: Enthrall
spell->Enthrall.description:
Your words fascinate your targets. You speak or sing without interruption throughout the casting and duration. Targets who notice your speech or song might give their undivided attention; each target must attempt a Will save. The GM might grant a circumstance bonus (to a maximum of +4) if the target is of an opposing religion, ancestry, or political leaning, or is otherwise unlikely to agree with what you're saying.

Each creature that comes within range has to attempt a save when you Sustain the spell. If you're speaking, enthrall gains the linguistic trait.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and notices that you tried to use magic.

Success The target needn't pay attention but doesn't notice you tried to use magic (it might notice others are enthralled).

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} with you. It can attempt another Will save if it witnesses actions or speech with which it disagrees. If it succeeds, it's no longer fascinated and is temporarily immune for 1 hour. If the target is subject to a hostile act, or if another creature succeeds at a Diplomacy or Intimidation check against it, the fascination ends immediately.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target can't attempt a save to end the fascination if it disagrees with you.

spell->Hypnotize.name: Hypnotize
spell->Hypnotize.description:
You create a cloud of mesmerizing patterns and colors that hovers in the air. Creatures are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} while inside the cloud. In addition, a creature must attempt a Will saving throw if it is inside the cloud when you cast it, when it enters the cloud, when it ends its turn within the cloud, or if it uses a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} or Interact action on the cloud. A creature currently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by hypnotize doesn't attempt new saves.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target is fascinated by the cloud.

Critical Failure The target is fascinated by the cloud. While it remains fascinated, it can't use reactions.

spell->Blur.name: Blur
spell->Blur.description: The target's form appears blurry. It becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}. As the nature of this effect still leaves the target's location obvious, the target can't use this concealment to Hide or Sneak.

spell->Invisibility.name: Invisibility
spell->Invisibility.description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Paranoia.name: Paranoia
spell->Paranoia.description:
You cause the target to see all other creatures as dire threats. The target is stricken by intense paranoia toward all creatures around it and must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target believes everyone it sees is a potential threat. It becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.I1ffBVISxLr2gC4u]{Unfriendly} to all creatures to which it wasn't already hostile, even those that were previously allies. It treats no one as an ally. The spell ends after 1 round.

Failure As success, but the effect lasts 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, except the target believes that everyone it sees is a mortal enemy. It uses its reactions and free actions against everyone, regardless of whether they were previously its allies, as determined by the GM. It otherwise acts as rationally as it normally does and likely prefers to attack creatures that are actively attacking or hindering it over those leaving it alone.

Heightened (6th) You can target up to 5 creatures.

spell->Charm.name: Charm
spell->Charm.description:
To the target, your words are honey and your visage seems bathed in a dreamy haze. It must attempt a Will save, with a +4 circumstance bonus if you or your allies recently threatened it or used hostile actions against it.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you use hostile actions against the target, the spell ends. When the spell ends, the target doesn't necessarily realize it was charmed unless its friendship with you or the actions you convinced it to take clash with its expectations, meaning you could potentially convince the target to continue being your friend via mundane means.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and aware you tried to charm it.

Success The target is unaffected but thinks your spell was something harmless instead of charm, unless it identifies the spell.

Failure The target's attitude becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v66R7FdOf11l94im]{Friendly} toward you. If it was Friendly, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v44P3WUcU1j0115l]{Helpful}. It can't use hostile actions against you.

Critical Failure The target's attitude becomes Helpful toward you, and it can't use hostile actions against you.

Heightened (4th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations.

Heightened (8th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations, and you can target up to 10 creatures.

spell->Illusory Disguise.name: Illusory Disguise
spell->Illusory Disguise.description:
You create an illusion that causes the target to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise is typically good enough to hide their identity, but not to impersonate a specific individual. The spell changes their appearance and voice, but not mannerisms. You can change the appearance of its clothing and worn items, such as making its armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item removed from the creature returns to its true appearance.

Casting illusory disguise counts as setting up a disguise for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} use of Deception; it ignores any circumstance penalties the target might take for disguising itself as a dissimilar creature, gives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through the disguise, and lets the target add its level to such Deception checks even if untrained. You can Dismiss this spell.

Heightened (3rd) The target can appear as any creature of the same size, even a specific individual. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 willing creatures. If you target multiple creatures, you can choose a different disguise for each target, but none can impersonate a specific individual. You can Dismiss each disguise individually or all collectively.

Heightened (7th) As 4th, but you can choose disguises that impersonate specific individuals. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3Ktyd5F9lOPo4myk]{Spell Effect: Illusory Disguise}

spell->Illusory Object.name: Illusory Object
spell->Illusory Object.description:
You create an illusory visual image of a stationary object. The entire image must fit within the spell's area. The object appears to animate naturally, but it doesn't make sounds or generate smells. For example, water would appear to pour down an illusory waterfall, but it would be silent.

Any creature that touches the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) Your image makes appropriate sounds, generates normal smells, and feels right to the touch. The spell gains the auditory and olfactory traits. The duration increases to 1 hour.

Heightened (5th) As the 2nd-rank version, but the duration is unlimited.

spell->Message.name: Message
spell->Message.description:
You mouth words quietly, but instead of coming out of your mouth, they're transferred directly to the ears of the target. While others can't hear your words any better than if you normally mouthed them, the target can hear your words as if they were standing next to you. The target can give a brief response as a reaction, or as a free action on their next turn if they wish, but they must be able to see you and be within range to do so. If they respond, their response is delivered directly to your ear, just like the original message.

Heightened (3rd) The spell's range increases to 500 feet.

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

spell->Sigil.name: Sigil
spell->Sigil.description:
You harmlessly place your unique magical sigil, which is about 1 square inch in size, on the targeted creature or object. The mark can be visible or invisible, and you can change it from one state to another by using an Interact action to touch the target. The mark can be scrubbed or scraped off with 5 minutes of work. If it's on a creature, it fades naturally over the course of a week. The time before the mark fades increases depending on your heightened rank.

Heightened (3rd) The sigil instead fades after 1 month.

Heightened (5th) The sigil instead fades after 1 year.

Heightened (7th) The sigil never fades.

spell->Ventriloquism (At Will).name: Ventriloquism (At Will)
spell->Ventriloquism (At Will).description:
Whenever you speak or make any other sound vocally, you can make your vocalization seem to originate from somewhere else within 60 feet, and you can change that apparent location freely as you vocalize. Any creature that hears the sound can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) The spell's duration increases to 1 hour, and you can also change the tone, quality, and other aspects of your voice. Before a creature can attempt to disbelieve your illusion, it must actively attempt a Perception check or otherwise use actions to interact with the sound.

action->Aquaphobic.name: Aquaphobic
action->Aquaphobic.description: Booted toms, like many felines, dislike water. Booted toms become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} if they take damage from an effect with the water trait.

action->Not the Boots!.name: Not the Boots!
action->Not the Boots!.description: Booted toms are protective of their boots and seek retribution against anyone who damages or attempts to steal them. Stealing or destroying a booted tom's boots leaves them @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} until the fey retrieves their boots or acquires a new pair.

action->Change Shape.name: Change Shape
action->Change Shape.description:
The booted tom changes into their humanoid, animal, or true form. A booted tom's true form is that of a Tiny, upright, booted feline. In humanoid form, the booted tom is Medium size of any common ancestry, but they must be wearing their signature boots. The booted tom's animal form is a house cat walking on four legs. In animal form, they can still cast ventriloquism, which gains the subtle trait. Their animal form is the only time they're seen without their boots, which meld to their body.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

action->Hissed Secrets.name: Hissed Secrets
action->Hissed Secrets.description: The booted tom directs their manipulative fury at any who oppose them. With a hiss, the booted tom throws their voice at a target and whispers the target's darkest secrets directly into their ear. The target takes @Damage[10d8[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:28|basic] save). The booted tom can't use Hissed Secrets again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Hissed Secrets]]{1d4 rounds}.

Bugaboo.name: Bugaboo
Bugaboo.publicNotes:
The more powerful and sophisticated bugaboo conceals themself within larger darkened spaces to stalk their prey. They might be spotted peering around the corner of a dim hallway only to quickly move out of sight, turn invisible, and attack their victim from an altogether different angle.

Bogeymen are stealers of innocence and devourers of souls. Few targets who survive an encounter with them remain untouched by repeated nightmares, feelings of paranoia, and newly realized phobias. Different names are given to bogeymen according to their varying sizes and degrees of power, which typically grow stronger and stronger as the monsters consume more and more souls.

Many bogeymen look like the mortal folk that they prey on, allowing them to often hide in plain sight.

spell->Paralyze.name: Paralyze
spell->Paralyze.description:
You block the target's motor impulses before they can leave its mind, threatening to freeze the target in place. The target must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The target is Paralyzed for 4 rounds. At the end of each of its turns, it can attempt a new Will save to reduce the remaining duration by 1 round, or end it entirely on a critical success.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

spell->Invisibility.name: Invisibility
spell->Invisibility.description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Knock.name: Knock
spell->Knock.description:
You make the target easier to open. Knock grants a +4 status bonus to any creature that tries to open the target door, lock, or container with an Athletics or a Thievery check. You can attempt a Thievery check to open the target as part of casting knock, and you add your level even if you're untrained.

Knock counteracts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Azoh0BSoCASrA1lr]{Lock}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.OSapCU8heNHst21y]{Spell Effect: Knock}

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Message.name: Message
spell->Message.description:
You mouth words quietly, but instead of coming out of your mouth, they're transferred directly to the ears of the target. While others can't hear your words any better than if you normally mouthed them, the target can hear your words as if they were standing next to you. The target can give a brief response as a reaction, or as a free action on their next turn if they wish, but they must be able to see you and be within range to do so. If they respond, their response is delivered directly to your ear, just like the original message.

Heightened (3rd) The spell's range increases to 500 feet.

action->Devour Soul.name: Devour Soul
action->Devour Soul.description:
Requirements The bugaboo has killed a creature within the last round and is adjacent to its corpse

Effect The bugaboo consumes the creature's soul. The soul is utterly destroyed—nothing short of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similar magic can restore it to life, and only after the bugaboo has been slain. The bogey regains Hit Points equal to double the level of the consumed creature. After devouring six souls within a year, the bogey transforms into a bogeyman.

action->Mobility.name: Mobility
action->Mobility.description: When the bugaboo uses a Stride action to move half their Speed or less, that movement does not trigger reactions.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: The bugaboo deals 1d6 extra precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

action->Striking Fear.name: Striking Fear
action->Striking Fear.description:
If a bugaboo scores a critical hit with a claw Strike, the target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:inflicts:frightened,inflicts:fleeing] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

action->Surprise Attack.name: Surprise Attack
action->Surprise Attack.description: On the first round of combat, creatures that haven't acted yet are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the bugaboo.

Cat Sith.name: Cat Sith
Cat Sith.publicNotes:
Cat siths can easily pass for common black house cats, noteworthy only for the white spots on their chests and their unusually bristly personalities. In actuality, they're cunning fey, fully capable of speech, trickery, and even walking upright on their hind legs and using their forepaws almost as skillfully as hands. Cat siths live around highland towns and cities, regularly venturing unnoticed into nearby communities by posing as domesticated felines or using magic to take humanoid form. While some cat siths gather information and undertake tasks for more powerful fey creatures, others serve only their own mysterious agendas.

Cat siths are harbingers of misfortune and find amusement in the unluckiness that follows in their wake. Though rarely malicious, they're fascinated by death in all its forms and may go so far as to steal the souls of those already dying for some inscrutable purpose.

Some foolhardy spellcasters attempt to take cat siths as their familiars, hoping to take advantage of their innate power. A cat sith might temporarily pretend to work alongside such a magic user, only to inevitably lead them toward deadly misfortune and capture their soul upon their death. Rarely does a cat sith's goals align with those of a mortal witch who has sworn fealty to a fey patron, and should they join forces, they become a dangerous force to be reckoned with.

spell->Humanoid Form (At Will).name: Humanoid Form (At Will)
spell->Humanoid Form (At Will).description:
You transform your appearance to that of a Small or Medium humanoid, such as a dwarf, elf, goblin, halfling, human, or orc. You gain the humanoid trait in addition to your other traits while in this form, as well as any trait related to the creature's kind (such as goblin or human). If this transformation reduces your size, it reduces your reach accordingly (typically to 5 feet). This transformation doesn't change your statistics in any way, and you don't gain any special abilities of the humanoid form you assume. You can still wear and use your gear, which changes size (if necessary) to match your new form. If items leave your person, they return to their usual size.

Humanoid form grants you a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to pass as a generic member of the chosen ancestry, and you add your level even if you're untrained, but you can't make yourself look like a specific person. If you want to Impersonate an individual, you still need to create a disguise, though the GM won't factor in the difference in ancestry when determining the DC of your Deception check. You can Dismiss this spell.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.B9Hzt4ki8eqlXxyh]{Spell Effect: Humanoid Form}

Heightened (3rd) You gain darkvision or low-light vision if the form you assume has that ability.

Heightened (5th) You can take on the appearance of a Large humanoid. If this increases your size, you gain the effects of the enlarge spell.

spell->Paranoia.name: Paranoia
spell->Paranoia.description:
You cause the target to see all other creatures as dire threats. The target is stricken by intense paranoia toward all creatures around it and must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target believes everyone it sees is a potential threat. It becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.I1ffBVISxLr2gC4u]{Unfriendly} to all creatures to which it wasn't already hostile, even those that were previously allies. It treats no one as an ally. The spell ends after 1 round.

Failure As success, but the effect lasts 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, except the target believes that everyone it sees is a mortal enemy. It uses its reactions and free actions against everyone, regardless of whether they were previously its allies, as determined by the GM. It otherwise acts as rationally as it normally does and likely prefers to attack creatures that are actively attacking or hindering it over those leaving it alone.

Heightened (6th) You can target up to 5 creatures.

action->Ill Omen.name: Ill Omen
action->Ill Omen.description:
60 feet. Any creature within the area that can see the cat sith must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:21] save or become struck by an ill omen. On a failure, the creature becomes immune to fortune effects as long as it remains in the aura and for 1 minute thereafter. On a critical failure, the creature takes a -1 penalty to attack rolls, skill checks, and saving throws while within the ill omen aura and becomes immune to fortune effects for 1 day.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.zXzXDlh0HkyPJu8f]{Effect: Ill Omen}

action->Cat Sith's Mark.name: Cat Sith's Mark
action->Cat Sith's Mark.description:
A creature hit by a cat sith's claw must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:23] save or be cursed with misfortune. Whenever the cursed creature rolls a critical success on a skill check or saving throw, it gets a success instead. Each day, a cursed creature can attempt a @Check[flat|dc:10] to break the curse.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.zTrZozbWDd1A5L5S]{Effect: Cat Sith's Mark}

action->Steal Soul.name: Steal Soul
action->Steal Soul.description: The cat sith touches a dying creature or the corpse of a creature that died within the past 3 days. If the target is a dying creature, it must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:25] save; on a failure, its dying value increases by 1 (2 on a critical failure). If the target is dead, its soul is automatically imprisoned in the cat sith's body, becoming freed only if the cat sith is slain. While its soul is imprisoned, the creature can't be brought back to life by any means short of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similar magic. The cat sith can hold only one soul at a time and can release a soul as a free action.

Choxani.name: Choxani
Choxani.publicNotes:
Known by mortals as "picture people," choxanis are reflections of natural mimicry and resemblance. They embody a chameleon's camouflage, a cloud that resembles a dragon, and all the other ways the natural world reflects upon itself, coincidentally or intentionally. Choxanis see these natural parallels as proof that all reality, from the First World to the Universe and beyond, has a parallel, repeating structure and destiny. Though rarely concerned with the affairs of deities, considering them merely another manifestation of the underlying nature of reality, they honor this structure itself with religious fervor.

Choxanis are humanoid figures with tough, woody skin and shimmering dragonfly wings. They communicate primarily through hand gestures and the colorful markings that cover their bodies, which can change in an instant to form text or images. Their faces are smooth and featureless, and they're unable to speak or eat—instead, they gain sustenance from the hues of other creatures, unfolding the markings off their bodies to siphon color from their prey. While not all choxanis are hostile, their diet makes most mortals wary—anyone can become a colorless gray husk after finding themselves a potential meal. Gnomes especially avoid choxanis, terrified of having their color drained.

While most choxanis are happy to converse peacefully, especially if interesting patterns or colors are given as a gift for them to consume, their mindsets can be difficult to fathom. Coincidental appearances capture their interest much more than important information or imminent danger, and whole communities of choxanis have been lost to natural disasters while noting that the oncoming tsunami or wildfire resembled the structure of a nearby leaf. Of course, in the First World, they know they'll likely be reborn with their memories intact after their journey through the River of Souls, so perhaps they simply consider a beautiful observation to be worth the price of death.

spell->Augury.name: Augury
spell->Augury.description:
You gain a vague glimpse of the future. During the casting of this spell, ask about the results of a particular course of action. The spell can predict results up to 30 minutes into the future and reveal the GM's best guess among the following outcomes: good, bad, mixed (the results will be a mix of good and bad), and nothing (there won't be particularly good or bad results).

The GM rolls a secret @Check[flat|dc:6|showDC:all|traits:secret]. On a failure, the result is always "nothing." This makes it impossible to tell whether a "nothing" result is accurate. If anyone asks about the same topic as the first casting of augury during an additional casting, the GM uses the secret roll result from the first casting. If circumstances change, though, it's possible to get a different result.

spell->Dizzying Colors.name: Dizzying Colors
spell->Dizzying Colors.description:
You unleash a swirling multitude of colors that overwhelms creatures based on their Will saves.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round, and dazzled for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The creature is stunned for 1 round and blinded for 1 minute.

spell->Guidance.name: Guidance
spell->Guidance.description:
You ask for the guidance of supernatural entities, granting the target a +1 status bonus to one attack roll, Perception check, saving throw, or skill check the target attempts before the duration ends. The target chooses which roll to use the bonus on before rolling. If the target uses the bonus, the spell ends. Either way, the target is then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3qHKBDF7lrHw8jFK]{Spell Effect: Guidance}

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3LyOkV25p7wA181H]{Effect: Guidance Immunity}

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

action->Discoloring Curse.name: Discoloring Curse
action->Discoloring Curse.description:
A creature hit by the choxani's discoloring touch Strike is drained of its color and afflicted with this curse. Nonliving creatures are immune

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:18]

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} and stupefied 1 (1 day)

Stage 3 clumsy 1, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1}, and stupefied 1

action->Hypnotic Colors.name: Hypnotic Colors
action->Hypnotic Colors.description: The choxani swirls the patterns on their skin, mesmerizing onlookers. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:15] must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:20] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the choxani for 1 minute or until they take damage, whichever comes first.

Cu Sith.name: Cu Sith
Cu Sith.publicNotes:
Cu siths are hound-like doorkeepers of remote portals to other planes, particularly portals to the untamed realm of the First World. They're highly territorial and roam the highland moors they call home, constantly on the hunt for any creatures that might intrude.
