Those that bargain with them for safe passage to or from a portal find cu siths to be vigilant (if strict) escorts, keeping their charges safe from extraplanar threats while ensuring they never veer from the most direct path to their destination. Cu siths are highly proficient hunters that offer a single warning in the form of a terrifying bark. Creatures that refuse to flee upon hearing a cu sith's warning bark risk a quick and brutal death.

Cu siths cut imposing figures; they stand as tall as bulls, covered in intertwining roots, plant matter, and shaggy green-and-white fur that terminates in a long, plaited tail. Their fur around their snouts and ears grows long and their eyes glow with a fiery green light.

Some scholars believe that cat siths and cu siths are two sides of the same mysterious coin. While the feline fey proffers naught but misfortune, their canine counterparts will often provide protection to those in need of it. However, both creatures act on their own interests, not wholly understood by mortalkind. And both are the basis of folk stories told around stony hearths and campfires to warn the listeners of the dangers of the wilder spaces of the world. Though cat siths and cu siths have been seen among the highlands, they're almost never spotted together. Many believe this is because the two are eternal enemies, though none have been able to prove this conjecture.

action->Dooming Bark.name: Dooming Bark
action->Dooming Bark.description:
Any creature within 200 feet of the cu sith that hears their Dooming Bark must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:inflicts:doomed,inflicts:fleeing,inflicts:frightened] save. A creature in an area that the cu sith can't easily reach—such as a hidden burrow or enclosed building—gets a result one degree of success better than it rolled.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and immune to Dooming Bark for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}; if already frightened, the creature's frightened value increases by 1, and it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}.

Failure As success, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure As success, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing}.

action->Worry Prey.name: Worry Prey
action->Worry Prey.description:
Requirements The cu sith has a Large or smaller creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} in their jaws

Effect The cu sith viciously shakes their prey. The cu sith makes a jaws Strike against the grabbed creature with a +2 circumstance bonus to the attack roll. If the cu sith hits, they deal jaws damage as normal, maintains their Grab, and attempts an Athletics check to [[/act disarm]] their target of anything it's holding; this attempt to Disarm neither applies nor counts toward the cu sith's multiple attack penalty. On a miss, the cu sith releases the creature.

Dream Builder.name: Dream Builder
Dream Builder.publicNotes: As the gods began to work on the First World in earnest, they created a variety of creatures to handle the smaller tasks. Among these are the dream builders, or byjvilis, small fey who resemble elderly humanoids. A byjvili uses powerful dream energies to create structures of any size within the First World, though they can do so only while they're sleeping. As a result, byjvilis are constantly dozing, only committing to long-term rest when shaping the landscape.

spell->Wall of Stone.name: Wall of Stone
spell->Wall of Stone.description:
You shape a wall of solid stone. You create a 1-inch-thick wall of stone up to 120 feet long, and 20 feet high. You can shape the wall's path, placing each 5 feet of the wall on the border between squares. The wall doesn't need to stand vertically, so you can use it to form a bridge or set of stairs, for example. You must conjure the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost.

Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 14, and 50 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage. A destroyed section of the wall can be moved through, but the rubble created from it is difficult terrain.

Heightened (+2) The Hit Points of each section of the wall increase by 15.

spell->Creation (At Will).name: Creation (At Will)
spell->Creation (At Will).description:
You conjure a temporary object from magical energy. It must consist of earthen or plant-derived matter (such as wood, paper, brick, or stone) and be 5 cubic feet or smaller. It can't rely on intricate artistry or complex moving parts, never fulfills a cost or the like, and can't be made of precious materials or materials with a rarity of uncommon or higher. It is obviously temporarily conjured, and thus can't be sold or passed off as a genuine item. The spell gains the appropriate trait for the item created, typically earth, plant, or wood.

Heightened (5th) The item is metal and can include common minerals, like feldspar or quartz. The spell gains the metal trait if used to create a metal object

spell->Mirage.name: Mirage
spell->Mirage.description:
You create an illusion that causes natural terrain to look, sound, feel, and smell like a different kind of terrain. This doesn't disguise any structures or creatures in the area.

Any creature that touches the illusion or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (5th) Your image can also disguise structures or create illusory structures (but still doesn't disguise creatures).

spell->Create Food (At Will).name: Create Food (At Will)
spell->Create Food (At Will).description:
You create enough food to feed six Medium creatures for a day. This food is bland and unappealing, but it is nourishing. After 1 day, if no one has eaten the food, it decays and becomes inedible. Most Small creatures eat one-quarter as much as a Medium creature (one-sixteenth as much for most Tiny creatures), and most Large creatures eat 10 times as much (100 times as much for Huge creatures and so on).

Heightened (4th) You can feed 12 Medium creatures.

Heightened (6th) You can feed 50 Medium creatures.

Heightened (8th) You can feed 200 Medium creatures.

spell->Shape Wood.name: Shape Wood
spell->Shape Wood.description: You shape the wood into a rough shape of your choice. The shaping power is too crude to produce with intricate parts, fine details, moving pieces, or the like. You cannot use this spell to enhance the value of the wooden object you are shaping.
spell->Shape Wood.target: an unworked piece of wood up to 20 cubic feet in volume

spell->Shatter.name: Shatter
spell->Shatter.description:
A high-frequency sonic attack shatters a nearby object. You deal 2d10 sonic damage to the object, ignoring the object's Hardness if it is 4 or lower.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10, and the Hardness the spell ignores increases by 2.

spell->Caustic Blast.name: Caustic Blast
spell->Caustic Blast.description:
You fling a large glob of acid that immediately detonates, spraying nearby creatures. Creatures in the area take 1d8 acid damage with a basic Reflex save; on a critical failure, the creature also takes @Damage[(1+floor((@item.rank -1)/2))[persistent,acid]] damage.

Heightened (+2) The initial damage increases by 1d8, and the persistent damage on a critical failure increases by 1.

spell->Create Water (At Will).name: Create Water (At Will)
spell->Create Water (At Will).description: As you cup your hands, water begins to flow forth from them. You create 2 gallons of water. If no one drinks it, it evaporates after 1 day.

spell->Frostbite.name: Frostbite
spell->Frostbite.description:
An orb of biting cold coalesces around your target, freezing its body. The target takes 2d4 cold damage with a basic Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the target also gains weakness 1 to bludgeoning until the start of your next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.DdqWMj7cuf4S1bgr]{Spell Effect: Frostbite}

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4 and the weakness on a critical failure increases by 1.

spell->Ignition.name: Ignition
spell->Ignition.description:
You snap your fingers and point at a target, which begins to smolder. Make a spell attack roll against the target's AC, dealing 2d4 fire damage on a hit. If the target is within your melee reach, you can choose to make a melee spell attack with the flame instead of a ranged spell attack, which increases all the spell's damage dice to d6s.

Critical Success The target takes double damage and 1d4 persistent fire damage.

Success The target takes full damage.

Heightened (+1) The initial damage increases by 1d4 and the persistent fire damage on a critical hit increases by 1d4.

@Damage[(@item.rank)d4[persistent,fire]]{Scaling Persistent Fire Damage}

@Damage[(@item.rank)d6[persistent,fire]]{Scaling Persistent Fire Damage (Melee)}

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

spell->Sleep (At Will).name: Sleep (At Will)
spell->Sleep (At Will).description:
Each creature in the area becomes drowsy, possibly nodding off. A creature that falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} from this spell doesn't fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} or release what it's holding. This spell doesn't prevent creatures from waking up due to a successful Perception check, limiting its utility in combat.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes a –1 status penalty to Perception checks for 1 round.

Failure The creature falls unconscious. If it's still unconscious after 1 minute, it wakes up automatically.

Critical Failure The creature falls unconscious. If it's still unconscious after 1 hour, it wakes up automatically.

Heightened (4th) The creatures fall unconscious for 1 round on a failure or 1 minute on a critical failure. They fall prone and release what they're holding, and they can't attempt Perception checks to wake up. When the duration ends, the creature is sleeping normally instead of automatically waking up.

spell->Tangle Vine.name: Tangle Vine
spell->Tangle Vine.description:
A vine appears from thin air, flicking from your hand and lashing itself to the target. Attempt a spell attack roll against the target.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.TwtUIEyenrtAbeiX]{Spell Effect: Tangle Vine}

Critical Success The target gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} condition and takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 round. It can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} against your spell DC to remove the penalty and the immobilized condition.

Success The target takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 round. It can attempt to Escape against your spell DC to remove the penalty.

Failure The target is unaffected.

Heightened (2nd) The effects last for 2 rounds.

Heightened (4th) The effects last for 1 minute.

action->Dreambuild.name: Dreambuild
action->Dreambuild.description: A dream builder can conjure a permanent structure or reshape an existing structure within the First World while they sleep. After the dream builder sleeps for at least 8 uninterrupted hours, the changes occur within 100 feet, with a new building harmlessly moving other objects and creatures out of the space it occupies. There's no limit to the size of a structure or changes a dream builder can make in this way, but more powerful fey can usually negate dreambuilding in their domains.

action->Sleepwalker.name: Sleepwalker
action->Sleepwalker.description:
A dream builder is never fully asleep. While a dream builder has the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} condition but not the dying condition, they can still act. They also don't fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}; drop held items; or take the –4 status penalty to AC, Perception, and Reflex saves, though they're still @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}. While unconscious, the dream builder takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds.

A dream builder's magic functions only while they sleep; they can't cast spells or use magic abilities (except for Sleepy Time) if they're conscious.

action->Slumbersight.name: Slumbersight
action->Slumbersight.description: A sleeping dream builder is aware of and detects any conscious creatures within range. The dream builder doesn't need to attempt a flat check when targeting a creature they detect in this way with a magical effect.

action->Back to Work!.name: Back to Work!
action->Back to Work!.description:
Requirements The dream builder is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} and not dying

Trigger The dream builder begins their turn

Effect The dream builder loses the unconscious condition, can Stand if they're @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}, and Strides or Flies up to half their Speed.

action->Dream Drop.name: Dream Drop
action->Dream Drop.description:
Requirements The dream builder is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} and not dying

Effect The dream builder quickly dreams up a mass of material falling in a @Template[type:burst|distance:20] within 60 feet, choosing to deal either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[4d8[untyped]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:26|basic] save. The material vanishes immediately afterward.

action->Sleepy Time.name: Sleepy Time
action->Sleepy Time.description: The dream builder falls asleep, gaining the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} condition. All other creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] feel particularly drowsy as well and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:26] save against the effects of 5th-rank sleep. Regardless of the result of its save, a creature becomes temporarily immune to the dream builder's Sleepy Time for 1 minute.

action->Tear Them Down!.name: Tear Them Down!
action->Tear Them Down!.description: The dream builder Strides or Flies and makes up to four chisel Strikes against different targets at any points during this movement. The attacks count toward its multiple attack penalty normally, but the penalty doesn't increase until after Tear Them Down! is complete.

Escorite.name: Escorite
Escorite.publicNotes:
The winged silhouette of a descending escorite makes for a terrifying yet beautiful sight that precedes a gruesome end. This enormous fey moth has a wingspan as wide as 15 feet. Equally intimidating are their fleshless horned skull and eerie tendrils that hang from their abdomen.

Escorites are portents of destruction and embodiments of the end that eventually comes to all things. With desolation as their sole priority, an escorite's mere presence accelerates entropy in the area. They irreversibly ruin their stalking grounds, the lingering dust shed by their wings preventing life from flourishing for generations to come. Ironically, however, they have no immunity to their own powers and live only a few years. They prefer it this way. After all, it's an escorite's calling to teach the inevitability of a permanent end to everything, including the immortal denizens of the First World.

spell->Translocate (Self Only).name: Translocate (Self Only)
spell->Translocate (Self Only).description:
You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

spell->Whispers of the Void.name: Whispers of the Void
spell->Whispers of the Void.description:
You whisper baleful secrets that transcend language and carry magically to the ears of your foes. The words take physical form, weakening the life force of the targets, each of which must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes @Damage[(floor(@item.rank/2))d8[persistent,void]] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[(floor(@item.rank/2)*2)d8[persistent,void]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}.

Critical Failure The creature takes @Damage[(floor(@item.rank/2)*2)d8[persistent,void]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}.

Heightened (+2) The persistent void damage increases by 1d8 on a success, or by 2d8 on a failure or critical failure.

spell->Sudden Blight (At Will).name: Sudden Blight (At Will)
spell->Sudden Blight (At Will).description:
You accelerate the processes of decay in the area. Each living creature in the area takes 2d10 void damage with a basic Fortitude save. A creature afflicted by a disease takes a –2 circumstance penalty to this save. You can also direct the blight to rot all Small and Tiny non-creature plants in the area, eliminating non-magical undergrowth and any resulting difficult terrain, cover, and concealment. Sudden blight attempts to counteract any magical effect on the plants before withering them.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10.

action->+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Aura of Inevitability.name: Aura of Inevitability
action->Aura of Inevitability.description: 30 feet. The escorite exudes an aura that reinforces the inevitability of nonexistence. Any creature that enters or begins their turn in the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} on a critical failure). On a successful save, a creature is temporarily immune to the escorite's aura for 24 hours.

action->Deteriorating Flight.name: Deteriorating Flight
action->Deteriorating Flight.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The escorite Flies, shedding dust from their wings, and can move through the spaces of any creatures in their path. Each creature whose space they move through takes @Damage[3d6[void]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:26|basic] save). On a failure, an invisible creature also becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} instead for 1 round.

action->Entropic Flurry.name: Entropic Flurry
action->Entropic Flurry.description: The escorite makes up to four tentacle Strikes, each against a different target within reach. The void damage from these Strikes is persistent void damage instead. Each attack counts toward their multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after the escorite makes all their attacks.

action->Hollow Eyes.name: Hollow Eyes
action->Hollow Eyes.description:
The escorite focuses the forces of entropy upon a creature they can see within 60 feet. The creature takes @Damage[8d6[void]] damage and must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:26] save.

Critical Success The creature takes no damage.

Success The creature takes half damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 1 round.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} for 1 round. A creature reduced to 0 HP by this damage immediately turns to dust, including all items it's currently carrying; the creature can be restored only via a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similarly powerful effect.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature takes double damage and is enfeebled 2 for 1 minute.

Faun Instigator.name: Faun Instigator
Faun Instigator.publicNotes:
Faun instigators are the brash bullies of their kin.

Fauns are humanoid fey with furry goat legs, tails, and horns of varying sizes. Some fauns have more goat-like faces, while others could be mistaken for humans if viewed from the neck up.

action->Keep the Party Going.name: Keep the Party Going
action->Keep the Party Going.description:
Trigger An ally the faun instigator can see is reduced to 0 HP

Effect The faun instigator attempts a @Check[performance|dc:15] check. On a success, the faun instigator grants themself or one ally within 30 feet 4 temporary Hit Points that last 1 minute.

action->Bash Back.name: Bash Back
action->Bash Back.description: The faun instigator throws their weight into their opponent. They attempt a melee Strike, which gains @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.6l7e7CHQLESlI57U]{Improved Push }10 feet. Regardless of the result of the Strike, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of the instigator's next turn.

Faun Reveler.name: Faun Reveler
Faun Reveler.publicNotes:
Faun revelers enjoy life to its fullest, tails swishing as they bask in the sun or enjoy ripe fruits from a tree.

Fauns are humanoid fey with furry goat legs, tails, and horns of varying sizes. Some fauns have more goat-like faces, while others could be mistaken for humans if viewed from the neck up.

spell->Charm.name: Charm
spell->Charm.description:
To the target, your words are honey and your visage seems bathed in a dreamy haze. It must attempt a Will save, with a +4 circumstance bonus if you or your allies recently threatened it or used hostile actions against it.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you use hostile actions against the target, the spell ends. When the spell ends, the target doesn't necessarily realize it was charmed unless its friendship with you or the actions you convinced it to take clash with its expectations, meaning you could potentially convince the target to continue being your friend via mundane means.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and aware you tried to charm it.

Success The target is unaffected but thinks your spell was something harmless instead of charm, unless it identifies the spell.

Failure The target's attitude becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v66R7FdOf11l94im]{Friendly} toward you. If it was Friendly, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v44P3WUcU1j0115l]{Helpful}. It can't use hostile actions against you.

Critical Failure The target's attitude becomes Helpful toward you, and it can't use hostile actions against you.

Heightened (4th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations.

Heightened (8th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations, and you can target up to 10 creatures.

spell->Daze.name: Daze
spell->Daze.description:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Guidance.name: Guidance
spell->Guidance.description:
You ask for the guidance of supernatural entities, granting the target a +1 status bonus to one attack roll, Perception check, saving throw, or skill check the target attempts before the duration ends. The target chooses which roll to use the bonus on before rolling. If the target uses the bonus, the spell ends. Either way, the target is then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3qHKBDF7lrHw8jFK]{Spell Effect: Guidance}

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3LyOkV25p7wA181H]{Effect: Guidance Immunity}

spell->Haunting Hymn.name: Haunting Hymn
spell->Haunting Hymn.description:
You echo a jarring hymn that only creatures in the area can hear. The hymn deals 1d8 sonic damage, with a basic Fortitude save. If a target critically fails the save, it's also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 minute.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d8.

spell->Summon Instrument.name: Summon Instrument
spell->Summon Instrument.description:
You materialize a handheld musical instrument in your grasp. The instrument is typical for its type, but it plays only for you. It vanishes when the spell ends. If you cast summon instrument again, any instrument you previously summoned disappears.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.oarBuzYXLl10pcO9]{Spell Effect: Summon Instrument}

Heightened (5th) The instrument is instead a virtuoso handheld instrument.

spell->Sure Strike.name: Sure Strike
spell->Sure Strike.description:
The next time you make an attack roll before the end of your turn, roll it twice and use the better result. The attack ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the target being @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}. You are then temporarily immune to sure strike for 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.fpGDAz2v5PG0zUSl]{Spell Effect: Sure Strike}

spell->Ventriloquism.name: Ventriloquism
spell->Ventriloquism.description:
Whenever you speak or make any other sound vocally, you can make your vocalization seem to originate from somewhere else within 60 feet, and you can change that apparent location freely as you vocalize. Any creature that hears the sound can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) The spell's duration increases to 1 hour, and you can also change the tone, quality, and other aspects of your voice. Before a creature can attempt to disbelieve your illusion, it must actively attempt a Perception check or otherwise use actions to interact with the sound.

equipment->Aulos (Handheld Musical Instr.name: Aulos (Handheld Musical Instrument)
equipment->Aulos (Handheld Musical Instr.description: Handheld instruments include bagpipes, a small set of chimes, small drums, fiddles and viols, flutes and recorders, small harps, lutes, trumpets, and similarly sized instruments. The GM might rule that an especially large handheld instrument (like a tuba) has greater Bulk. Heavy instruments such as large drums, a full set of chimes, and keyboard instruments are less portable and generally need to be stationary while played.

action->Invigorating Melody.name: Invigorating Melody
action->Invigorating Melody.description: The faun reveler plays a song on their aulos that energizes those around them. The faun reveler and their allies in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60] gain a +5-foot status bonus to their Speeds until the end of the faun reveler's next turn.

Fear Eater.name: Fear Eater
Fear Eater.publicNotes:
Fear eaters are malicious fey who revel in causing fear in mortals, using it to grow strange, glowing mushrooms from the bodies of their terrified victims. While they require no sustenance to live, fear eaters consider these emotion-soaked mushrooms to be delicacies of the highest order. A few have established "farms" in remote corners of the First World, where they hold kidnapped mortals captive and regularly harvest their fears, discreetly selling their produce to influential fey.

A fear eater resembles a grotesque caterpillar, lined with several pairs of arms and many stubby legs. They can be found in a variety of colors, and some exhibit iridescent patterns across their elongated torsos, dyed by consumption of their colorful crop. A fear eater almost always carries a hookah bowl strapped to their side or back, from which they continually take deep lungfuls of a miasma made from spores of their fear mushrooms.

spell->Darkness.name: Darkness
spell->Darkness.description:
You create a shroud of darkness that prevents light from penetrating or emanating within the area. Light does not enter the area and any non-magical light sources, such as a torch or lantern, do not emanate any light while inside the area, even if their light radius would extend beyond the darkness. This also suppresses magical light of your darkness spell's rank or lower. Light can't pass through, so creatures in the area can't see outside. From outside, it appears as a globe of pure darkness.

Heightened (4th) Even creatures with darkvision (but not greater darkvision) can barely see through the darkness. They treat targets seen through the darkness as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}.

spell->Illusory Creature.name: Illusory Creature
spell->Illusory Creature.description:
You create an illusory image of a Large or smaller creature. It generates the appropriate sounds, smells, and feels believable to the touch. If you and the image are ever farther than 500 feet apart, the spell ends.

The image can't speak, but you can use your actions to speak through the creature, with the spell disguising your voice as appropriate. You might need to attempt a Deception or Performance check to mimic the creature, as determined by the GM. This is especially likely if you're trying to imitate a specific person and engage with someone that person knows.

In combat, the illusion can use 2 actions per turn, which it uses when you Sustain the spell. It uses your spell attack modifier for attack rolls and your spell DC for its AC. Its saving throw modifiers are equal to your spell DC – 10. It is substantial enough that it can flank other creatures. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends.

The illusion can cause damage by making the target believe the illusion's attacks are real, but it cannot otherwise directly affect the physical world. If the illusory creature hits with a Strike, the target takes @Damage[3d4[mental]] damage. The illusion's Strikes are nonlethal. If the damage doesn't correspond to the image of the monster—for example, if an illusory Large dragon deals only 5 damage—the GM might allow the target to attempt an immediate Perception check to disbelieve the spell. Any relevant resistances and weaknesses apply if the target thinks they do, as judged by the GM. For example, if the illusion wields a warhammer and attacks a creature resistant to bludgeoning damage, the creature would take less mental damage. However, illusory damage does not deactivate regeneration or trigger other effects that require a certain damage type. The GM should track illusory damage dealt by the illusion.

Any creature that touches the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. When a creature disbelieves the illusion, it recovers from half the damage it had taken from it (if any) and doesn't take any further damage from it.

Heightened (+1) The damage of the image's Strikes increases by 1d4, and the maximum size of creature you can create increases by one (to a maximum of Gargantuan).

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Fear (At Will).name: Fear (At Will)
spell->Fear (At Will).description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

action->Fearsight.name: Fearsight
action->Fearsight.description: A fear eater can smell the presence of creatures with the frightened or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} condition as an imprecise sense at the listed range.

action->Hookah.name: Hookah
action->Hookah.description: A fear eater's hookah pipe allows them to make smoke ring Strikes when wielded in 1 hand. Like a weapon, it can be Disarmed, but it's attached to the hookah bowl strapped to the fear eater's back and always remains in their space, even if they move.

action->Feast on Fear.name: Feast on Fear
action->Feast on Fear.description:
Requirements The fear eater is adjacent to a creature that has a mushroom growing on it from Sprout Fear

Effect The fear eater Interacts to pluck the mushroom and then eat it, regaining @Damage[3d8[healing]] Hit Points. The creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:22] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 1 minute.

action->Sprout Fear.name: Sprout Fear
action->Sprout Fear.description:
The fear eater focuses their mind on a creature they can sense within 60 feet that has the frightened condition. That creature attempts a @Check[will|dc:22] save.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target reduces the value of their frightened condition by 1 as the fear is concentrated into a fungus that bursts forth from their skin. The creature takes @Damage[1d6[persistent,bleed]] damage from the eruption. The mushroom remains for 10 minutes or until a creature Interacts to remove it; if that creature isn't a fear eater, the mushroom withers to nothing.

Critical Failure As failure but @Damage[2d6[persistent,bleed]] damage.

Fetch Behemoth.name: Fetch Behemoth
Fetch Behemoth.publicNotes:
A fetch behemoth is much larger than a stalker and forms from the soul of a Large fey or humanoid.

A fetch is a twisted, deviant simulacrum of a humanoid creature that exists or existed at one point on the Universe. While there are rumors of fetches who are reflections of beings from other planes, if such exist, they must still be duplicates of a sapient creature. A fetch can manifest spontaneously when a powerful person undergoes a significant emotional event or dies, either while in the First World or in an area significantly influenced by that plane. However, they've also been created by potent entities like the Eldest to torment and vex those who've annoyed them. While a fetch manifests from a soul's "reflection," and as such bears a striking resemblance to that soul's appearance, they have no true memories of their own. They hold fragments of false remembrances from their source, as if they experienced them in a half-remembered dream—which ensures the fetch is enraged by and jealous of their original.

A fetch is similar in appearance to the creature whose soul spawned them, except that they often possess fey-like features such as pointed ears, plant elements, or supernatural grace. A fetch who seeks to impersonate a still-living source must take care to hide these features and manifest a fetch weapon that their living template wields.

When a fetch dies, they fade away along with all of their manifested items into a bloom of plant life, their soul instantly recycled into the First World, leaving behind a patch of weeds and thorny flowers roughly in the shape they held while alive.
Fetch Behemoth.saveDetails: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

spell->Cataclysm.name: Cataclysm
spell->Cataclysm.description:
You call upon the unimaginable power of world-ending cataclysms, ripping a small piece of each cataclysm and combining them together into one horrifically powerful attack. The following effects come down upon all creatures in the area. Treat the resistances of creatures in the area as if they were 10 lower for the purpose of determining the cataclysm's damage. Each creature attempts one basic Reflex save that applies to all five types of damage.

  • Flesh-dissolving acid rain deals 3d10 acid damage.
  • A roaring earthquake shakes and bludgeons creatures on the ground, dealing 3d10 bludgeoning damage.
  • A blast of freezing wind deals 3d10 cold damage.
  • Incredible lightning lashes the area, dealing 3d10 electricity damage.
  • Beating winds churn across the sky, dealing 3d10 bludgeoning damage to creatures flying in the area.
  • An instant tsunami sweeps over creatures in the area, dealing 3d10 bludgeoning damage with the water trait (doubled for creatures swimming in the area).
  • A massive wildfire burns in a sudden inferno, dealing 3d10 fire damage.

spell->Detonate Magic.name: Detonate Magic
spell->Detonate Magic.description: You cause the magic within the target to dissipate in a destructive explosion. You attempt to counteract the target. If the attempt succeeds, an explosion of magical force deals 8d6 force damage with a basic Reflex save. If you successfully counteract the magic of an item, it's deactivated for 1 week (or destroyed on a critical success) and the explosion is a 5-foot emanation from the item. If you successfully counteract a spell, the effect ends and the explosion affects either all creatures in the spell's area or the target of the spell and all creatures in a 5-foot emanation around it.

spell->Earthquake.name: Earthquake
spell->Earthquake.description:
You shake the ground, topple creatures into fissures, and collapse structures. The GM might add additional effects in certain areas. Cliffs might collapse, causing creatures to fall, or a lake might drain as fissures open up below its surface, leaving a morass of quicksand.

  • Shaking Ground The ground is difficult terrain, and creatures on it take a -2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls, AC, and skill checks. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.09rtx50laDw68FGT]{Spell Effect: Earthquake (Shaking Ground)}
  • Fissures Each creature on the ground must attempt a Reflex save at the start of its turn to keep its footing and avoid falling into 40-foot-deep fissures that open beneath it. The fissures are permanent, and their sides require successful @Check[athletics|dc:15|traits:action:climb] to Climb.
  • Collapse Structures and ceilings might collapse. The GM rolls a flat check for each (@Check[flat|dc:16] for a sturdy structure, @Check[flat|dc:14] for an average structure and most natural formations, @Check[flat|dc:9] for a shoddy structure, all adjusted higher or lower as the GM sees fit). A collapse deals 11d6 bludgeoning damage to each creature caught in it with a basic Reflex save. A creature falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} unless it critically succeeds and falls into a fissure if it critically fails.

Heightened (10th) You create a massive earthquake that can devastate a settlement. The range increases to half a mile and the area to a quarter-mile burst.

spell->Interplanar Teleport (First Worl.name: Interplanar Teleport  (First World or the Universe only)
spell->Interplanar Teleport (First Worl.description:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.

spell->Truespeech (Constant).name: Truespeech (Constant)
spell->Truespeech (Constant).description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

action->+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Swat Projectile.name: Swat Projectile
action->Swat Projectile.description:
Requirements The fetch behemoth must have a free hand but can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.wQYmDStjdjn0I26t]{Release} anything as part of this reaction

Trigger The fetch behemoth is targeted by a physical ranged attack

Effect The fetch behemoth gains a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses and the projectile was made of stone, the fetch behemoth can immediately throw it back at the attacker as a rock ranged Strike.

action->Create Boulder.name: Create Boulder
action->Create Boulder.description: The fetch behemoth molds a boulder from primal earth and throws it as a rock Strike. A creature hit by the Strike must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:26] save or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Fetch Stalker.name: Fetch Stalker
Fetch Stalker.publicNotes:
Fetch stalkers form from the souls of Medium or Small fey or humanoids. Small fetch stalkers have the same statistics as the fetch stalker below.

spell->Interplanar Teleport (to the Firs.description:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

spell->Truespeech (Constant).name: Truespeech (Constant)
spell->Truespeech (Constant).description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

spell->Illusory Creature.name: Illusory Creature
spell->Illusory Creature.description:
You create an illusory image of a Large or smaller creature. It generates the appropriate sounds, smells, and feels believable to the touch. If you and the image are ever farther than 500 feet apart, the spell ends.

The image can't speak, but you can use your actions to speak through the creature, with the spell disguising your voice as appropriate. You might need to attempt a Deception or Performance check to mimic the creature, as determined by the GM. This is especially likely if you're trying to imitate a specific person and engage with someone that person knows.

In combat, the illusion can use 2 actions per turn, which it uses when you Sustain the spell. It uses your spell attack modifier for attack rolls and your spell DC for its AC. Its saving throw modifiers are equal to your spell DC – 10. It is substantial enough that it can flank other creatures. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends.

The illusion can cause damage by making the target believe the illusion's attacks are real, but it cannot otherwise directly affect the physical world. If the illusory creature hits with a Strike, the target takes @Damage[3d4[mental]] damage. The illusion's Strikes are nonlethal. If the damage doesn't correspond to the image of the monster—for example, if an illusory Large dragon deals only 5 damage—the GM might allow the target to attempt an immediate Perception check to disbelieve the spell. Any relevant resistances and weaknesses apply if the target thinks they do, as judged by the GM. For example, if the illusion wields a warhammer and attacks a creature resistant to bludgeoning damage, the creature would take less mental damage. However, illusory damage does not deactivate regeneration or trigger other effects that require a certain damage type. The GM should track illusory damage dealt by the illusion.

Any creature that touches the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. When a creature disbelieves the illusion, it recovers from half the damage it had taken from it (if any) and doesn't take any further damage from it.

Heightened (+1) The damage of the image's Strikes increases by 1d4, and the maximum size of creature you can create increases by one (to a maximum of Gargantuan).

spell->Ignition.name: Ignition
spell->Ignition.description:
You snap your fingers and point at a target, which begins to smolder. Make a spell attack roll against the target's AC, dealing 2d4 fire damage on a hit. If the target is within your melee reach, you can choose to make a melee spell attack with the flame instead of a ranged spell attack, which increases all the spell's damage dice to d6s.

Critical Success The target takes double damage and 1d4 persistent fire damage.

Success The target takes full damage.

Heightened (+1) The initial damage increases by 1d4 and the persistent fire damage on a critical hit increases by 1d4.

@Damage[(@item.rank)d4[persistent,fire]]{Scaling Persistent Fire Damage}

@Damage[(@item.rank)d6[persistent,fire]]{Scaling Persistent Fire Damage (Melee)}

spell->Illusory Disguise (At Will).name: Illusory Disguise (At Will)
spell->Illusory Disguise (At Will).description:
You create an illusion that causes the target to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise is typically good enough to hide their identity, but not to impersonate a specific individual. The spell changes their appearance and voice, but not mannerisms. You can change the appearance of its clothing and worn items, such as making its armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item removed from the creature returns to its true appearance.

Casting illusory disguise counts as setting up a disguise for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} use of Deception; it ignores any circumstance penalties the target might take for disguising itself as a dissimilar creature, gives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through the disguise, and lets the target add its level to such Deception checks even if untrained. You can Dismiss this spell.

Heightened (3rd) The target can appear as any creature of the same size, even a specific individual. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 willing creatures. If you target multiple creatures, you can choose a different disguise for each target, but none can impersonate a specific individual. You can Dismiss each disguise individually or all collectively.

Heightened (7th) As 4th, but you can choose disguises that impersonate specific individuals. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3Ktyd5F9lOPo4myk]{Spell Effect: Illusory Disguise}

spell->Read Aura.name: Read Aura
spell->Read Aura.description:
You focus on the target object, opening your mind to perceive magical auras. When the casting is complete, you know whether that item is magical. You or anyone you advise about the aura gains a +2 circumstance bonus to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic} on the item. If the object is illusory, you detect this only if the effect's rank is lower than the rank of your read aura spell.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.J6OhRNSN23KzOPRL]{Spell Effect: Read Aura}

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to 10 objects.

Heightened (6th) You can target any number of objects.

action->+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Manifest Fetch Weapon.name: Manifest Fetch Weapon
action->Manifest Fetch Weapon.description:
Trigger The fetch starts their turn

Effect A fetch weapon manifests in the fetch's hand. As soon as a fetch weapon is no longer wielded by a fetch, it vanishes. The fetch chooses the type of weapon they manifest, but it does not gain any of that weapon's standard weapon traits, damage die, or damage type, instead using the traits and statistics listed above in the fetch weapon Strike.

Frog Prince.name: Frog Prince
Frog Prince.publicNotes: Lo and behold the tale of the frog prince, often depicted as a lost royal transformed by vile machinations. His daring, amphibious exploits are all in search of the destined love who'll elevate him to his true form and his rightful place upon the throne—or so it goes. When such stories persist in a region, whether as folk tales about a nearby pond or as placation for excitable children before bedtime, the innocent belief in their plight seemingly invokes an inexplicable, ancient power that gives form to frog princes. These fey appear as unusually large frogs, gifted with a capacity for expression atypical for most amphibians.

action->Watery Demesne.name: Watery Demesne
action->Watery Demesne.description: The frog prince designates an unclaimed body of water (typically a pond) to become his demesne. While in his demesne, the frog prince can speak and gains a +15-foot status bonus to all his Speeds. If the frog prince dies or finds a new demesne, the waters turn murky and putrid for 1 week before returning to normal as it ceases to be his demesne.

action->How Dare You!.name: How Dare You!
action->How Dare You!.description:
Trigger A creature misses a Strike against the frog prince

Effect The frog prince makes a melee Strike against the triggering creature if it's within range.

action->Princely Monologue.name: Princely Monologue
action->Princely Monologue.description:
Requirements The frog prince is in his watery demesne

Effect The frog prince enraptures all those who play audience to his speech. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] saving throw. The monologue lasts until the end of the frog prince's next turn, but he can Sustain it for up to 10 minutes. Each time he Sustains the monologue, any creature in the area who hasn't already attempted a saving throw against Princely Monologue must attempt the saving throw.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to Princely Monologue for 1 hour.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} with the frog prince, but only for 1 round.

Failure The creature is fascinated with the frog prince and can't willingly move away from the frog prince while it can hear the Princely Monologue.

Critical Failure As failure, except the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} while it can hear the frog prince's Princely Monologue.

action->True Love's Bond.name: True Love's Bond
action->True Love's Bond.description:
Frequency once per year

Trigger A humanoid creature who truly loves the frog prince kisses him

Effect The frog prince permanently transforms into a Small or Medium humanoid. He chooses his ancestry and the details of his appearance, and his equipment changes to suit his new form. The frog prince loses the fey trait and gains the humanoid trait. He has a land Speed of 25 feet and loses his swim Speed. He can use his rapier and water jet Strikes as normal. If the GM determines the humanoid creature's feelings aren't true love, this ability has no effect.

Gathlain Wanderer.name: Gathlain Wanderer
Gathlain Wanderer.publicNotes:
Many gathlains leave the trees of their birth to seek lives of exploration and adventure, some even finding portals to the Universe along their travels.

Gathlains have made a name for themselves as inquisitive and mischievous, as well as flighty and distractable. These eccentric little fey want nothing more than to explore the many wonders of the world for their own pleasure.

Born of magical trees in seed pods that float hundreds of miles on the wind, gathlains are a bizarre mix of flesh and flora. Sprigs of mistletoe bloom from their back and form a delicate pair of wings. They enjoy adorning themselves with oddities found on their journeys, such as beads, pieces of fine cloth, and bits of armor. The fey see these accessories as trophies, proof of their travels, and mementos of their adventures.

The typical gathlain is only 2 feet tall, but their small size doesn't deter them from seeking out and exploring potentially dangerous places. They sometimes even use their size to their advantage, squeezing through tight spaces that most would never be able to fit through. Moreover, their vine-laced wings let them reach heights many adventurers would find daunting. These traits have made them celebrated explorers whose presence is welcome in a group of travelers—as long as everyone is prepared for their nigh-endless questions. A conversation with a gathlain can feel more like an interrogation, as they care little for the comfort of others if it means they will learn something new and interesting to add to their store of knowledge.

Gathlains are particularly fond of gnomes, as they feel a sort of familial attachment to their exiled fey kin, and they usually attempt to ingratiate themselves with any gnomes they run across. Gnomes don't always return this affection, and many tend to distrust gathlains due to the smaller creatures' gossipy and flighty nature.

action->Final Jape.name: Final Jape
action->Final Jape.description: When the gathlain dies, their wings explode into a cloud of toxic mist. Each creature within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] takes @Damage[2d6[poison]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:17|basic] save).

action->Forest Passage.name: Forest Passage
action->Forest Passage.description: The gathlain ignores difficult terrain caused by plants and fungi, such as bushes, vines, and undergrowth.

action->Rootbound.name: Rootbound
action->Rootbound.description:
Requirements The gathlain isn't using their wings to fly

Effect The gathlain sprouts woody roots from the tips of their wings that bind an adjacent creature's limbs. The target must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:17] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} by the gathlain's wing-tip vines until the start of the gathlain's next turn.

Gerbie.name: Gerbie
Gerbie.publicNotes:
A lone traveler strays into the woods and stumbles across a circle of mushrooms that tower overhead like trees, each one hollowed out and marked with holes. Numerous pairs of oversized, circular eyes suddenly glow from within the hollows. Within moments, a crowd of small, furry bipeds swarms the wanderer, each resembling a hybrid between a mouse and lizard. And then… the gerbies begin chattering in squeaky, high-pitched voices, bombarding the newcomer with greetings and questions. All welcoming, all smiling, all happy to meet a new friend!

Gerbies live in quaint, communal societies where they craft all their material needs and practice vegetarianism. Knowing that not all places have the privilege of such harmony, gerbies make it their life's purpose to foster peace and friendship wherever they go. Gerbies value empathy and positive communication, and with their natural knack for both, they often appoint themselves as mediators for any conflicts in their vicinity. Conveniently, all it takes is a touch of magical persuasion—and in severe cases, memory modification—to resolve most disputes. Even without their mind-affecting powers, gerbies possess exceptionally pleasant smiles and exude disarming affability.

spell->Truespeech (Constant).name: Truespeech (Constant)
spell->Truespeech (Constant).description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

spell->Calm (At Will).name: Calm (At Will)
spell->Calm (At Will).description:
You forcibly calm creatures in the area, soothing them into a nonviolent state; each creature must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success Calming urges impose a -1 status penalty to the creature's attack rolls.

Failure Any emotion effects that would affect the creature are suppressed and the creature can't use hostile actions. If the target is subject to hostility from any other creature, it ceases to be affected by calm.

Critical Failure As failure, but hostility doesn't end the effect.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.Qr5rgoZvI4KmFY0N]{Spell Effect: Calm}

spell->Charm.name: Charm
spell->Charm.description:
To the target, your words are honey and your visage seems bathed in a dreamy haze. It must attempt a Will save, with a +4 circumstance bonus if you or your allies recently threatened it or used hostile actions against it.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you use hostile actions against the target, the spell ends. When the spell ends, the target doesn't necessarily realize it was charmed unless its friendship with you or the actions you convinced it to take clash with its expectations, meaning you could potentially convince the target to continue being your friend via mundane means.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and aware you tried to charm it.

Success The target is unaffected but thinks your spell was something harmless instead of charm, unless it identifies the spell.

Failure The target's attitude becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v66R7FdOf11l94im]{Friendly} toward you. If it was Friendly, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v44P3WUcU1j0115l]{Helpful}. It can't use hostile actions against you.

Critical Failure The target's attitude becomes Helpful toward you, and it can't use hostile actions against you.

Heightened (4th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations.

Heightened (8th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations, and you can target up to 10 creatures.

action->All My Favorite Things!.name: All My Favorite Things!
action->All My Favorite Things!.description:
The gerbie overloads the mind of a creature within 100 feet with thoughts of sunny days, of cute fauna and beautiful flora, of frolicking in fields, and of many other pleasant things. The creature takes @Damage[4d6[mental]] damage and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} and stupefied 1 for 1 round.

action->Forget Now.name: Forget Now
action->Forget Now.description: The gerbie attempts a jaws Strike. If the Strike hits, the gerbie affects the creature they just attacked with Make it All Better to make it forget the attack.

action->Friendship Aura.name: Friendship Aura
action->Friendship Aura.description:
30 feet. When a creature enters or starts its turn in the gerbie's friendship aura, it attempts a @Check[will|dc:21] save.

Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to this gerbie's friendship aura for 24 hours.

Failure The creature is unable to take hostile actions toward the gerbie until it leaves the aura or until the gerbie targets it with a hostile action.

Critical Failure The creature is unable to take hostile actions toward anyone in the friendship aura until it leaves the aura.

action->Make it All Better.name: Make it All Better
action->Make it All Better.description: Effect The gerbie touches a creature and causes it to forget something, suppressing all memory of a particular topic, detailed in 50 words or fewer. If the creature is unwilling, it can attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] save to negate the effect. A creature with a memory altered this way can attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] save to regain the original memory each morning.

Goodfellow.name: Goodfellow
Goodfellow.publicNotes:
Every royal court needs a fool, both to entertain and to humble the mighty with the blade of cutting wit. Among the nobles of the First World, the fey most favored to fill this important role are the charming, mischievous goodfellows. Their favorite targets for pranks are mortals they deem "too uptight." Fey nobles fully expect they, too, will be targets of pranks, though goodfellows wisely keep these on the harmless side. That said, their chaotic whims might strike at any time, and they can't be fully trusted with anything but mischief.

Goodfellows average around 4 to 5 feet tall, with skin that ranges from red to brown and full heads of wild, feathery hair that run a similar spectrum.

spell->Blister.name: Blister
spell->Blister.description:
You point at a target in range, and its skin grows searing blisters filled with caustic fluid. The target must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target grows one blister. You can spend a single action, which has the concentrate trait, to pop a blister. The target and each creature in a @Template[cone|distance:15] originating from the target takes 7d6 acid damage (basic Fortitude save). You choose the direction of the cone, which can't include the target. When no blisters are left, the spell ends.

Failure As success, but the target grows two blisters.

Critical Failure As success, but the target grows four blisters.

Heightened (+1) The damage of a popped blister increases by 1d6.

spell->Magic Passage.name: Magic Passage
spell->Magic Passage.description:
You create a visible tunnel through the wall in the chosen area, replacing the area with empty space. If the wall is thicker than 10 feet, the tunnel ends 10 feet in. Even a small layer of metal in the wall prevents this spell from functioning. This spell doesn't reduce the integrity of the structure. When the spell ends, anyone inside the tunnel is shunted to the nearest exit.

Heightened (7th) The tunnel can be up to 20 feet deep. The areas of the wall that contain your tunnel's entrance appear completely normal (unless viewed with truesight or a similar effect), despite the tunnel's existence. The tunnel's entrance functions as a solid wall, but you can specify a password or a trigger, allowing creatures to enter freely.

spell->Fly.name: Fly
spell->Fly.description:
The target can soar through the air, gaining a fly Speed equal to its Speed or 20 feet, whichever is greater.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.MuRBCiZn5IKeaoxi]{Spell Effect: Fly}

Heightened (7th) The duration increases to 1 hour.

spell->Mirage.name: Mirage
spell->Mirage.description:
You create an illusion that causes natural terrain to look, sound, feel, and smell like a different kind of terrain. This doesn't disguise any structures or creatures in the area.

Any creature that touches the illusion or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (5th) Your image can also disguise structures or create illusory structures (but still doesn't disguise creatures).

spell->Curse of Lost Time.name: Curse of Lost Time
spell->Curse of Lost Time.description:
You curse the target with rapid aging or erosion. The effect depends on whether the target is an object, a construct, or a living creature. Artifacts, along with objects and constructs made of precious materials (as determined by the GM), are immune.

  • Object If the object is attended, its bearer can attempt a Fortitude save. If the bearer fails or the object is unattended, the object immediately takes 4d6 damage (applying Hardness normally) and the item is cursed with an unlimited duration. Until the curse ends, the item becomes shoddy and can't be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.bT3skovyLUtP22ME]{Repaired}, and the curse attempts to counteract any spell that would restore the object's Hit Points. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction} can target an item affected by this spell.
  • Construct The construct takes 4d6 damage (basic Fortitude save). On a failure, for 1 hour the construct is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}, is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1}, and can't be Repaired, and the curse attempts to counteract any spell that would restore the construct's Hit Points. On a critical failure, these effects have an unlimited duration.
  • Living Creature The living creature must attempt a Fortitude save. Ageless creatures are immune.
    • Critical Success The living creature is unaffected.
    • Success The living creature briefly ages, becoming clumsy 1 and enfeebled 1 for 1 round.
    • Failure As success, with a duration of 1 hour.
    • Critical Failure As success, with an unlimited duration.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.
spell->Curse of Lost Time.target: 1 Large or smaller object, construct, or living creature

spell->Haste.name: Haste
spell->Haste.description:
Magic empowers the target to act faster. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} condition and can use the extra action each round only for Strike and Stride actions.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 6 creatures.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.ElkXovNrHB0Doi6O]{Spell Effect: Haste}

spell->Mad Monkeys.name: Mad Monkeys
spell->Mad Monkeys.description:
Magical monkey spirits fill the area as they pile and climb on top of one another. Because the monkeys are magical spirits, they can't be attacked or hurt. Casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.b515AZlB0sridKSq]{Calm} or a similar effect over the monkeys makes them docile, causing them to cease making mischief for the duration of mad monkeys.

Choose the kind of mischief your monkeys make when you Cast the Spell. They produce the effect listed for that mischief when you Cast the Spell and the first time each round when you Sustain the Spell. The first time each round when you Sustain the Spell, you can move the area of the monkeys by 5 feet.

Flagrant Burglary The monkeys try to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.RDXXE7wMrSPCLv5k]{Steal} any one item from one creature in the area. Use your spell DC - 10 as the monkeys' Thievery modifier. Their attempt relies more on distraction than subtlety, so the victim knows what item the monkeys were trying to take and whether it was taken. Getting a stolen item from the monkeys-even for the caster-requires Stealing it from them or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarming} them, using your spell DC. When the spell ends, any stolen items fall to the ground in any square of the spell's area you choose.

Raucous Din The monkeys screech loudly, potentially deafening creatures in the spell's area. Each creature in the spell's area must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 10 minutes.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature is Deafened for 1 minute.

Tumultuous Gymnastics The monkeys jump and climb all over creatures in the spell's area, interfering with complex movements. Each creature in the spell's area must attempt a Reflex save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 10 minutes.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure For 1 round, the creature must succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:5] whenever it attempts a manipulate action. If it fails this check, the creature loses that action.

Critical Failure As failure, but the monkeys cling to the creature tenaciously, and the effect lasts until the spell ends, even if the creature leaves the spell's area.

spell->Animal Messenger.name: Animal Messenger
spell->Animal Messenger.description:
You offer food, and an ordinary Tiny animal within range approaches to eat it. You imprint the image, direction, and distance of an obvious place or landmark well known to you within the animal. You can also attach a small object or note up to light Bulk to it. The animal does its best to reach the destination; if it makes it there, it waits nearby and allows nonhostile creatures to approach and remove the attached object. The spell ends after the message is delivered or after 24 hours, whichever comes first.

If there are no Tiny wild animals in range, the spell is lost.

spell->Deafness.name: Deafness
spell->Deafness.description:
The target loses hearing; it must attempt a Fortitude save. The target is then temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 round.

Failure The target is Deafened for 10 minutes.

Critical Failure The target is Deafened permanently.

spell->Humanoid Form.name: Humanoid Form
spell->Humanoid Form.description:
You transform your appearance to that of a Small or Medium humanoid, such as a dwarf, elf, goblin, halfling, human, or orc. You gain the humanoid trait in addition to your other traits while in this form, as well as any trait related to the creature's kind (such as goblin or human). If this transformation reduces your size, it reduces your reach accordingly (typically to 5 feet). This transformation doesn't change your statistics in any way, and you don't gain any special abilities of the humanoid form you assume. You can still wear and use your gear, which changes size (if necessary) to match your new form. If items leave your person, they return to their usual size.

Humanoid form grants you a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to pass as a generic member of the chosen ancestry, and you add your level even if you're untrained, but you can't make yourself look like a specific person. If you want to Impersonate an individual, you still need to create a disguise, though the GM won't factor in the difference in ancestry when determining the DC of your Deception check. You can Dismiss this spell.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.B9Hzt4ki8eqlXxyh]{Spell Effect: Humanoid Form}

Heightened (3rd) You gain darkvision or low-light vision if the form you assume has that ability.

Heightened (5th) You can take on the appearance of a Large humanoid. If this increases your size, you gain the effects of the enlarge spell.

spell->Invisibility (At Will, Self Only).name: Invisibility (At Will, Self Only)
spell->Invisibility (At Will, Self Only).description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
spell->Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an invisibility potion) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

spell->Gentle Landing.name: Gentle Landing
spell->Gentle Landing.description:
Trigger a creature within range is falling

You raise a magical updraft to arrest a fall. The target's fall slows to 60 feet per round, and the portion of the fall during the spell's duration doesn't count when calculating falling damage. If the target reaches the ground while the spell is in effect, it takes no damage from the fall. The spell ends as soon as the target lands.

spell->Mending.name: Mending
spell->Mending.description:
You repair the target item. You restore 5 Hit Points per spell rank to the target, potentially removing the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken} condition if this repairs it past the item's Broken Threshold. You can't replace lost pieces or repair an object that's been completely destroyed.

Heightened (2nd) You can target a non-magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Heightened (3rd) You can target a non-magical object of 2 Bulk or less, or a magical object of 1 Bulk or less.
spell->Mending.target: non-magical object of light Bulk or less

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

spell->Puff of Poison.name: Puff of Poison
spell->Puff of Poison.description:
You exhale a shimmering cloud of toxic breath at an enemy's face. The target takes 1d4 poison damage and @Damage[(ceil(@item.level/2))d4[persistent,poison]], depending on its Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The target takes half initial damage and no persistent damage.

Failure The target takes full initial and persistent damage.

Critical Failure The target takes double initial and persistent damage.

Heightened (+2) The initial poison damage increases by 1d4, and the persistent poison damage increases by 1d4.

spell->Summon Instrument.name: Summon Instrument
spell->Summon Instrument.description:
You materialize a handheld musical instrument in your grasp. The instrument is typical for its type, but it plays only for you. It vanishes when the spell ends. If you cast summon instrument again, any instrument you previously summoned disappears.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.oarBuzYXLl10pcO9]{Spell Effect: Summon Instrument}

Heightened (5th) The instrument is instead a virtuoso handheld instrument.

action->Lost with their Fears.name: Lost with their Fears
action->Lost with their Fears.description:
Frequency once per round

Requirements The goodfellow's aura is active

Effect All frightened enemies within the aura take @Damage[4d8[mental]] damage with a basic @Check[will|dc:28] save. A creature who critically succeeds at this basic save also becomes temporarily immune to this goodfellow's aura for 1 hour.

action->Through Bog, Through Bush, Throu.name: Through Bog, Through Bush, Through Brake, Through Briar
action->Through Bog, Through Bush, Throu.description:
