The goodfellow Strides and takes on the illusory appearance of a gruesome and terrifying creature, such as a rabid dog, a headless bear, or a rampaging living fire. They gain a terrifying aura in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60] that lasts for 1 minute and can be Dismissed. A frightened creature in this aura doesn't reduce its frightened value at the end of its turn. An enemy who enters or begins its turn in this aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28] saving throw.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and temporarily immune to this effect for 1 hour.

Success The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target becomes frightened 2 and can't use reactions until the end of their next turn.
action->Through Bog, Through Bush, Throu.selfEffect: Effect: Through Bog, Through Bush, Through Brake, Through Briar

Green Knight.name: Green Knight
Green Knight.publicNotes:
Consider a lord on a festival day, fair-faced and merry in his cups, extending his largess to any who please him. Consider that lord on a harvest day, a tyrant in the fields, demanding work he would not do himself. Consider that lord on his commendation day, swearing to protect and nurture the lands and its people in exchange for fealty and troth from those very same subjects.

Consider a green knight, great and green of skin and green of armor, who might appear on such a day to that lord.

The green knights are avatars of honor and of one's word given and kept. They're duty-bound to ensure others, especially those of high station, hold true to the promises they make. Sallying forth from their keeps in the depths of the First World, the green knights arrive anywhere nobility falters: where a lord forgets his vassal vows, a knight wavers in her cause, or an oath maker finds themself on the path of betrayal, a green knight arrives to test their worth. They serve as self-appointed judge, jury, and sometimes executioner, offering boons to those who pass their tests and banes for those who fail.

The greatest among the green knights answer to Magdh herself, who sends them forth to judge and guide mortals who find themselves at such crossroads. Some answer to different Eldest or to older and stranger powers, and others follow only their own codes. Even those green knights who swear no fealty to a higher power, however, have the uncanny ability to find those most deserving of their judgment.

Green knights tower over those they challenge, standing 8 feet tall or more and wearing thick green armor that makes them seem larger still. Despite their intimidating presence, they're genteel and graceful, with perfectly coiffed hair, elegantly trimmed beard, and flawless etiquette. They invariably carry massive bronze axes, symbols of their station, but—as courtly graces demand—they rarely brandish their weapons unless faced with harm. However, should someone be foolhardy enough to challenge a green knight to martial combat, they might find their head quickly and cleanly severed from their body with one mighty blow from that axe.

spell->Interplanar Teleport (To the Firs.name: Interplanar Teleport (To the First World or Universe only)
spell->Interplanar Teleport (To the Firs.description:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.

spell->Truespeech (Constant).name: Truespeech (Constant)
spell->Truespeech (Constant).description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

spell->Fly.name: Fly
spell->Fly.description:
The target can soar through the air, gaining a fly Speed equal to its Speed or 20 feet, whichever is greater.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.MuRBCiZn5IKeaoxi]{Spell Effect: Fly}

Heightened (7th) The duration increases to 1 hour.

weapon->Gallant Axe.name: Gallant Axe
weapon->Gallant Axe.description: This large battle axe is too heavy to wield with only one hand. Many greataxes incorporate two blades, and they are often "bearded," having a hook at the bottom to increase the strength of their chopping power.

action->Courtly Judgment.name: Courtly Judgment
action->Courtly Judgment.description: A green knight senses the mettle of all creatures with a glance that pierces the soul. They know the edicts and anathema, if any, of all creatures they can see.

action->Decapitation Immunity.name: Decapitation Immunity
action->Decapitation Immunity.description: A green knight doesn't automatically die if they're decapitated (such as by a vorpal weapon). They continue to see and use their other senses through their severed head.

action->No Succor.name: No Succor
action->No Succor.description:
Trigger A creature within reach uses a move action and ends its movement further from the green knight than it started

Effect The green knight teleports to a free space adjacent to the triggering creature.

action->Twelvemonth and a Day.name: Twelvemonth and a Day
action->Twelvemonth and a Day.description:
Frequency once per year and a day

Trigger The green knight is reduced to 0 Hit Points by an attack or spell

Effect The green knight returns to life with full Hit Points, points at the creature responsible for their death, and vanishes, returning to the First World. Exactly a year and a day later, they reappear in the nearest free space to the creature they pointed at. The green knight immediately targets them with the triggering attack or spell as a free action, either immediately or as soon as the target is within range. The attack or spell uses the same attack modifier, save DC, damage, and any other effects as the triggering effect, but the green knight gets a result on their attack roll one degree of success better than they rolled or the target gets a result on their save one degree of success worse than they rolled.

action->Courtly Game.name: Courtly Game
action->Courtly Game.description:
Frequency once per year and a day

Effect The green knight offers a test to a creature they can see, challenging them to live up to their ideals. The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:35] save. If they fail, they must choose one of two paths.

  • Brave, Bold, and Courteous The target upholds their edicts and anathema at great personal cost. They immediately receive a grievous blow that reduces them to 0 Hit Points and makes them dying 3 but suffer no further effects; the target's initiative position moves directly before the green knight's turn, as usual. If the target and the green knight are both still alive 14 days later, the green knight appears before them and offers a reward.

  • Fallen Knight The target strays from its path, possibly falling from grace. For the next year and a day, the target must attempt a @Check[flat|dc:5] before using any ability granted by a class, archetype, or other feature that imposes edicts or anathema. On a failure, the ability has no effect. If the target's abilities don't rely on upholding edicts or anathema (or that target has no edicts or anathema), the target instead takes a –1 penalty to Will saves for the duration. In addition, the green knight can communicate telepathically with the creature for the duration, regardless of distance, as long as both are in either the First World or the Universe.

action->Cry of Challenge.name: Cry of Challenge
action->Cry of Challenge.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The green knight issues a challenge in a booming voice, daring their foes to face them. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:34] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the green knight for 1 minute. This fascinated condition doesn't end if the green knight uses hostile actions against the creature or its allies (though it still ends if any other enemy does so).

action->Gallant Axe.name: Gallant Axe
action->Gallant Axe.description: The green knight's axe is the symbol of their power and judgment. While they or a creature cursed by their Courtly Game wields it, it gains the vorpal rune, which doesn't count against its maximum number of property runes.

action->Pronounce Judgment.name: Pronounce Judgment
action->Pronounce Judgment.description: The subject of the green knight's game can't escape them. The green knight Strides twice then makes a melee Strike against a creature cursed by their Courtly Game.

action->Whirling Blow.name: Whirling Blow
action->Whirling Blow.description: The green knight makes a melee Strike against each creature within reach. These attacks count towards the green knight's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the green knight makes all their attacks.

Gremlin Swarm.name: Gremlin Swarm
Gremlin Swarm.publicNotes:
Most gremlins are communal creatures, dwelling in gangs, mobs, and hives just out of mortal sight. These groups are often contentious, each gremlin believing they are taking advantage of the rest, yet they never live alone if they can help it.

On occasion, an entire mass of gremlins can be roused to anger. Such a swarm is surprisingly coordinated and effective, driven not by any one gremlin's leadership but by their excellent instincts for causing trouble. Gremlin swarms cooperate easily to bring down much larger foes, trussing them up like a holiday goose or poking them with knives and claws until they stop twitching.

Like many fey, gremlins personify a natural force of the world: entropy. It's a fundamental truth that everything breaks, that every complex system, from a machine to a society, will inevitably grind itself down to nothing. Gremlins are happy to give those complex systems a friendly shove down the stairs.

Nearly all gremlins live in the Universe, where they have fully acclimated to the plane. No one is quite certain why, but it seems likely that some long-forgotten gremlin managed to so irritate the Eldest to such a degree that their entire species was exiled—though it appears the Eldest missed a few, as some gremlins still lurk in the First World.

Gremlins are usually found in an odd, parasitic relationship with mortal communities in the Universe. They don't need to eat or sleep, don't age or sicken, and never really die—but they do need to cause trouble. It's as essential to them as food and drink are to mortals, and nowhere do they get as many chances for chaos and confusion as in a mortal settlement. Gremlins thus become pests, living on the margins of society and bedeviling anyone and anything they can get their hands on.

action->Absolute Nuisances.name: Absolute Nuisances
action->Absolute Nuisances.description: 5 feet. The gremlin swarm constantly harasses nearby creatures to break their concentration, kicking shins and screaming in ears. A creature in the aura taking a concentrate action, must first succeed at a @Check[will|dc:18] save or lose the action. Creatures occupying the gremlin swarm's space take a –2 circumstance penalty to this save.

action->Clever Little Monsters.name: Clever Little Monsters
action->Clever Little Monsters.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The gremlin swarm cooperates to harass a foe, attempting to [[/act disarm]], [[/act grapple]], [[/act shove]], or [[/act trip]] a creature that occupies the swarm's space. The swarm can use their Thievery ( [[/act disarm skill=thievery]], [[/act grapple skill=thievery]], [[/act shove skill=thievery]], or [[/act trip skill=thievery]]) modifier, rather than Athletics, for the skill check for this action.

action->Grem-a-pult.name: Grem-a-pult
action->Grem-a-pult.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The gremlin swarm hurls a hapless "volunteer" at the enemy. Each creature in a @Template[type:burst|distance:5] within 30 feet takes @Damage[3d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save). A creature who critically fails the save is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round. The gremlin swarm then loses @Damage[1d4[healing]|options:area-damage] Hit Points as the gremlin scuttles back injured.

action->Swarming Blows.name: Swarming Blows
action->Swarming Blows.description: Each enemy in the mob's space takes @Damage[2d8[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save). A creature that fails this save is also knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Grit Flinger.name: Grit Flinger
Grit Flinger.publicNotes:
These pink- and peach-furred fey resemble large bipedal meerkats. They often wear simple clothes and bands of gemstones wrapped with string and leather. These gems are elegantly cut in the shapes of lizards, scorpions, and desert blooms. Grit flingers possess an innate ability for controlling sand and carry a magical sack of endless sand they use to augment their talents. They tend to live in small communities with expansive tunnel networks deep below ground, typically beneath deserts and badlands.

These resilient fey are believed to guard deposits of precious materials, such as of gemstones, silver, and the purest of iron. The easiest way to anger a grit flinger is to dig near their homes. Upon discovering a hole or tunnel, they'll use their endless sandy sack to fill it in. They then summon a giant sandstorm to scare off any remaining creatures, transforming the landscape into a desert as a warning for any who might think of excavating there.

action->Sack of Sand.name: Sack of Sand
action->Sack of Sand.description: A grit flinger's bag is filled with infinite sand that they can use to beset their foes. The grit flinger can use their abilities with the earth trait only if they're holding an intact sack of sand in one hand. The sack can be targeted by Strikes (AC 27). If the sack of sand takes at least 15 piercing or slashing damage from a single Strike, it starts to leak. At the start of each of the grit flinger's turns, the leaking bag spills sand in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5], creating difficult terrain that lasts for 1 day. The grit flinger can repair the sack with 1 minute of work. If the sack is separated from the grit flinger, it loses its magic and becomes a mundane sack of sand.

action->Wrathful Sands.name: Wrathful Sands
action->Wrathful Sands.description: 10 feet. A cloud of sand surrounds the grit flinger. A creature that enters or begins its turn in the aura takes @Damage[4d6[slashing]] damage with a @Check[fortitude|dc:24|basic] save. The grit flinger can activate or deactivate the aura with a Sustain action. If the grit flinger's sack of sand starts leaking, the aura ends.

action->Blinding Sand.name: Blinding Sand
action->Blinding Sand.description: A creature hit by the grit flinger's sand slash becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

action->Disseminating Scurry.name: Disseminating Scurry
action->Disseminating Scurry.description: The grit flinger Strides up to half their Speed, spreading sand and gravel into the air while subtly guiding it into annoying nooks and crannies. Each creature the grit flinger moves adjacent to while scurrying must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:26] save as debris lodges uncomfortably under armor, in shoes, or up noses. On a failure, the creature becomes covered in sand until it spends an action shaking off the debris. Anytime a creature covered in sand attempts an action with the concentrate trait, the action is disrupted unless the creature succeeds at a @Check[flat|dc:5].

Harmona.name: Harmona
Harmona.publicNotes:
Catching a glimpse of a harmona is said to be lucky. Flying quickly, these brightly colored avian fey are all but hidden to the naked eye. A soft buzz, discernible only to creatures with particularly keen hearing, accompanies them as they observe and scout places where they might find new sources of food.

Intelligent and curious, these tiny fey birds freely roam the First World, accompanying high-ranking fey creatures like queens or their courts. In turn, companions who treat a harmona with respect for their knowledge and skill benefit from the harmona's aid in times of need.

When these curious creatures find a natural gate between the planes, they glide through to explore and expand their knowledge. Those who find their way onto the Universe often choose to remain there in search of diverse and unusual places. This frequently leads them to the same locations that draw curious adventurers. A harmona might befriend a non-fey adventurer as a companion, but they resent those who would treat them as pets and fight to the death to avoid capture.

spell->Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
spell->Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an invisibility potion) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

action->Flit Back.name: Flit Back
action->Flit Back.description:
Trigger A creature enters the harmona's space or an adjacent square

Effect The harmona Flies 10 feet away from the triggering creature.

action->Concussive Blow.name: Concussive Blow
action->Concussive Blow.description:
The harmona makes a beak Strike, channeling disruptive sound waves into the blow. On a hit, the target must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:30] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} on a critical failure).

After this Strike, the harmona can Fly up to half their fly Speed.

action->Subsonic Pulse.name: Subsonic Pulse
action->Subsonic Pulse.description:
The harmona beats their wings rapidly towards the ground, creating a nearly inaudible rumble and sending a wave of shaking earth to overwhelm their enemies.

Each creature in a @Template[emanation|distance:15] must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:30|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:prone] save or take @Damage[6d6[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage. A creature that fails its save is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} from the shaking ground.

action->Ultrasonic Thrust.name: Ultrasonic Thrust
action->Ultrasonic Thrust.description:
The harmona beats their wings skyward, creating a spiraling vibration. Each creature in a @Template[cone|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:30|options:area-effect,damaging-effect,forced-movement,inflicts:off-guard,inflicts:prone] save as the high-frequency blast flings them up and away.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is pushed 5 feet away and knocked off balance, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of their next turn.

Failure Sonic waves fling the creature 15 feet back from the harmona. The creature takes @Damage[6d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage from the fall and lands @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is flung 30 feet and takes double damage.

Hobkins.name: Hobkins
Hobkins.publicNotes:
Hobkins are eerie little creatures, pallid humanoids with enormous, lantern-like eyes and massive ears on a too-big head. Unlike other gremlins, hobkins aren't fully in step with the Universe. Instead, they're trapped halfway between it and the First World—eternally out of phase, just a hair's breadth from reality. They move strangely, with jerking, jittery gestures that jump between too fast and too slow, and they float above the ground. They have a physical form, but they feel off to the touch, with a texture not quite like anything else.

Where most gremlins dismantle machines or relationships, hobkins love to scare people, striving to spread paranoia and terror wherever they go. A hobkins might lurk outside a child's window during a storm, pressing its great gleaming eyes against the glass until a lightning flash illuminates its horrible visage—and then vanish before the next lightning strike, giggling to itself with delight.

Like many fey, gremlins personify a natural force of the world: entropy. It's a fundamental truth that everything breaks, that every complex system, from a machine to a society, will inevitably grind itself down to nothing. Gremlins are happy to give those complex systems a friendly shove down the stairs.

Nearly all gremlins live in the Universe, where they have fully acclimated to the plane. No one is quite certain why, but it seems likely that some long-forgotten gremlin managed to so irritate the Eldest to such a degree that their entire species was exiled—though it appears the Eldest missed a few, as some gremlins still lurk in the First World.

Gremlins are usually found in an odd, parasitic relationship with mortal communities in the Universe. They don't need to eat or sleep, don't age or sicken, and never really die—but they do need to cause trouble. It's as essential to them as food and drink are to mortals, and nowhere do they get as many chances for chaos and confusion as in a mortal settlement. Gremlins thus become pests, living on the margins of society and bedeviling anyone and anything they can get their hands on.

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Illusory Object.name: Illusory Object
spell->Illusory Object.description:
You create an illusory visual image of a stationary object. The entire image must fit within the spell's area. The object appears to animate naturally, but it doesn't make sounds or generate smells. For example, water would appear to pour down an illusory waterfall, but it would be silent.

Any creature that touches the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) Your image makes appropriate sounds, generates normal smells, and feels right to the touch. The spell gains the auditory and olfactory traits. The duration increases to 1 hour.

Heightened (5th) As the 2nd-rank version, but the duration is unlimited.

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

action->Not Where You Think.name: Not Where You Think
action->Not Where You Think.description:
Trigger A frightened creature misses the hobkins with a Strike

Requirements There is a creature other than the attacker within 15 feet that would be a valid target for the triggering attack

Effect The hobkins redirects the triggering attack to the required creature. The attacker rerolls the attack against the new target.

action->Floating.name: Floating
action->Floating.description: Hobkins always levitate about an inch off the ground, ignoring difficult terrain unless it would also affect flying creatures. If they're further than an inch off the ground at the end of their turn, they gently fall to that height, without taking damage, unless they have something to hold on to.

action->Spooky Little Thing.name: Spooky Little Thing
action->Spooky Little Thing.description:
Requirements The hobkins is hidden

Effect The hobkins produces eerie lights and uncanny sounds with no clear source, attempting to [[/act demoralize]] a foe within 30 feet. Demoralizing this way loses the auditory trait, gains the visual trait, and doesn't cause the hobkins to lose the hidden condition. The hobkins takes no penalty to their check if the target cannot understand their language.

House Spirit Mob.name: House Spirit Mob
House Spirit Mob.publicNotes:
Even the smallest house spirits can band together against a threat to the home.

House spirits are a collection of fey who live among peasants and poor rural folk. They hide themselves from mortal eyes—hence why they're so commonly called "spirits"—but their presence is always felt. Given suitable respect, these house fey take a decidedly parental interest in the mortals they live with, doing all manner of work around the household. They cook, they clean, they sweep, they chop wood, they care for animals, they tend the stove. If disrespected, however, they becomes a veritable plague of ill will.

action->Shy.name: Shy
action->Shy.description: A house sprit mob is naturally @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} while within sight of their bound area. The house spirit mob can become visible or even selectively visible—allowing only certain people to see them.

action->Uncooperative Surroundings.name: Uncooperative Surroundings
action->Uncooperative Surroundings.description: 30 feet. The house spirit mob rallies household items to hamper their foes. Each enemy in the aura that fails an attack roll, Reflex saving throw, or Acrobatics or Athletics skill check becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} and knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} on a critical failure).

action->Swarming Blows.name: Swarming Blows
action->Swarming Blows.description: Each enemy in the mob's space takes @Damage[3d6[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic] save).

action->Tragic Accident.name: Tragic Accident
action->Tragic Accident.description: Combining powers, the mob creates a horrific accident, dealing @Damage[5d10[untyped]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] or @Template[type:line|distance:20] within their bound area (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic] save). The area becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute, and the damage is most often bludgeoning. The mob can't use Tragic Accident again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Tragic Accident]]{1d4 rounds}.

Huldra.name: Huldra
Huldra.publicNotes:
At first glance, a huldra seems like a simple creature—a human in plain robes or peasant dress, sporting long hair. These tresses and full skirts in fact disguise the huldra's supernatural features: a hollow wooden back, a long bovine tail, and incredible strength.

Folk legends from the lands of the north describe huldras as the creations of troll witches, intended to lure potential meals to the slaughter. Indeed, a huldra's regeneration is so similar to a troll's that a link between the two creatures seems entirely possible, but huldras despise trolls and resent tales suggesting any connection between them. Rather, huldras are wardens of the woodlands they occupy. Grown from saplings by powerful forest-dwelling fey as a response to humanoid encroachment, huldras protect and parley for the forest itself. Woodland creatures adore huldras and sometimes approach humans or elves thinking they're huldras. This illusion is shattered if the animal sees the humanoid's back is made of flesh or that they're lacking a tail.

Huldras respond well to travelers who show respect and deference for the forest, bestowing those they favor with supernatural luck and fortune. Those who scorn or attack a huldra, or those who mock their distinctive, bovine tails, find themselves plagued by poor decisions and even worse luck. Huldras commonly carry a bad reputation as sirens of the deep forest—cunning monsters who seek to lure woodcutters and unwary adventurers to uncertain ends. These stories largely come from miscreants foolish enough to have treated a huldra rudely and later complain about how they were unjustly persecuted. Even woodcutters and hunters can stay in the good graces of huldras provided they plant new trees to replace what they've taken and don't kill any creatures they don't eat.

Though huldras choose to appear unassuming, their awareness is sometimes lacking when it comes to their strength. They often perform feats of strength, like bending horseshoes straight or lifting heavy objects, without realizing they're breaking their carefully crafted facade.

0.label: to Impersonate a human version of themselves

action->Befuddling Lash.name: Befuddling Lash
action->Befuddling Lash.description: When the huldra damages a creature with their tail, a wave of befuddlement clouds the target's thoughts. The creature must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:19] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} on a critical failure) for 1 minute.

action->Manipulate Luck.name: Manipulate Luck
action->Manipulate Luck.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The huldra touches another creature to manipulate the creature's luck. The creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] save.

On a failure, the huldra chooses good luck or bad luck. If the huldra chooses good luck, the affected creature can roll twice on one d20 roll within the next minute and use the higher result; this is a fortune effect. If the huldra chooses bad luck, the creature must roll twice and use the lower result on its next d20 roll; this is a misfortune effect.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.2DlOfFoYLGSlfugH]{Effect: Manipulate Luck (Good)}

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.zzdOof9hHUf9s13H]{Effect: Manipulate Luck (Bad)}

Hungersome Wolf.name: Hungersome Wolf
Hungersome Wolf.publicNotes:
A hungersome wolf is a fearsome beast who stalks the forests of the First World, following after their prey with silent steps and unending patience. They're known to choose a target and bide their time, finding out the target's usual routes and routines, eventually identifying the perfect time and place to strike. When the moment is right, the wolf will enter into the home of the target, consume one of their loved ones, and shift into that victim's form, waiting for the target to return and become the perfect dessert to their vicious meal.

A hungersome wolf prefers the prey they find in the First World, but occasionally, one finds their way into the Universe. The resulting carnage inspires many stories whispered in the dark of night to children as a warning—against leaving the trail, against leaving an unprotected loved one alone, and most importantly, a warning to trust your instincts.

action->Better to See You With.name: Better to See You With
action->Better to See You With.description: The wolf's keen sense of sight can see through both mundane and magical hindrances when they have their sights set on their prey. The wolf ignores their prey's concealment if they're visible. If their prey is invisible, the wolf treats their invisibility as concealment instead.

action->Run If You Can.name: Run If You Can
action->Run If You Can.description:
Trigger A creature within reach of the wolf's jaws attempts to move out of reach

Effect The hungersome wolf attempts a jaws Strike against the triggering creature. On a hit, they disrupt the triggering creature's move action.

action->Stalk Prey.name: Stalk Prey
action->Stalk Prey.description:
The hungersome wolf designates a single sapient creature they can smell and hear as their prey. The hungersome wolf gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [[/act seek]] their prey and Survival checks to [[/act track]] their prey. The wolf gains an additional reaction each round they can use only for Run If You Can against their prey.

If the wolf uses Stalk Prey again, any creature they'd designated as their prey is no longer their prey.

action->You Are What You Eat.name: You Are What You Eat
action->You Are What You Eat.description: This functions as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.eQM5hQ1W3d1uen97]{Change Shape}, except the hungersome wolf must transform into the last creature they Swallowed Whole. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage bonuses, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning). The transformation lasts until the hungersome wolf takes 20 or more damage from a single ability, attack, or spell.

Jabberwock.name: Jabberwock
Jabberwock.publicNotes:
Few beasts have inspired as many legends, poems, songs, and myths, in as many cultures, as this bizarre draconic creature. Jabberwocks hail from the fey realm of the First World and are part of a group of powerful First World creatures known collectively as the Tane: living weapons for a war beyond mortal comprehension. Jabberwocks were among the first of the Tane, their kind making up one of the Five Beasts of Ending.

Like all members of the Tane, jabberwocks are living creatures who age, eat, drink, and sleep, but they don't reproduce normally. Instead, they're created directly by the godlike Eldest who rule the First World, and they serve at the pleasure (or frustration) of these capricious and mysterious entities. Believed to be the most powerful of all the Tane, jabberwocks are typically only ever created with one purpose: to wreak destruction and havoc upon the Universe. One of the Eldest might send a jabberwock to devastate a country, continent, or even entire world just to get revenge for some slight made against them by a single mortal. Sometimes, no specific insult or injury is required, as some of the Eldest resent the very existence of the Universe and periodically create jabberwocks simply to express the wrath of the First World against its younger, less chaotic sibling.

Once a jabberwock arrives in the Universe, their first order of business is to seek out a lair. They prefer dwelling in remote forest locations about a day's flight from civilization—the more dangerous the woodland to those who eventually come hunting them, the better!

The relationship between jabberwocks and vorpal weapons is the subject of much debate and speculation among scholars, and the various poems, songs, and legends about jabberwocks do little to clarify the issue, conflicting and diverging on this point. Some believe that vorpal weapons were first created specifically to combat jabberwocks, but others take the story a step further. Certain ancient myths hold that there might once have been only a single, unique jabberwock, so powerful that nothing could so much as scratch them—nothing, that is, except for the first vorpal sword, crafted for that very purpose. So epic was the resulting battle that it created strange echoes throughout reality, and as a result, these echoes, in the form of vorpal weapons, can now be found on many worlds. Those who subscribe to this belief claim that the jabberwocks seen today are but pale imitations of this proto-jabberwock, and they speculate that only the combined efforts of several Eldest would be sufficient to create such a creature again.

Variant Jabberwocks

The Eldest have sometimes altered certain aspects of the jabberwocks they create. Some of the more notorious or legendary variant jabberwocks include the following.

Frumious Jabberwock: Frumious jabberwocks have two heads instead of one. They are 24th level and gain an extra action on each of their turns they can use only to make a jaws Strike.

Mimsy Jabberwock: Typically hailing from wintry regions of the First World, mimsy jabberwocks have glowing blue-white scales, resist cold instead of fire, and have eyes that burn with blue flames that deal cold damage instead of fire damage.

Slithy Jabberwock: Wreaking destruction beneath the waves, these sinuous jabberwocks are amphibious, have a swim Speed of 80 feet instead of the normal fly Speed, and don't have a wing Strike. A slithy jabberwock's Whiffling aura is activated whenever they Swim, make a tail Strike, or Burble.

spell->Truesight (Constant).name: Truesight (Constant)
spell->Truesight (Constant).description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

action->Planar Acclimation.name: Planar Acclimation
action->Planar Acclimation.description: The jabberwock always treats the plane it is currently located on as its home plane.

action->Claws That Catch.name: Claws That Catch
action->Claws That Catch.description:
Trigger A creature within the jabberwock's reach uses a concentrate, manipulate, or move action; leaves a square during a move action; or makes a ranged attack

Effect The jabberwock makes a claw Strike against the triggering creature. If the Strike hits, the jabberwock disrupts the triggering action.

action->Vorpal Fear.name: Vorpal Fear
action->Vorpal Fear.description: A jabberwock damaged by a vorpal weapon becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} on a critical hit).

action->Burble.name: Burble
action->Burble.description:
The jabberwock creates a blast of strange noises and shouted nonsense in the various languages it knows (and invariably some languages it doesn't know), creating one of two effects.

The jabberwock can't Burble again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Burble]]{1d4 rounds}.

  • Confusion 60 feet. Each creature in the emanation must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:46|options:area-effect] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

  • Sonic Beam The jabberwock focuses its Burbling into a 60 foot line of sonic energy that deals @Damage[24d6[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage to creatures in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:46|basic|options:area-effect] save).

action->Jaws That Bite.name: Jaws That Bite
action->Jaws That Bite.description: If the jabberwock makes a jaws attack and rolls a natural 19 on the d20 roll, the attack is a critical hit. This has no effect if the 19 would be a failure.

action->Whiffling.name: Whiffling
action->Whiffling.description:
Trigger The jabberwock Flies or makes a wing Strike

Effect The jabberwock's wings whiffle, creating severe winds within a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. These winds move outward from the jabberwock, and they persist until the start of the jabberwock's next turn. During this time, flight of any kind in the emanation requires a successful [[/act maneuver-in-flight dc=43]]{Acrobatics} check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Qf1ylAbdVi1rkc8M]{Maneuver in Flight}, and creatures flying toward the jabberwock are moving through greater difficult terrain. Creatures on the ground in the emanation must succeed at a @Check[athletics|dc:43|name:Approach Jabberwock] check to approach the jabberwock.

Jack-o’-Lantern.name: Jack-o’-Lantern
Jack-o’-Lantern.publicNotes:
These fey creatures appear as road-worn travelers with a coin purse and flask at their belt, carrying a staff bearing a turnip with a glowing, grinning face. When wandering the road at night, should you see a figure holding up a lantern in the distance, take care—it could be a jack-o'-lantern.

Legends say the original Jack of the Lantern was a greedy trickster who fooled a beggar out of his last silver coin. To punish him, an archon cursed the coin so that any who held it would be rooted in place until released by the coin's owner. Luckily for Jack, he already had the coin in his purse and avoided the curse.

When a powerful devil later tried to bargain for Jack's soul, Jack left the shining coin on the table. The greedy devil couldn't resist it and was rooted to the ground for years, causing a bloody revolution in the devil's holdings in Hell.

When Jack died, Heaven refused him on principle, and Hell refused him out of embarrassment, leaving his restless soul to wander. Amused at Jack's antics, the Lantern King placed a speck of his own essence into a carved turnip, offering the implement of power to Jack in return for his eternal service. Ever since, echoes of Jack—jack-o'-lanterns—have roamed the planes at the Lantern King's command, spreading chaos and trickery.

spell->Translocate.name: Translocate
spell->Translocate.description:
You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

spell->Darkness.name: Darkness
spell->Darkness.description:
You create a shroud of darkness that prevents light from penetrating or emanating within the area. Light does not enter the area and any non-magical light sources, such as a torch or lantern, do not emanate any light while inside the area, even if their light radius would extend beyond the darkness. This also suppresses magical light of your darkness spell's rank or lower. Light can't pass through, so creatures in the area can't see outside. From outside, it appears as a globe of pure darkness.

Heightened (4th) Even creatures with darkvision (but not greater darkvision) can barely see through the darkness. They treat targets seen through the darkness as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}.

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Ignition.name: Ignition
spell->Ignition.description:
You snap your fingers and point at a target, which begins to smolder. Make a spell attack roll against the target's AC, dealing 2d4 fire damage on a hit. If the target is within your melee reach, you can choose to make a melee spell attack with the flame instead of a ranged spell attack, which increases all the spell's damage dice to d6s.

Critical Success The target takes double damage and 1d4 persistent fire damage.

Success The target takes full damage.

Heightened (+1) The initial damage increases by 1d4 and the persistent fire damage on a critical hit increases by 1d4.

@Damage[(@item.rank)d4[persistent,fire]]{Scaling Persistent Fire Damage}

@Damage[(@item.rank)d6[persistent,fire]]{Scaling Persistent Fire Damage (Melee)}

spell->Ventriloquism.name: Ventriloquism
spell->Ventriloquism.description:
Whenever you speak or make any other sound vocally, you can make your vocalization seem to originate from somewhere else within 60 feet, and you can change that apparent location freely as you vocalize. Any creature that hears the sound can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) The spell's duration increases to 1 hour, and you can also change the tone, quality, and other aspects of your voice. Before a creature can attempt to disbelieve your illusion, it must actively attempt a Perception check or otherwise use actions to interact with the sound.

weapon->Lantern Staff.name: Lantern Staff
weapon->Lantern Staff.description: This long piece of wood can aid in walking and deliver a mighty blow.

action->Lantern Allure.name: Lantern Allure
action->Lantern Allure.description: 60 feet. Any creature in the aura that can see the jack-o'-lantern's lantern staff and is in darkness or dim light must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:28] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the light for 1 minute. Regardless of the result, the creature is then temporarily immune to this aura for 24 hours.

action->Snuffed Out.name: Snuffed Out
action->Snuffed Out.description: A jack-o'-lantern whose lantern staff is doused with water or otherwise extinguished takes @Damage[3d6[persistent,mental]] damage, which they automatically recover from when they reignite their lantern. While the flame is snuffed out, the jack-o'-lantern can't use their lantern fire Strike, and their lantern staff Strike doesn't deal fire damage.

action->Heavy Coin.name: Heavy Coin
action->Heavy Coin.description: Any creature that accepts or steals the coin from a jack-o'-lantern's purse must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:30] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 10 minutes. A creature that fails its save can attempt a new Will save every minute and the first time each round that it takes damage. The jack-o'-lantern can Dismiss this effect.

action->Spit Summons.name: Spit Summons
action->Spit Summons.description:
Frequency once per day

Requirements The jack-o'-lantern is holding or carrying their flask

Effect The jack-o'-lantern sips from their flask and spits on the ground. The liquor ignites and animates as it leaves their mouth, summoning a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.pVbggIyXxCo8pPue]{Living Wildfire} that also has the fey trait.

Jubjub Bird.name: Jubjub Bird
Jubjub Bird.publicNotes:
A jubjub bird resembles a giant dodo with long, muscular legs and wings capable of brief, if awkward, flight. When attacked with magic, their brilliant plumage, normally purple, shifts randomly in hue and pattern with each spell that hits home.

Jubjub birds belong to the Tane, a group of powerful creatures brought into existence as living weapons by the Eldest. Jubjubs have the dubious reputation of being the least powerful and intelligent of the Tane, though they're still formidable enough that few who underestimate them live long enough to regret the mistake.

Though these birds are sometimes kept as guardians or mounts, the Eldest generally create them for a singular purpose: to be hunted. Just threatening enough to provide a sporting challenge for the high fey lords, once they've been brought down, they make a delicious prize. Their cooked meat is famously exquisite, especially fermented for a few months in mahogany or ivory jars. Mortals who participate in such hunts, however, should take care if they're offered a portion of the prize—certain fey enjoy adding unusual seasonings, including, but not limited to, sawdust, glue, and locusts.

action->Planar Acclimation.name: Planar Acclimation
action->Planar Acclimation.description: The jubjub bird always treats the plane it's on as its home plane.

action->Adaptive Defense.name: Adaptive Defense
action->Adaptive Defense.description:
Trigger The jubjub bird is damaged by an attack that deals cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage

Effect The jubjub bird takes damage as normal, then gains resistance 20 to the triggering damage type for 1 round. If the triggering attack dealt more than one of the listed damage types, the jubjub bird gains resistance 20 to each of them.

action->Perpetual Passion.name: Perpetual Passion
action->Perpetual Passion.description: Jubjub birds grow more frenzied and dangerous as their situation becomes more desperate. The first time the bird's Hit Points are reduced below half of its maximum HP (170 HP), it gains a +1 circumstance bonus to its AC and attack rolls. The first time its Hit Points are reduced below a quarter of its maximum HP (85 HP), the bonus increases to +2, and its Strikes deal an additional 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

action->Scream Shrill and High.name: Scream Shrill and High
action->Scream Shrill and High.description:
The jubjub bird rends the sky with a shrill note like a pencil on a slate. Non-Tane creatures within 120 feet must attempt a @Check[will|dc:40] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is startled by the cry and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for 1 round.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and is momentarily frozen with fear, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and is immobilized for as long as it remains frightened.

action->Sprint.name: Sprint
action->Sprint.description: The jubjub bird Strides three times in a straight line.

action->Sudden Charge.name: Sudden Charge
action->Sudden Charge.description: The jubjub bird Strides twice. If it ends its movement within melee reach of at least one creature, it can make a melee Strike against that creature.

Kaztili.name: Kaztili
Kaztili.publicNotes:
Though always dressed like they're attending the finest court functions, a kaztili behaves more like the patron of an ale hall. Consummate comedians and witty debaters, these liminal sprites love ambages and flyting. Though to outsiders, their interests might seem align with those of murxies, most kaztilis look down on such fellows, considering them low-brow hacks, though others cultivate eager followings of the weaker fey. Kaztilis appear as miniature elves, but with angular, gossamer wings sprouting from their backs.

Elusive, flighty, and ebullient, sprites are what many villagers first imagine when they hear the terms "fey" or "fairy."

spell->Blistering Invective.name: Blistering Invective
spell->Blistering Invective.description:
A heap of insults and invectives spew from your mouth-words so devastating your foes burn from the intensity of your diatribe. Your words deal 2d6 persistent fire damage, and the target must attempt a Will save. If the target doesn't understand the language or you're not speaking a language, it gains a +4 circumstance bonus to its save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half the persistent fire damage.

Failure The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} and takes the full persistent fire damage.

Critical Failure The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and takes double the persistent fire damage.

Heightened (+2) You can target two additional creatures, and the persistent damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Invisibility.name: Invisibility
spell->Invisibility.description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Agitate.name: Agitate
spell->Agitate.description:
You send the target's mind and body into overdrive, forcing it to become restless and hyperactive. During the duration, the target must Stride, Fly, or Swim at least once each turn or take 2d8 mental damage at the end of its turn. The GM might decide to add additional move actions to the list for creatures that possess only a more unusual form of movement. The duration of this effect depends on the target's Will save.

Critical Success The spell has no effect.

Success The duration is 1 round.

Failure The duration is 2 rounds.

Critical Failure The duration is 4 rounds.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d8.

spell->Befuddle.name: Befuddle
spell->Befuddle.description:
You sow seeds of confusion in your target's mind, causing its actions and thoughts to become clumsy.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 3}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused}.

spell->Daze.name: Daze
spell->Daze.description:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

action->+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Comedic Versatility.name: Comedic Versatility
action->Comedic Versatility.description: A kaztili can use Performance for all Deception and Intimidation actions.

action->Witty Repartee.name: Witty Repartee
action->Witty Repartee.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The kaztili speaks a sharp remark about its current situation, emboldening its friends or debilitating its foes. The kaztili attempts a Performance check against the Will DC of a creature within 30 feet. On a success, the kaztili chooses to give that creature either a +1 status bonus or –1 status penalty to the next attack roll or skill check it makes before the start of the kaztili's next turn.

Kikimora.name: Kikimora
Kikimora.publicNotes:
According to folklore, the kikimora was once a swamp or forest spirit that came to prefer living in a peasant's home to dwelling out in the muck and cold. They look rather like the people they live alongside but sometimes have animalistic features.

House spirits are a collection of fey who live among peasants and poor rural folk. They hide themselves from mortal eyes—hence why they're so commonly called "spirits"—but their presence is always felt. Given suitable respect, these house fey take a decidedly parental interest in the mortals they live with, doing all manner of work around the household. They cook, they clean, they sweep, they chop wood, they care for animals, they tend the stove. If disrespected, however, they becomes a veritable plague of ill will.
Kikimora.senses: tremorsense (imprecise) within their entire bound home

spell->Nightmare.name: Nightmare
spell->Nightmare.description:
You send disturbing nightmares to your target. The next time the target falls asleep, it must attempt a Will save. If you know the target only by name and have never met them, the target gets a +4 circumstance bonus to the Will save.

Critical Success The target suffers no adverse effects and is temporarily immune for 1 week.

Success The target experiences the nightmares but suffers no adverse effects other than unpleasant memories.

Failure The target experiences the nightmares and awakens @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued}.

Critical Failure The target experiences the nightmares, awakens Fatigued, and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} until it is no longer Fatigued.

spell->Grease.name: Grease
spell->Grease.description:
You conjure grease, choosing an area or target.

  • Area [4 contiguous 5-foot squares] All solid ground in the area is covered with grease. Each creature standing on the greasy surface must succeed at a Reflex save or an Acrobatics check against your spell DC or fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. Creatures using an action to move onto the greasy surface during the spell's duration must attempt either a Reflex save or an Acrobatics check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.M76ycLAqHoAgbcej]{Balance}. A creature that Steps or Crawls doesn't have to attempt a check or save.
  • Target [1 object of Bulk 1 or less] If you Cast the Spell on an unattended object, anyone trying to pick up the object must succeed at an Acrobatics check or Reflex save against your spell DC to do so. If you target an attended object, the creature that has the object must attempt an Acrobatics check or Reflex save. On a failure, the holder or wielder takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all checks that involve using the object; on a critical failure, the holder or wielder releases the item. The object lands in an adjacent square of the GM's choice. If you Cast this Spell on a worn object, the wearer gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves against attempts to grapple them.

spell->Mending.name: Mending
spell->Mending.description:
You repair the target item. You restore 5 Hit Points per spell rank to the target, potentially removing the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken} condition if this repairs it past the item's Broken Threshold. You can't replace lost pieces or repair an object that's been completely destroyed.

Heightened (2nd) You can target a non-magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Heightened (3rd) You can target a non-magical object of 2 Bulk or less, or a magical object of 1 Bulk or less.
spell->Mending.target: non-magical object of light Bulk or less

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

spell->Telekinetic Hand.name: Telekinetic Hand
spell->Telekinetic Hand.description:
You create a floating, magical hand, either invisible or ghostlike, that grasps the target object and levitates it slowly up to 20 feet in any direction. When you Sustain the spell, you can move the object an additional 20 feet. If the object is in the air when the spell ends, the object falls.

Heightened (3rd) You can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (7th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 2 or less.
spell->Telekinetic Hand.target: 1 unattended object of light Bulk or less

spell->Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
spell->Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

action->Master of the Hearth.name: Master of the Hearth
action->Master of the Hearth.description: A kikimora often shares custody of a home with a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.AzYYP23uGecb0Jmw]{Domovoi}. When the two agree, the circumstance bonus or penalty the domovoi provides to checks to Craft, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.QyzlsLrqM0EEwd7j]{Earn Income}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.bT3skovyLUtP22ME]{Repair}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.49y9Ec4bDii8pcD3]{Subsist} in the home increases to +3 or –3, depending on their shared mood. When the domovoi and the kikimora disagree, all such checks always take a –1 circumstance penalty from the dispute. A kikimora must spend a week in a place before these benefits occur.

action->Shy.name: Shy
action->Shy.description: A kikimora is naturally @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} while within sight of their bound home. The kikimora can become visible or even selectively visible—allowing only certain people to see them.

action->Home Guardian.name: Home Guardian
action->Home Guardian.description: By commanding their home to attack, the kikimora can [[/act disarm skill=household-lore]], [[/act grapple skill=household-lore]], [[/act reposition skill=household-lore]], [[/act shove skill=household-lore]], or [[/act trip skill=household-lore]] with their enraged home Strike. The kikimora uses their Household Lore instead of Athletics skill for these checks.

action->Unravel.name: Unravel
action->Unravel.description: The kikimora attempts a claw Strike against a creature that's wearing clothing made of fabric. If it hits, the creature's clothing starts to come apart. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} on a critical hit) until it Interacts twice to fix its clothing. Once a creature has had its clothing unraveled, the kikimora can't unravel it further until the target changes clothes.

Kirakor.name: Kirakor
Kirakor.publicNotes:
Kirakors are well-dressed fey musicians, performers, and ambassadors, and as such are often the first fey many commonfolk ever meet. They have a strong sense of conscience and an even greater sense of style, using their dazzling looks to defuse situations before they devolve into combat. However, when fights happen, they stand firm against injustice, even when it's bigger than they are. Kirakors look like bipedal crickets with a full head of humanoid-like hair.

Elusive, flighty, and ebullient, sprites are what many villagers first imagine when they hear the terms "fey" or "fairy."

spell->Invisibility.name: Invisibility
spell->Invisibility.description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Revealing Light.name: Revealing Light
spell->Revealing Light.description:
A wave of magical light washes over the area. You choose the appearance of the light, such as colorful, heatless flames or sparkling motes. A creature affected by revealing light is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled}. If the creature was @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} instead. If the creature was already concealed for any other reason, it is no longer concealed.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The light affects the creature for 2 rounds.

Failure The light affects the creature for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The light affects the creature for 10 minutes.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Illusory Disguise.name: Illusory Disguise
spell->Illusory Disguise.description:
You create an illusion that causes the target to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise is typically good enough to hide their identity, but not to impersonate a specific individual. The spell changes their appearance and voice, but not mannerisms. You can change the appearance of its clothing and worn items, such as making its armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item removed from the creature returns to its true appearance.

Casting illusory disguise counts as setting up a disguise for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} use of Deception; it ignores any circumstance penalties the target might take for disguising itself as a dissimilar creature, gives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through the disguise, and lets the target add its level to such Deception checks even if untrained. You can Dismiss this spell.

Heightened (3rd) The target can appear as any creature of the same size, even a specific individual. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 willing creatures. If you target multiple creatures, you can choose a different disguise for each target, but none can impersonate a specific individual. You can Dismiss each disguise individually or all collectively.

Heightened (7th) As 4th, but you can choose disguises that impersonate specific individuals. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3Ktyd5F9lOPo4myk]{Spell Effect: Illusory Disguise}

spell->Jump (At Will).name: Jump (At Will)
spell->Jump (At Will).description:
Your legs surge with strength, ready to leap high and far. You jump 30 feet in any direction without touching the ground. You must land on a space of solid ground within 30 feet of you, or else you fall after using your next action.

Heightened (3rd) The range becomes touch, the target changes to one touched creature, and the duration becomes 1 minute, allowing the target to jump as described whenever it takes the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.d5I6018Mci2SWokk]{Leap} action.

action->Jaunty Jig.name: Jaunty Jig
action->Jaunty Jig.description:
The kirakor dances, rubbing its legs together to emit a pleasant tune that inspires listeners to join in. Each non-fey creature within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:17] save. A kirakor can Sustain this effect for up to 1 minute, and the first time each round that the kirakor Sustains the effect in subsequent rounds, each non-fey creature in the emanation must attempt the save again.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature dances, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} and taking a –10-foot circumstance penalty to all its Speeds for 1 round.

Critical Failure As failure, and the creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.

Kishi.name: Kishi
Kishi.publicNotes:
Kishis are duplicitous, murderous fey who dwell on the edges of Golarion's densest jungles. At first glance, kishis appear to be attractive humans, usually of a local ethnicity, but their full heads of thick hair conceal a second face: that of a snarling hyena. When a kishi lures their prey into a vulnerable situation, their head swivels around, revealing this fearsome visage. In this form, a kishi's powerful jaws are almost impossible to pry loose and can crush a victim's bones in a matter of moments.

Kishis range widely in their physical features, and their height and weight vary as much as the people whose communities they infiltrate. They dress in fine clothing aligned with the latest fashion trends, and they wear flashy jewelry to draw onlookers' eyes.

Like most fey, kishis have inscrutable motives, though to their victims, their goal seems simple—to revel in the expression of shock, betrayal, and terror on a victim's face. Although kishis can cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm} to make unwitting companions complacent, most of these sinister creatures prefer to trick their prey using guile, gifts, and their dashing good looks. These ultimate sadists derive pleasure from the thrill of the hunt as much as the delicious reward at the end. The more uptight, prudish, or haughty a target, the better—for nothing satisfies kishis as much as earning (and destroying) the trust of someone who rarely grants it.

When kishis get their new friends or lovers alone, they choose the most dramatic moments to reveal their true monstrous forms and clamp their jaws down on their victim. Kishis have no desire to share their true nature with the entire community, so they typically aim for the throat to keep their victim from crying out for help. The fey then consume every part of their victims' bodies, leaving no trace of the crime—even lapping up any spilled blood, claiming the victim's treasures as their own, and cleaning the murder scene as much as possible.

Few things can bind a community together as swiftly as uncovering a kishi. Once found out, a kishi flees, hoping to find a new community to prey upon.

spell->Charm (At Will).name: Charm (At Will)
spell->Charm (At Will).description:
To the target, your words are honey and your visage seems bathed in a dreamy haze. It must attempt a Will save, with a +4 circumstance bonus if you or your allies recently threatened it or used hostile actions against it.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you use hostile actions against the target, the spell ends. When the spell ends, the target doesn't necessarily realize it was charmed unless its friendship with you or the actions you convinced it to take clash with its expectations, meaning you could potentially convince the target to continue being your friend via mundane means.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and aware you tried to charm it.

Success The target is unaffected but thinks your spell was something harmless instead of charm, unless it identifies the spell.

Failure The target's attitude becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v66R7FdOf11l94im]{Friendly} toward you. If it was Friendly, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v44P3WUcU1j0115l]{Helpful}. It can't use hostile actions against you.

Critical Failure The target's attitude becomes Helpful toward you, and it can't use hostile actions against you.

Heightened (4th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations.

Heightened (8th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations, and you can target up to 10 creatures.

action->Head Spin.name: Head Spin
action->Head Spin.description: The kishi switches between showing their attractive human face and their snarling hyena face. A kishi can use their innate spell and their Deception and Diplomacy skills only when their human face is showing, and they can use their jaws Strike only when their hyena face is showing.

action->Sudden Charge.name: Sudden Charge
action->Sudden Charge.description: The kishi Strides twice. If they end their movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, they can make a melee Strike against that enemy.

action->Vicelike Jaws.name: Vicelike Jaws
action->Vicelike Jaws.description: A creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} in the kishi's jaws can barely speak; a creature must succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:8] to speak or cast spells, doing so in a choked whisper.

Laluxi.name: Laluxi
Laluxi.languages: Telepathy 100 feet (doesnt need to share a language)
Laluxi.publicNotes:
Laluxis, also whispered of as "dream scribes" by those few who survive an encounter with one, are ancient, almost-mythical beings who dwell in the drifting silk islands of the Astral Tangle—the volatile borderlands where the First World and the Astral Plane mix.

Laluxis are prophets, poets, and wielders of thought, collecting the dreams and nightmares of fey and mortals alike on their long journeys. They don't speak so much as write into the minds of their victims, filling their heads with lifetimes of dreams through a mere glance. Where they go, dream and reality unravel into thread and tangle together, and minds stretched too tightly might snap.

Laluxis are beautiful creatures of fine fur and featureless black carapaces, with elegant humanoid arms and four shimmering, colorful wings. Their awe-inspiring presence means they're sometimes mistaken for divine messengers. In truth, they serve only their own cryptic purposes, gathering the finest subconscious castoffs to weave into their ever-growing cosmological tapestry.

spell->Warp Mind.name: Warp Mind
spell->Warp Mind.description:
You scramble a creature's mental faculties and sensory input. The target must attempt a Will saving throw. Regardless of the result of that save, the target is then temporarily immune for 10 minutes. Warp mind's effects happen instantly, so @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} and other effects that counteract spells can't counteract them. However, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} rituals and abilities that can remove non-magical effects can still counteract the effects.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target spends the first action on its next turn with the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} condition.

Failure The target is Confused for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is Confused permanently.

spell->Dreaming Potential (At Will).name: Dreaming Potential (At Will)
spell->Dreaming Potential (At Will).description: You draw the target into a lucid dream where it can explore the endless possibilities of its own potential within the everchanging backdrop of its dreamscape. If it sleeps the full 8 hours uninterrupted, when it wakes, it counts as having spent a day of downtime retraining, though it can't use dreaming potential for any retraining that would require either an instructor or specialized knowledge it can't access within the dream.
