spell->Illusory Scene (At WIll).name: Illusory Scene (At WIll)
spell->Illusory Scene (At WIll).description:
You craft an imaginary scene that includes up to 10 discrete creatures or objects of various sizes, all of which must be within the spell's area. These elements generate appropriate sounds and smells, and they feel right to the touch. Elements of an illusory scene are incapable of speech. Unlike with the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.f8SBoXiXQjlCKqly]{Illusory Creature} spell, creatures in your scene lack combat abilities and statistics. Your scene doesn't include changes to the environment around it, though you can place your scene within the illusory environment of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HBJPsonQnWcC3qdX]{Mirage} spell.

When you create the scene, you can choose to have it be static or follow a program. Though a static scene is stationary, it includes basic natural movement. For example, wind blowing on an illusory piece of paper would rustle it. A program can be up to 1 minute long and repeats when finished. For instance, you could create a scene of two orcs fighting each other, and the fight would go the same way for each repetition. If you create a loop, the two fighters end up in the same place at the start of the scene and at the end of it, but you can smooth the program so it's hard to tell when the loop ends and begins. Anyone observing the scene for more than a few minutes almost always notices it looping. You're unable to alter the program after you create the illusion.

Any creature that touches any part of the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. If they interact with a portion of the illusion, they disbelieve only that portion. They disbelieve the entire scene only on a critical success.

Heightened (6th) Creatures or objects in your scene can speak. You must speak the specific lines for each actor when creating your program. The spell disguises your voice for each actor.

Heightened (8th) As the 6th-rank version, and the duration is unlimited.

spell->Shadow Blast.name: Shadow Blast
spell->Shadow Blast.description:
Area varies

Defense @Check[reflex|basic|options:area-effect] or @Check[will|basic|options:area-effect] (target's choice)

You shape the shadow substance of the Netherworld into a blast. Choose @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[acid]|options:area-damage], @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage], @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[cold]|options:area-damage], @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[electricity]|options:area-damage], @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[fire]|options:area-damage], @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[force]|options:area-damage], @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[piercing]|options:area-damage], @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[slashing]|options:area-damage], @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[sonic]|options:area-damage], or @Damage[(@item.rank+1)d8[spirit]|options:area-damage] damage, and choose a @Template[cone|distance:30], a @Template[burst|distance:15] within 120 feet, or a @Template[line|distance:50]. The blast deals 6d8 damage of the type you chose to each creature in the area.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d8.

spell->Mirage.name: Mirage
spell->Mirage.description:
You create an illusion that causes natural terrain to look, sound, feel, and smell like a different kind of terrain. This doesn't disguise any structures or creatures in the area.

Any creature that touches the illusion or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (5th) Your image can also disguise structures or create illusory structures (but still doesn't disguise creatures).

spell->Rewrite Memory.name: Rewrite Memory
spell->Rewrite Memory.description:
You alter the target's memories by erasing a memory, enhancing a memory's clarity, altering a memory, or adding a false memory. The target can attempt a Will save to resist the spell.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and realizes you tried to alter its memory.

Success The target is unaffected but thinks your spell was something harmless instead of rewrite memory, unless it identifies the spell.

Failure During the first 5 minutes of the spell's duration, you can Sustain the spell to modify a memory once each round. When you do, you imagine up to 6 seconds of memory to modify, to a maximum of 5 continuous minutes of memory.

Any memories you've altered remain changed as long as the spell is active. If the target moves out of range before the 5 minutes is up, you can't alter any further memories.

Heightened (6th) You can Cast the Spell on a willing target to suppress all memory of a particular topic, detailed in 50 words or fewer. The effect is permanent, and it patches these omissions with an indistinct haze.

spell->Telekinetic Maneuver.name: Telekinetic Maneuver
spell->Telekinetic Maneuver.description: With a rush of telekinetic power, you move a foe or something they carry. You can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shove}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.lOE4yjUnETTdaf2T]{Reposition}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip} the target using a spell attack roll instead of an Athletics check.

spell->Command.name: Command
spell->Command.description:
You shout a command that's hard to ignore. You can command the target to approach you, run away (as if it had the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} condition), release what it's holding, drop @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}, or stand in place. It can't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.A72nHGUtNXgY5Ey9]{Delay} or take any reactions until it has obeyed your command. The effects depend on the target's Will save.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure For the first action on its next turn, the creature must use a single action to do as you command.

Critical Failure The target must use all its actions on its next turn to obey your command.

Heightened (5th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

spell->Daze.name: Daze
spell->Daze.description:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

spell->Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
spell->Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

action->Astral Stitch.name: Astral Stitch
action->Astral Stitch.description: 30 feet. A laluxi's presence subtly alters the world around them, weaving the stuff of dreams into reality. Illusions within the emanation are distorted and become slightly more real, imposing a –2 circumstance penalty to saves against them and to saves or checks to disbelieve them.

action->Flickerwing.name: Flickerwing
action->Flickerwing.description:
Trigger The laluxi is targeted by an attack

Effect The laluxi disappears in a whirl of light and threads, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses, the laluxi can teleport up to 20 feet; this is a teleportation effect.

action->Starweaver's Lure.name: Starweaver's Lure
action->Starweaver's Lure.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The laluxi conjures a cascade of refracted dreams and starlight threads, hurling it at a creature within 60 feet. The target must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:36] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the laluxi for 1 minute. While fascinated, the target can't end any move action farther from the laluxi than where it started.

action->Steal Dreams.name: Steal Dreams
action->Steal Dreams.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The laluxi snaps their great wings open, siphoning threads of dreams and nightmares from creatures that witness them. Each creature in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] takes @Damage[12d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[will|dc:36|basic] save. A creature that fails the save is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 minute.

Lurker In Light.name: Lurker In Light
Lurker In Light.publicNotes:
As easily as a Darklands predator hides in the unsettling mystery of shadows, a lurker in light disappears into the brightest light. These malicious and strange fey appear as fairies about 2 feet tall, with insectile wings, large eyes, and bulbous heads. They slaughter and cause mischief in patterns only their alien intellect understands, but they've been seen to take particular umbrage with dwarves, gnomes, and creatures who live in darkness. With their relentless grudges and pursuit of their own wicked and sadistic whims, lurkers in light deftly overturn the conventional wisdom that creatures associated with light are benign and friendly.

Though lurkers in light are fey and have ties to the First World, these creatures are often found elsewhere in the Great Beyond. They're particularly fond of invading the Netherworld to bring light to those who dwell there—not to help, but to spread misery and pain among those to whom light is agonizing.

spell->Translocate (Only when in bright.name: Translocate (Only when in bright light, and only to an area in bright light)
spell->Translocate (Only when in bright.description:
You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

spell->Blindness.name: Blindness
spell->Blindness.description:
You blind the target. The effect is determined by the target's Fortitude save. The target then becomes temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} until its next turn begins.

Failure The target is Blinded for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is Blinded permanently.

spell->Holy Light.name: Holy Light
spell->Holy Light.description:
You shine a blazing ray of light tinged with holy energy. Make a ranged spell attack. The ray deals 5d6 fire damage. If the target has the unholy trait, you deal an extra 5d6 spirit damage.

Critical Success The target takes double damage.

Success The target takes full damage.

If the light passes through an area of magical darkness or targets a creature affected by magical darkness, holy light attempts to counteract the darkness. If you need to determine whether the light passes through an area of darkness, draw a line between yourself and the spell's target.

Heightened (+1) The fire damage increases by 2d6, and the spirit damage against unholy creatures increases by 2d6.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

spell->Summon Fey.name: Summon Fey
spell->Summon Fey.description:
You summon a creature that has the fey trait and whose level is –1 to fight for you.

Heightened As listed in the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.8gcp880pEWZ9VPnF]{summon} trait.

spell->Summon Fey.name: Summon Fey
spell->Summon Fey.description:
You summon a creature that has the fey trait and whose level is –1 to fight for you.

Heightened As listed in the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.8gcp880pEWZ9VPnF]{summon} trait.

spell->Telekinetic Hand.name: Telekinetic Hand
spell->Telekinetic Hand.description:
You create a floating, magical hand, either invisible or ghostlike, that grasps the target object and levitates it slowly up to 20 feet in any direction. When you Sustain the spell, you can move the object an additional 20 feet. If the object is in the air when the spell ends, the object falls.

Heightened (3rd) You can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (7th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 2 or less.
spell->Telekinetic Hand.target: 1 unattended object of light Bulk or less

action->Blend with Light.name: Blend with Light
action->Blend with Light.description:
Trigger The lurker in light uses a move action

Requirements The lurker in light is in an area of bright light

Effect The lurker in light becomes invisible until they enter an area of dim light or darkness, or until they use a hostile action.

action->Lurker's Glow.name: Lurker's Glow
action->Lurker's Glow.description:
A creature that takes damage from a lurker in light's mote of light Strike must attempt a @Check[will|dc:22] save.

Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to lurker's glow for 24 hours.

Failure The creature is lined in golden light for 1 minute and can't be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} during this time. If the creature becomes invisible, it's concealed rather than undetected.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature sheds bright light in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] for the duration of the effect. In addition, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} until the end of its next turn.

action->Ritual Gate.name: Ritual Gate
action->Ritual Gate.description:
Requirements The lurker in light has reduced a living creature to 0 Hit Points on this turn or their previous turn and has a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.hs7h8f4Z1ZNdUt3s]{Summon Fey} innate spell available

Effect The lurker in light casts summon fey with only a concentrate trait, using the act of slaughter to replace the normal manipulate traits for the spell. If the fey creature summoned shares the lurker in light's current goals, the lurker in light can sustain the summon fey spell for up to 1 hour instead of 1 minute.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: A lurker in light's Strikes deal an additional 2d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Mari Lwyd.name: Mari Lwyd
Mari Lwyd.publicNotes: Winter celebrants beware! A song at the door may herald the arrival of a mari lwyd, a shrouded creature with a grinning, horse-like skull. Despite their macabre visage, these fey singers mean no harm, wishing only to join in with seasonal festivities and partake in hospitality. They're especially partial to alcohol and cheese but can be appeased with other treats if the household has none.

action->Gracious Guest.name: Gracious Guest
action->Gracious Guest.description: The mari lwyd will not pass through a closed threshold without first receiving permission to do so, though they can compel permission using Pwnco.

action->Mostly Harmless.name: Mostly Harmless
action->Mostly Harmless.description: The mari lwyd is out to enjoy the season but becomes dangerous if provoked. Their attacks lose the nonlethal trait against creatures that have damaged them and objects.

action->Persistent Wassailing.name: Persistent Wassailing
action->Persistent Wassailing.description: The mari lwyd is immune to any effect that would prevent them from singing or prevent others from hearing their song.

action->Festive Rampage.name: Festive Rampage
action->Festive Rampage.description:
Requirements The mari lwyd gained permission to enter a structure

Effect The mari lwyd Strides or Swims to enter the structure and goes on a celebratory rampage, smashing furniture and dishware. They then gain resistance 10 to all damage (except cold iron), and their attacks ignore 10 Hardness of any objects they encounter. The effect lasts until the mari lwyd leaves the structure, damages a living creature, or is offered food and drink.

action->Joyous Procession.name: Joyous Procession
action->Joyous Procession.description: The mari lwyd Strides, compelling nearby creatures to join their celebration. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] at the start of the Stride must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:30] save or use its first action on its next turn to Stride directly toward the mari lwyd.

action->Pwnco.name: Pwnco
action->Pwnco.description:
The mari lwyd begins a rhyming contest, requesting entrance to a structure from creatures within. Before the start of the mari lwyd's next turn, at least one occupant can spend 2 actions to [[/act perform dc=33]] a song of their own; the DC is equal to the mari lwyd's Performance DC. If multiple occupants attempt the check, the group takes the highest result. If no occupant spends actions to respond, the group critically fails. Determine the results at the start of the mari lwyd's turn.

Critical Success The respondents win the Pwnco, and the mari lwyd can't enter the structure for 1 month.

Success The response is good, and the Pwnco continues. The mari lwyd must use Pwnco again on their next turn, taking a circumstance penalty to their Performance DC equal to double the number of times they have used Pwnco to attempt to enter the structure today.

Failure The respondents lose. The door unlocks and opens, and any nonmagical barriers move out of the way. If the door is magically sealed, the mari lwyd attempts to counteract the effect (counteract rank 6, counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+22 #Counteract]]{+22}).

Critical Failure As failure, but the mari lwyd gets a result one degree of success better than they roll for any attempts to counteract magical barriers.

Marraine.name: Marraine
Marraine.publicNotes:
The stories are as common as they are unlikely: the mysterious noble who won the heart of a prince at a courtly ball is revealed to be the humble third son of a miller and rises to a station beyond his wildest dreams. A proud elf turns an elderly visitor away and is cursed to transform into a hideous beast, cured only when she finds "true love," and with it, happiness her wealth could never bring.

In truth, most of these stories are the machinations of fey marraines. These courtiers of the First World make up the councils marraine, a loose confederation of fey nobility who compete in a complicated game of status that mostly hinges on the bragging rights secured by ensuring the happiness and prosperity of their chosen "pet" mortals, which they call their godchildren.

While nominally benevolent, relations can quickly sour if a marraine's mortal charge disagrees with their self-proclaimed godparent's designs. Those who accept a marraine's initial gifts but reject their future meddling, or who seek to escape a "happily ever after" they've come to regret, quickly find their former benefactor enacting vengeance through powerful magic or fey allies.

spell->Lifewood Cage.name: Lifewood Cage
spell->Lifewood Cage.description:
You create an immobile, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} prison of hardened wood suffused with vital energy from the Forge of Creation. The cage is a 20-foot cube made of wooden branches, each a half inch thick and a half inch apart. Each creature in the area where you create the cage must attempt a Reflex save. If such a creature fails, it becomes trapped inside the cage. If it succeeds, it's pushed outside the cage into a space of its choice. If a creature in the area is too big to fit inside the prison, the spell automatically fails.

The cage has AC 10, Hardness 20, and 40 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage, though it has weakness 5 to void damage. A creature capable of passing through the space between the bars (typically a Tiny creature) can leave; all others are confined within. The vitality energy suffusing the wood prevents incorporeal undead creatures from passing through the beams. Attacks with a weapon too large to fit between the bars can't pass through the cage, and the bars provide standard cover even against attacks that can pass through the gaps. Spells and most area effects (such as dragon breath) can pass through the cage uninhibited.

spell->Planar Palace.name: Planar Palace
spell->Planar Palace.description:
You grow an extradimensional demiplane consisting of a spacious dwelling with a single entrance. The entrance connects to the plane where you Cast the Spell, appearing anywhere within the spell's range as a faint, shimmering, vertical rectangle 5 feet wide and 10 feet high. You designate who can enter when you Cast the Spell. Once inside, you can shut the entrance, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. You and the creatures you designated can reopen the door at will.

Inside, the demiplane appears to be a mansion featuring a magnificent foyer and numerous opulent chambers. The mansion can have any floor plan you imagine as you Cast the Spell, provided it fits within a space 40 feet wide, 40 feet deep, and 30 feet tall. While the entrance to the mansion is closed, effects from outside the mansion fail to penetrate it, and vice versa, except for @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.5bTt2CvYHPvaR7QQ]{Interplanar Teleport}, which can be used to enter the mansion. You can use scrying magic and similar effects to observe the outside only if they're capable of crossing planes.

A staff of up to 24 servants attends to anyone within the mansion. These are like the servant created by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.xqmHD8JIjak15lRk]{Phantasmal Minion} spell, though they're visible, with an appearance you determine during casting. The mansion is stocked with enough food to serve a nine-course banquet to 150 people.

spell->Awaken Animal (DC 25).cost: herbs, 1/5 the value on Creature Creation Rituals table
spell->Awaken Animal (DC 25).description:
You grant intelligence to the target, transforming it into a beast. If it was previously an animal companion or minion, it can no longer serve as one.

Critical Success The target's Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma modifiers each increase to +2 if they were lower, and it becomes helpful to you for awakening it.

Success The target's Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma modifiers increase to +0 if they were lower and it becomes friendly to you for awakening it.

Failure You fail to awaken the target.

Critical Failure You accidentally awaken the target with a pure bestial hatred toward you. The target's Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma modifiers increase to -2 if they were lower. It becomes hostile to you, attempting to destroy you.

spell->Curse of True Form (DC 25).name: Curse of True Form (DC 25)
spell->Curse of True Form (DC 25).cost: a piece of the target's body (a lock of hair, a small vial of blood, etc.), First World herbs worth the target's level x 50 gp, and the heart of the creature you wish to turn the target into
spell->Curse of True Form (DC 25).description:
You look within the heart of the target and give it a form that reflects its true self. Over the course of the casting, the target slowly transforms into an animal representing its most recent or most heinous transgression—a bull for rage, a pig for greed and gluttony, a swan for vanity, and so on. The ritual concludes with inserting a piece of the target into the chosen animal's heart and burying it at a crossroads. You can Dismiss this ritual.

Critical Success The target transforms fully into the animal and remains in that form for the duration. It keeps its mind but can't speak or otherwise communicate in a way that an animal wouldn't. If the ritual reaches its full duration without you Dismissing it, the target becomes the animal permanently in both body and mind.

Success As critical success, but the target returns to its original form at the end of the duration.

Failure The target partially transforms and is aware you were the primary caster. For 1 week, the target has visible animal traits and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1}.

Critical Failure The ritual reflects back on you, transforming you into an appropriate creature for 1 week.

spell->Cursed Metamorphosis.name: Cursed Metamorphosis
spell->Cursed Metamorphosis.description:
You transform the target creature into a harmless animal appropriate to the area, with effects based on its Fortitude save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target's body gains minor features of the harmless animal. Its insides churn as they partially transform, causing it to be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}. When it recovers from the sickened condition, its features revert to normal.

Failure The target transforms for 1 minute but keeps its mind. If it spends all its actions on its turn concentrating on its original form, it can attempt a @Check[will] save to end the effect immediately.

Critical Failure The target is transformed into the chosen harmless animal, body and mind, for an unlimited duration.

Failure The target transforms for 1 minute but keeps its mind. If it spends all its actions on its turn concentrating on its original form, it can attempt a @Check[will] save to end the effect immediately.

Critical Failure The target is transformed into the chosen harmless animal, body and mind, for an unlimited duration.

spell->Dragon Form.name: Dragon Form
spell->Dragon Form.description:
Calling upon powerful magic, you gain a Large dragon battle form. When you Cast this Spell, choose one type of common dragon or another type to which your GM allows access. While in this form, you gain the dragon trait. You have hands in this battle form and can take manipulate actions. You can Dismiss the spell.

You gain the following statistics and abilities regardless of which battle form you choose:

  • AC = 18 + your level. Ignore your armor's check penalty and Speed reduction.

  • 10 temporary Hit Points.

  • Speed 40 feet, fly 100 feet. You gain any of the following Speeds the chosen dragon has, but with the listed amount: burrow 20 feet, climb 40 feet, swim 60 feet.

  • Resistance 10 against the damage type of your Dragon Breath (see below).

  • Darkvision and imprecise scent 60 feet.

  • The following unarmed melee attacks, which are the only attacks you can Strike with. You're trained with them. Your attack modifier is +22, and your damage bonus is +6. These attacks are Strength based (for the purpose of the enfeebled condition, for example). If your unarmed attack modifier is higher, you can use it instead. See below for more on these attacks.

    • Melee 1 jaws, Damage 2d12 piercing plus 2d6 damage of the same damage type as your Dragon Breath (see below);

    • Melee 1 claw (agile), Damage 3d10 slashing;

    • Melee 1 tail (reach 10 feet), Damage 3d10 bludgeoning.

  • Athletics modifier of +23, unless your own is higher.

  • Dragon Breath 2 You exhale deadly magical energy in an area, dealing 10d6 damage to each creature in the area with a basic save against your spell DC. The shape, damage type, and save type match that of your chosen dragon's breath. If the chosen dragon's breath can deal more than one type of damage, choose one when you cast dragon form. The shape is a 30-foot cone or a 100-foot line. Once activated, Dragon Breath can't be used again for 1d4 rounds. Dragon Breath has the tradition trait matching the type of dragon and the damage trait matching the type of damage it deals, if applicable.

  • Tradition Resistance If the dragon's magical tradition matches that of your dragon form spell, you gain the listed ability. Arcane resistance 5 against magic; divine resistance 10 to spirit, vitality, and void; occult resistance 10 to mental; primal resistance 5 to physical damage.

spell->Scrying.name: Scrying
spell->Scrying.description:
You magically spy on a creature of your choice. Scrying works like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.zvKWclOZ7A53DObE]{Clairvoyance}, except that the image you receive is less precise, insufficient for teleport and similar spells. Instead of creating an eye in a set location within 500 feet, you instead create an eye that manifests just above the target. You can choose a target either by name or by touching one of its possessions or a piece of its body. If you haven't met the target in person, scrying's DC is 2 lower, and if you are unaware of the target's identity (perhaps because you found an unknown creature's fang at a crime scene), the DC is instead 10 lower.

The effect of scrying depends on the target's Will save.

Critical Success The spell fails and the target is temporarily immune for 1 week. The target also gains a glimpse of you and learns its rough distance and direction from you.

Success The spell fails and the target is temporarily immune for 1 day.

Failure The spell succeeds.

Critical Failure The spell succeeds, and the eye follows the target if it moves, traveling up to 60 feet per round.

spell->Illusory Scene.name: Illusory Scene
spell->Illusory Scene.description:
You craft an imaginary scene that includes up to 10 discrete creatures or objects of various sizes, all of which must be within the spell's area. These elements generate appropriate sounds and smells, and they feel right to the touch. Elements of an illusory scene are incapable of speech. Unlike with the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.f8SBoXiXQjlCKqly]{Illusory Creature} spell, creatures in your scene lack combat abilities and statistics. Your scene doesn't include changes to the environment around it, though you can place your scene within the illusory environment of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HBJPsonQnWcC3qdX]{Mirage} spell.

When you create the scene, you can choose to have it be static or follow a program. Though a static scene is stationary, it includes basic natural movement. For example, wind blowing on an illusory piece of paper would rustle it. A program can be up to 1 minute long and repeats when finished. For instance, you could create a scene of two orcs fighting each other, and the fight would go the same way for each repetition. If you create a loop, the two fighters end up in the same place at the start of the scene and at the end of it, but you can smooth the program so it's hard to tell when the loop ends and begins. Anyone observing the scene for more than a few minutes almost always notices it looping. You're unable to alter the program after you create the illusion.

Any creature that touches any part of the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. If they interact with a portion of the illusion, they disbelieve only that portion. They disbelieve the entire scene only on a critical success.

Heightened (6th) Creatures or objects in your scene can speak. You must speak the specific lines for each actor when creating your program. The spell disguises your voice for each actor.

Heightened (8th) As the 6th-rank version, and the duration is unlimited.

spell->Truespeech (Constant).name: Truespeech (Constant)
spell->Truespeech (Constant).description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

spell->Bestial Curse.name: Bestial Curse
spell->Bestial Curse.description:
You tap into the target's inner being and curse it to become a bestial version of itself. The effect is based on its Fortitude save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target's body gains minor bestial features. Its insides churn as they partially transform, causing it to be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round. When it recovers from the clumsy condition, its features revert to normal, and the spell ends.

Failure The target transforms into a bestial form for 1 hour. The target becomes clumsy 1 and gains weakness 1 to silver. It gains a claw, hoof, horn, or jaws Strike (your choice) that uses the target's unarmed Strike statistics except that the damage type changes to bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing, as appropriate. Whenever the target attempts to use any manipulate action, it must succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:5] or the action is lost.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.8wCVSzWYcURWewbd]{Spell Effect: Bestial Curse (Failure)}

Critical Failure As failure, but the duration is unlimited.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.KtAJN4Qr2poTL6BB]{Spell Effect: Bestial Curse (Critical Failure)}

spell->Clairvoyance.name: Clairvoyance
spell->Clairvoyance.description: You create an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} floating eye at a location within range (even if it's outside your line of sight or line of effect). The eye can't move, but you can see in all directions from that point as if using your normal visual senses.

spell->Creation.name: Creation
spell->Creation.description:
You conjure a temporary object from magical energy. It must consist of earthen or plant-derived matter (such as wood, paper, brick, or stone) and be 5 cubic feet or smaller. It can't rely on intricate artistry or complex moving parts, never fulfills a cost or the like, and can't be made of precious materials or materials with a rarity of uncommon or higher. It is obviously temporarily conjured, and thus can't be sold or passed off as a genuine item. The spell gains the appropriate trait for the item created, typically earth, plant, or wood.

Heightened (5th) The item is metal and can include common minerals, like feldspar or quartz. The spell gains the metal trait if used to create a metal object

spell->Blindness.name: Blindness
spell->Blindness.description:
You blind the target. The effect is determined by the target's Fortitude save. The target then becomes temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} until its next turn begins.

Failure The target is Blinded for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is Blinded permanently.

spell->Cozy Cabin.name: Cozy Cabin
spell->Cozy Cabin.description:
You shape a cabin 20 feet on each side and 10 feet high. This cabin has the structure trait and the same restrictions as magic items that create structures. The walls of the hut are simple and wooden, with small, square glass windows, and it has one wooden door. It doesn't include its own lock, but it has a fastener to which a lock can be applied.

The interior contains three cots, one chamber pot, and a small fireplace holding a magical fire. The interior is lit with a small magical light that you can light or extinguish at will using a Sustain action. The climate inside the hut is comfortable and allows creatures inside it to withstand most hostile weather conditions, but incredible heat or cold, powerful storms, and winds of hurricane force or greater destroy the hut. Other creatures can freely enter and exit the hut without damaging it, but if you exit the hut, the spell ends. You can Dismiss the spell.

spell->Mystic Carriage (DC 25).name: Mystic Carriage (DC 25)
spell->Mystic Carriage (DC 25).cost: toy carriage, horse statues, rare incense, and feathers worth 50 gp total
spell->Mystic Carriage (DC 25).description:
Magic is often the ideal method of transportation. This ritual allows you and the other casters to conjure a magical carriage that transports you to a destination of your choice. To summon the mystic carriage, you must be within 250 miles of your destination and spend 1 hour burning incense and feathers while chanting the name of the location you wish the carriage to take you to. When it arrives, the carriage is a Large vehicle that can fit 6 Medium or smaller passengers, as well as 100 Bulk of cargo. It has a Speed of 60 feet, AC 14, Fortitude saving throw modifier of +8, Hardness 5, 100 Hit Points (BT 50), object immunities, and immunity to critical hits and precision damage.

Once loaded and boarded, the mystic carriage sets out at a Speed of 60 feet, heading unerringly towards its destination using whatever roads and trails are available. If it's attacked, it continues going as long as nothing blocks its passage. If something blocks its way, living or otherwise, it will stop until the way is cleared, waiting to continue until all its passengers are aboard once more.

Critical Success You create a mystic carriage that lasts for 2 weeks instead of 1 week. It can take you to up to two destinations, the first of which must be within 250 miles and the second of which must be within 250 miles of the first destination.

Success You create a mystic carriage as described above, save that it lasts only 1 week.

Failure You don't create a mystic carriage.

Critical Failure You don't create a mystic carriage, and you're attacked by a herd of four riding horses.

Heightened (+1) The carriage's AC, Fortitude save, and Hardness increase by 2, its Hit Points increase by 20, and its Broken Threshold increases by 10.

spell->Safe Passage.name: Safe Passage
spell->Safe Passage.description:
Area 10-foot-wide, 10-foot-tall, 60-foot-long section of terrain

You make passage through the area safe for a brief amount of time. Anyone passing through the area gains the following benefits against harmful effects of the terrain and environment, including environmental damage, hazardous terrain, and hazards in the area. The spell grants a +2 status bonus to AC and saves against such effects, and resistance 5 to all damage from such effects. Furthermore, the spell prevents anything in the area that's prone to collapse, such as a rickety bridge or an unstable ceiling, from collapsing, except under extreme strain that would collapse a normal structure of its type.

Safe passage protects only against harm, not inconvenience, and it doesn't reduce difficult terrain, remove the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} condition caused by precipitation, or the like, nor does it protect against creatures within the spell's area.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.5blVLpIH65hvFJpn]{Spell Effect: Safe Passage}

Heightened (5th) The granted resistance increases to 10, and the area can be 120 feet long.

Heightened (8th) The granted resistance increases to 15, and the area can be 500 feet long.

spell->Shrink Item.name: Shrink Item
spell->Shrink Item.description: You shrink the target to roughly the size of a coin with negligible Bulk. You can Dismiss the spell, and the spell ends if you toss the object onto a solid surface. The object can't be used to attack or cause damage during the process of it returning to normal size. If there isn't room for the object to return to normal size when the spell ends, the spell's duration continues until the object is in a location large enough to accommodate its normal size.
spell->Shrink Item.target: 1 non-magical object up to 20 cubic feet in volume and up to 80 Bulk

spell->Wall of Thorns.name: Wall of Thorns
spell->Wall of Thorns.description:
You grow a wall of thorny brambles from the ground. You create a 5-foot-thick wall of brambles and thorns in a straight line up to 60 feet long and 10 feet high. You must create the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost. The wall stands vertically. If you wish, the wall can be of a shorter length or height. Everything on each side of the wall has cover from creatures on the opposite side, and the wall's spaces are difficult terrain. For every move action a creature uses to enter at least one of the wall's spaces, that creature takes 3d4 piercing damage.

Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 20 Hit Points. It's immune to critical hits and precision damage. A destroyed section can be moved through freely.

Heightened (+1) The Hit Points of each section of the wall increase by 5, and the piercing damage increases by 1d4.

spell->Animate Object (DC 25).name: Animate Object (DC 25)
spell->Animate Object (DC 25).cost: rare oils, see Creature Creation Rituals
spell->Animate Object (DC 25).description:
You transform the target into an animated object with a level up to that allowed by the Creature Creation Rituals table and of a type corresponding to the object (so a broom would become an animated broom).

Critical Success The target becomes an animated object of the appropriate type. If it's at least 4 levels lower than you, you can make it a minion. This gives it the minion trait, meaning it can use 2 actions when you command it, and commanding it is a single action that has the auditory and concentrate traits. You can have a maximum of four minions under your control. If it doesn't become a minion, you can give it one simple command. It pursues that goal single-mindedly, ignoring any of your subsequent commands.

Success As critical success, except an animated object that doesn't become your minion stays in place and attacks anyone that attacks it or tries to steal or move it, rather than following your command.

Failure You fail to create the animated object.

Critical Failure You create the animated object, but it goes berserk and attempts to destroy you.
