spell->Animated Assault.name: Animated Assault
spell->Animated Assault.description:
You use your mind to manipulate unattended objects in the area, temporarily animating them to attack. The objects hover in the air, then hurl themselves at nearby creatures in a chaotic flurry of debris. This assault deals 2d10 bludgeoning damage (basic Reflex save) to each creature in the area. On subsequent rounds, the first time each round you Sustain this Spell, it deals @Damage[(floor(@item.level/2))d10[bludgeoning]] damage (basic Reflex save) to each creature in the area.

Heightened (+2) The initial damage increases by 2d10 and the subsequent damage increases by 1d10.

spell->Befitting Attire.name: Befitting Attire
spell->Befitting Attire.description:
You cloak the targets in an illusion, shaping their clothing and worn items into ones suitable for a particular occasion. You visualize the occasion, and the spell creates illusory attire customized to each target. For instance, if you visualized a noble ball, armor would appear to be fine clothing. This doesn't change identifying details of the targets' appearances other than their clothes.

Any creature that touches the attire, uses the [[/act seek]] action to examine it, or otherwise interacts with it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 20 creatures.

Heightened (5th) You can target up to 100 creatures.

spell->Charitable Urge.name: Charitable Urge
spell->Charitable Urge.description:
You speak on the virtue of charity, compelling the target to give away its possessions. The target must attempt a Will save. If the target has no items on its person, the spell fails.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} as it wrestles with the urge.

Failure On its next turn, before it does anything else, the target must present the nearest creature with an item in its possession; the target chooses which item to give, and if the only item it has is one that it's currently using to defend itself, such as a weapon during a combat encounter, it can choose to be stunned for 1 round instead of giving up the item. This might require the target to Interact to retrieve an item or move to reach the nearest creature, and passing the item off requires an Interact action as normal.

Critical Failure As failure, except the duration is 4 rounds, and the target must repeat the effects of a failure on each of its turns. At the end of each of its turns, the target can attempt a new Will save to reduce the remaining duration by 1 round, ending the effects entirely on a critical success.

spell->Invisibility (At Will, Self only).name: Invisibility (At Will, Self only)
spell->Invisibility (At Will, Self only).description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Knock.name: Knock
spell->Knock.description:
You make the target easier to open. Knock grants a +4 status bonus to any creature that tries to open the target door, lock, or container with an Athletics or a Thievery check. You can attempt a Thievery check to open the target as part of casting knock, and you add your level even if you're untrained.

Knock counteracts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Azoh0BSoCASrA1lr]{Lock}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.OSapCU8heNHst21y]{Spell Effect: Knock}

spell->Marvelous Mount.name: Marvelous Mount
spell->Marvelous Mount.description:
You conjure a Large fantastical creature to serve as a mount for the target. The mount is the target's minion, has a Speed of 40 feet, and can bear the target with any carried possessions. It can't carry any other creature. The mount uses the target's AC and saves, but it's destroyed if it takes more than 10 damage at one time, ending the spell.

Heightened (3rd) The mount can walk on water, but it must end its turn on solid ground or sink.

Heightened (4th) The mount has a Speed of 60 feet and can walk on water.

Heightened (5th) The mount has a Speed of 60 feet and can walk on water. It also has a fly Speed of 60 feet, but it must end its turn on a surface or fall.

Heightened (6th) The mount has a Speed and fly Speed of 80 feet.

spell->Telekinetic Maneuver.name: Telekinetic Maneuver
spell->Telekinetic Maneuver.description: With a rush of telekinetic power, you move a foe or something they carry. You can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shove}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.lOE4yjUnETTdaf2T]{Reposition}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip} the target using a spell attack roll instead of an Athletics check.

spell->Charm.name: Charm
spell->Charm.description:
To the target, your words are honey and your visage seems bathed in a dreamy haze. It must attempt a Will save, with a +4 circumstance bonus if you or your allies recently threatened it or used hostile actions against it.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you use hostile actions against the target, the spell ends. When the spell ends, the target doesn't necessarily realize it was charmed unless its friendship with you or the actions you convinced it to take clash with its expectations, meaning you could potentially convince the target to continue being your friend via mundane means.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and aware you tried to charm it.

Success The target is unaffected but thinks your spell was something harmless instead of charm, unless it identifies the spell.

Failure The target's attitude becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v66R7FdOf11l94im]{Friendly} toward you. If it was Friendly, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v44P3WUcU1j0115l]{Helpful}. It can't use hostile actions against you.

Critical Failure The target's attitude becomes Helpful toward you, and it can't use hostile actions against you.

Heightened (4th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations.

Heightened (8th) The duration lasts until the next time you make your daily preparations, and you can target up to 10 creatures.

spell->Daze.name: Daze
spell->Daze.description:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

spell->Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
spell->Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an invisibility potion) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

spell->Disguise Magic.name: Disguise Magic
spell->Disguise Magic.description:
You alter how an item's or spell's magical aura appears to effects like detect magic. You can hide the auras entirely, have an item register as a common item of lower level, or make a spell register as a common spell of the same or lower rank. You can Dismiss the spell. A caster using @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OhD2Z6rIGGD5ocZA]{Read Aura} of a higher rank than disguise magic can attempt to disbelieve the illusion using the skill matching the tradition of the spell (Arcana for arcane, Religion for divine, Occultism for occult, or Nature for primal). Further attempts by the same caster get the same result as the initial check to disbelieve.

Heightened (2nd) You can Cast this Spell on a creature, disguising all items and spell effects on it.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Gentle Landing.name: Gentle Landing
spell->Gentle Landing.description:
Trigger a creature within range is falling

You raise a magical updraft to arrest a fall. The target's fall slows to 60 feet per round, and the portion of the fall during the spell's duration doesn't count when calculating falling damage. If the target reaches the ground while the spell is in effect, it takes no damage from the fall. The spell ends as soon as the target lands.

spell->Item Facade.name: Item Facade
spell->Item Facade.description:
You make the target object look and feel as though it were in much better or worse physical condition. When you cast this spell, decide whether you want to make the object look decrepit or perfect. An item made to look decrepit appears @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken} and shoddy. An intact item made to look better appears as though it's brand new and highly polished or well maintained. A Broken item appears to be intact and functional. Destroyed items can't be affected by this spell. A creature that Interacts with the item can attempt to disbelieve the illusion.

Heightened (2nd) The duration is 24 hours.

Heightened (3rd) The duration is unlimited.
spell->Item Facade.target: 1 object no more than 10 feet by 10 feet by 10 feet

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

spell->Mending.name: Mending
spell->Mending.description:
You repair the target item. You restore 5 Hit Points per spell rank to the target, potentially removing the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken} condition if this repairs it past the item's Broken Threshold. You can't replace lost pieces or repair an object that's been completely destroyed.

Heightened (2nd) You can target a non-magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Heightened (3rd) You can target a non-magical object of 2 Bulk or less, or a magical object of 1 Bulk or less.
spell->Mending.target: non-magical object of light Bulk or less

spell->Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
spell->Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

spell->Thoughtful Gift (At Will).name: Thoughtful Gift (At Will)
spell->Thoughtful Gift (At Will).description:
You teleport one object of light or negligible Bulk held in your hand to the target. The object appears instantly in the target's hand if they have a free hand, or at their feet if they don't. The target knows what object you're attempting to send them. If the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} or refuses to accept your gift, or if the spell would teleport a creature (even if the creature is inside an extradimensional container), the spell fails.

Heightened (3rd) The spell's range increases to 500 feet.

Heightened (5th) As 3rd rank, and the object's maximum Bulk increases to 1. You can Cast the Spell with 3 actions instead of 1; doing so increases the range to 1 mile, and you don't need line of sight to the target, but you must be extremely familiar with the target.

weapon->Marraine Wand.name: Marraine Wand
weapon->Marraine Wand.description: A light mace has a short wooden or metal shaft ending with a dense metal head. Used much like a club, it delivers heavy bludgeoning blows, but with extra power derived from the head's metal ridges or spikes.

action->Council Marraine.name: Council Marraine
action->Council Marraine.description: For their mutual benefit, marraines form councils of exactly three or seven members. A council marraine acts as a hag's coven but has the arcane trait instead of occult and their granted spells also include @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.TUj8eugNqAvB1vVR]{Creation}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Ucf8eynbZMfUucjE]{Illusory Scene}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.r784cIz17eWujtQj]{Scrying}. If the council has seven members, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.5c692cCcTDXjSEzk]{dragon form,} @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HES5jvGiNZZnJycK]{Lifewood Cage}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vPWMEyVTreMOoFnm]{Planar Palace} are also added to their granted spells, and when council members Cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.dN8QBNuTiaBHCKUe]{Cursed Metamorphosis} as a coven spell, they can transform targets into sentient animated objects as well as harmless animals, and can transform animals or objects into humanoids. If a creature critically fails, their transformation into an object ends at the next midnight or sunrise (depending on the council's bylaws).

action->Sudden Appearance.name: Sudden Appearance
action->Sudden Appearance.description:
Frequency once per week

Requirements The target is in the Universe, and the marraine is in either the First World or the Universe

Effect The marraine teleports to an unoccupied space within 30 feet of a creature they've marked as their godchild. They must have previously seen the target, typically with a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.zvKWclOZ7A53DObE]{Clairvoyance} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.r784cIz17eWujtQj]{Scrying} spell.

Melixie.name: Melixie
Melixie.publicNotes:
Melixies are hyperactive insect sprites with legendary sweet tooths, capable of gulping down honey, nectar, sugar, and other sweets in alarming quantities. Melixies have antennae and additional insect features that typically resemble those of bees but sometimes butterflies, moths, ladybugs, or other beetles. Melixies live in a pattern of rapid sweets consumption, incredible productivity in tasks of all sorts, and then a crash to sleep it all off and start again. In their spare time, they love to dance, and some learn a dancelike sign language called Melipatter, allowing them to communicate a full range of information through movement.

Elusive, flighty, and ebullient, sprites are what many villagers first imagine when they hear the terms "fey" or "fairy."

spell->Ant Haul.name: Ant Haul
spell->Ant Haul.description:
You reinforce the target's musculoskeletal system to bear more weight. The target can carry 3 more Bulk than normal before becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.D5mg6Tc7Jzrj6ro7]{Encumbered} and up to a maximum of 6 more Bulk.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.5yCL7InrJDHpaQjz]{Spell Effect: Ant Haul}

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

action->Speak with Arthropods.name: Speak with Arthropods
action->Speak with Arthropods.description: A melixie can communicate with arthropods, such as insects, spiders, scorpions, crabs, and similar invertebrate animals. They can use Diplomacy to [[/act make-an-impression]] on arthropods and [[/act request]] things from arthropods.

action->Sugar Rush.name: Sugar Rush
action->Sugar Rush.description: The melixie consumes a large quantity of sugar, honey, nectar, or similar sweets and goes into a frenzied state. The melixie immediately Strides or Flies. For the next 1d4+1 rounds, the melixie is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} and can use the additional action only to Stride or Fly. As soon as the rush ends, the melixie is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} for 1 minute.

Monaciello.name: Monaciello
Monaciello.publicNotes:
Monaciellos delight in moral and institutional decay. They tempt with the easy course, encouraging laziness and apathy. They're the little voice that whispers that no one will notice, that it's not really worth the effort, that there's a quicker, easier solution if you just try just a little less hard.

Monaciellos resemble small, sharp-toothed humanoids clad in the formal clothing of whatever institution or organization they're harassing. Most dress like religious figures—there's nothing a monaciello loves quite so much as a church lost to decadence and self-indulgence—but a monaciello might also pose as a well-to-do farmer, a civil servant, or even a soldier. There's always something slovenly and unkempt about their uniform of choice, and they keep a filthy magic bag thrown over one shoulder or near at hand. Monaciellos cause endless trouble by stealing small items, secreting them in their sack, and then bringing them out at the perfect moment to tempt mortals into indolence and sloth. These items are rarely impressive, but the gremlins always seem to have a drink or gold coin at hand when a mortal craves it most.

Like many fey, gremlins personify a natural force of the world: entropy. It's a fundamental truth that everything breaks, that every complex system, from a machine to a society, will inevitably grind itself down to nothing. Gremlins are happy to give those complex systems a friendly shove down the stairs.

Nearly all gremlins live in the Universe, where they have fully acclimated to the plane. No one is quite certain why, but it seems likely that some long-forgotten gremlin managed to so irritate the Eldest to such a degree that their entire species was exiled—though it appears the Eldest missed a few, as some gremlins still lurk in the First World.

Gremlins are usually found in an odd, parasitic relationship with mortal communities in the Universe. They don't need to eat or sleep, don't age or sicken, and never really die—but they do need to cause trouble. It's as essential to them as food and drink are to mortals, and nowhere do they get as many chances for chaos and confusion as in a mortal settlement. Gremlins thus become pests, living on the margins of society and bedeviling anyone and anything they can get their hands on.
Monaciello.saveDetails: +1 status to all saves vs. divine magic

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Illusory Disguise.name: Illusory Disguise
spell->Illusory Disguise.description:
You create an illusion that causes the target to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise is typically good enough to hide their identity, but not to impersonate a specific individual. The spell changes their appearance and voice, but not mannerisms. You can change the appearance of its clothing and worn items, such as making its armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item removed from the creature returns to its true appearance.

Casting illusory disguise counts as setting up a disguise for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} use of Deception; it ignores any circumstance penalties the target might take for disguising itself as a dissimilar creature, gives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through the disguise, and lets the target add its level to such Deception checks even if untrained. You can Dismiss this spell.

Heightened (3rd) The target can appear as any creature of the same size, even a specific individual. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 willing creatures. If you target multiple creatures, you can choose a different disguise for each target, but none can impersonate a specific individual. You can Dismiss each disguise individually or all collectively.

Heightened (7th) As 4th, but you can choose disguises that impersonate specific individuals. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3Ktyd5F9lOPo4myk]{Spell Effect: Illusory Disguise}

spell->Illusory Object.name: Illusory Object
spell->Illusory Object.description:
You create an illusory visual image of a stationary object. The entire image must fit within the spell's area. The object appears to animate naturally, but it doesn't make sounds or generate smells. For example, water would appear to pour down an illusory waterfall, but it would be silent.

Any creature that touches the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) Your image makes appropriate sounds, generates normal smells, and feels right to the touch. The spell gains the auditory and olfactory traits. The duration increases to 1 hour.

Heightened (5th) As the 2nd-rank version, but the duration is unlimited.

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

action->Magic Sack.name: Magic Sack
action->Magic Sack.description: A monaciello's sack functions as a spacious pouch (type I) as long as it's in the monaciello's possession. If the sack is separated from the monaciello, its contents are lost and it becomes a normal bag. A monaciello who loses their bag must create a new one, a process that takes 2 days.

action->+1 Status to All Saves vs. Divin.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Divine Magic

action->Rude Blasphemy.name: Rude Blasphemy
action->Rude Blasphemy.description:
Trigger A creature within 30 feet casts a divine spell

Effect The monaciello makes a blasphemous gesture tailor-made to offend the target's religion, attempting to counteract the spell (counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+6 #Counteract]]{+6}, counteract rank 1st). The monaciello can't use Rude Blasphemy again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Rude Blasphemy]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Heart's Desire.name: Heart's Desire
action->Heart's Desire.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The monaciello pulls a desirable object from its sack. Each creature within 15 feet who can see the object immediately covets it and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:17] save. If the monaciello spends two actions on Heart's Desire, this must be a real object already in their possession. If they spend three actions, they can cast illusory object as part of the activity, which gains the subtle trait.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Failure The target is slowed 1 for 1 round and, if it doesn't have a free hand, must spend its first action on its next turn to Release one item it's holding to grab for the object instead.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} instead.

Murxie.name: Murxie
Murxie.publicNotes:
Sprite

The fey of the Ether Court in the Darklands have evolved somewhat differently from the First World kin that exiled them, becoming more cruel and less mischievous than is typical for their kind.

Ether Sprite

The excitable sprites of the Ether Court prefer to frolic, drink, insult each other, and perform improv comedy.

Sprite Collections

Ether sprites have a reputation for being thieves. In truth, they're generally curious about the world and simply have a tendency to walk away with objects that don't belong to them, not understanding the concept of ownership. As a result, ether sprites tend to have small interesting objects in their possession, such as talismans or gemstones.

action->Natural Glow.name: Natural Glow
action->Natural Glow.description: A murxie sheds light as a torch. The murxie can Sustain this glow to suppress or reignite it.

action->Hilarious Insult.name: Hilarious Insult
action->Hilarious Insult.description: he murxie taunts a creature within 30 feet, attempting a @Check[performance|defense:will] check against the target's Will DC. On a success, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} until the end of its next turn, after which it is temporarily immune to Hilarious Insult for 10 minutes.

Nornhound.name: Nornhound
Nornhound.publicNotes:
While norns typically keep to themselves, only consulting their triumvirate or occasionally other fellow norns, they sometimes require servants to further their goals or protect their homes. Nornhounds are massive wolves norns spun from the old, tattered threads of fate, usually moments of time severed to end a life. These wolves gain a portion of their creators' power over fate and serve their norn masters with unflinching loyalty.

Where their masters snip and mend threads of fate with subtlety and precision, nornhounds do so brutally and forcefully, overwhelming their foes with blasts and waves of skipped time and overlapping possibilities. A mortal who faces down a nornhound often finds themselves with permanent mental effects, remembering lives that aren't their own or responding to questions a second before they're asked.

Nornhound Packs

Long-lived or powerful norns sometimes spin multiple nornhounds and keep entire packs as guardians. These packs make quick work of intruders, gaining additional powers when working together. Much like a norn triumvirate, a nornhound pack can combine their power to affect the flow of time in a localized area, even stopping it outright. These packs are rarely found far from the domains of their masters, but those who survive an encounter find the experience impossible to describe to others.

spell->Cast into Time.name: Cast into Time
spell->Cast into Time.description:
You release a wave of temporal energy that sends creatures violently tumbling through time, scarring their thoughts with the information flowing around them. Although the journey can feel like it lasts for minutes or even days, the targets reappear instantly. Witnessing this chaotic flow of time and being bashed against objects from the past and future deals 5d8 mental damage and 5d6 bludgeoning damage to creatures in the area, with a Fortitude save. A creature that falls into time disappears until the end of your turn. It then reappears in the same space it left; if that space is occupied, it appears in the nearest empty space, chosen by the GM. Creatures that are immune to mental effects can still be affected by this spell but take no mental damage.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature falls into time. When it returns, it takes half damage.

Failure The creature falls into time. When it returns, it takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Critical Failure The creature falls into time. When it returns, it takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.

Heightened (+1) The bludgeoning damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Teleport (Self Only, At Will).name: Teleport (Self Only, At Will)
spell->Teleport (Self Only, At Will).description:
You and the targets are instantly transported to any location within range, as long as you can identify the location precisely both by its position relative to your starting position and by its appearance (or other identifying features). Incorrect knowledge of the location's appearance usually causes the spell to fail, but it could instead lead to teleporting to an unwanted location or some other unusual mishap determined by the GM. Teleport is not precise over great distances. The targets appear at a distance from the intended destination equal to roughly 1 percent of the total distance traveled, in a direction determined by the GM. For short journeys, this lack of precision is irrelevant, but for long distances this could be up to 1 mile.

Heightened (7th) You and the other targets can travel to any location within 1,000 miles.

Heightened (8th) You and the other targets can travel to any location on the same planet. If you travel more than 1,000 miles, you arrive only 10 miles off target.

Heightened (9th) You and the other targets can travel to any location on another planet within the same solar system. Assuming you have accurate knowledge of the location's position and appearance, you arrive on the new planet 100 miles off target.

Heightened (10th) As the 9th-rank version, but you and the other targets can travel to any planet within the same galaxy.
spell->Teleport (Self Only, At Will).target: you and up to 4 targets touched, either willing creatures or objects roughly the size of a creature.

spell->Truesight (Constant).name: Truesight (Constant)
spell->Truesight (Constant).description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

spell->Inevitable Disaster.name: Inevitable Disaster
spell->Inevitable Disaster.description:
You briefly glimpse cause and effect, putting into motion a chain of events that will visit doom on your enemy at some point in the future, though you're not quite sure when or how the doom will occur. Some kind of strange accident occurs [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds} later, dealing 55 damage to the creature, with a basic Fortitude save. This happens regardless of where the target is located at the time, even if it travels to another plane. The GM should roll to determine when the damage occurs secretly and determine the form of the accident as well as the type of damage it deals; generally, the accident should be one that deals physical damage of some type (for instance, a tree branch might fall on the foe and deal bludgeoning damage, or a window might break and fling sharp slashing glass at them), though other damage types might be appropriate in more unusual environments.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 10.

spell->Truespeech (Constant).name: Truespeech (Constant)
spell->Truespeech (Constant).description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

spell->Slow.name: Slow
spell->Slow.description:
You dilate the flow of time around the target, slowing its actions.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} for 1 minute.

Heightened (6th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

spell->Detect Magic (Constant).name: Detect Magic (Constant)
spell->Detect Magic (Constant).description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an invisibility potion) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

condition->Quickened.name: Quickened
condition->Quickened.description: You gain 1 additional action at the start of your turn each round. Many effects that make you quickened specify the types of actions you can use with this additional action. If you become quickened from multiple sources, you can use the extra action you've been granted for any single action allowed by any of the effects that made you quickened. Because quickened has its effect at the start of your turn, you don't immediately gain actions if you become quickened during your turn.

action->Sense Fate.name: Sense Fate
action->Sense Fate.description: A nornhound automatically rolls a 20 when it rolls initiative.

action->Beyond Fate.name: Beyond Fate
action->Beyond Fate.description: A nornhound can ignore any fortune or misfortune effects that affect them. If they're forced to roll twice as part of such an effect, they can take whichever die result they prefer, even if the effect would normally force them to choose one of the results.

action->Follow the Thread.name: Follow the Thread
action->Follow the Thread.description: A nornhound is permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened}. It can use its extra action only to Step or Stride.

action->Pack Attack.name: Pack Attack
action->Pack Attack.description: The nornhound's Strikes deal 1d6 extra damage to creatures within reach of at least two of its allies.

action->Temporal Wave.name: Temporal Wave
action->Temporal Wave.description: The nornhound unleashes a blast of temporal energy in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] that deals @Damage[15d8[mental]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[will|dc:40|basic] save). Creatures that fail their save become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round. The nornhound can't use Temporal Wave again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Temporal Wave]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Time Bound.name: Time Bound
action->Time Bound.description: The nornhound jumps into the air, releasing multiple blasts of temporal energy. The nornhound leaps to a point within 60 feet. It can make up to three temporal blast Strikes at any point during this movement, each against a different target. These attacks count toward the nornhound's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after all the attacks.

Nuglub.name: Nuglub
Nuglub.publicNotes:
The "towering" hunchbacked nuglubs are among the largest gremlins, though they're not even 3 feet tall. They have three glowing blue eyes and black, oily hair on their head and back that covers them like a cloak. Nuglubs enjoy killing with a glee that other gremlins reserve for sabotage. They spend long hours preparing ambushes for unwary travelers or plotting the murders of sleeping villagers. Though less technically inclined than their kin, nuglubs do enjoy building traps.

Like many fey, gremlins personify a natural force of the world: entropy. It's a fundamental truth that everything breaks, that every complex system, from a machine to a society, will inevitably grind itself down to nothing. Gremlins are happy to give those complex systems a friendly shove down the stairs.

Nearly all gremlins live in the Universe, where they have fully acclimated to the plane. No one is quite certain why, but it seems likely that some long-forgotten gremlin managed to so irritate the Eldest to such a degree that their entire species was exiled—though it appears the Eldest missed a few, as some gremlins still lurk in the First World.

Gremlins are usually found in an odd, parasitic relationship with mortal communities in the Universe. They don't need to eat or sleep, don't age or sicken, and never really die—but they do need to cause trouble. It's as essential to them as food and drink are to mortals, and nowhere do they get as many chances for chaos and confusion as in a mortal settlement. Gremlins thus become pests, living on the margins of society and bedeviling anyone and anything they can get their hands on.

spell->Shatter.name: Shatter
spell->Shatter.description:
A high-frequency sonic attack shatters a nearby object. You deal 2d10 sonic damage to the object, ignoring the object's Hardness if it is 4 or lower.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10, and the Hardness the spell ignores increases by 2.

spell->Grease.name: Grease
spell->Grease.description:
You conjure grease, choosing an area or target.

  • Area [4 contiguous 5-foot squares] All solid ground in the area is covered with grease. Each creature standing on the greasy surface must succeed at a Reflex save or an Acrobatics check against your spell DC or fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. Creatures using an action to move onto the greasy surface during the spell's duration must attempt either a Reflex save or an Acrobatics check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.M76ycLAqHoAgbcej]{Balance}. A creature that Steps or Crawls doesn't have to attempt a check or save.
  • Target [1 object of Bulk 1 or less] If you Cast the Spell on an unattended object, anyone trying to pick up the object must succeed at an Acrobatics check or Reflex save against your spell DC to do so. If you target an attended object, the creature that has the object must attempt an Acrobatics check or Reflex save. On a failure, the holder or wielder takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all checks that involve using the object; on a critical failure, the holder or wielder releases the item. The object lands in an adjacent square of the GM's choice. If you Cast this Spell on a worn object, the wearer gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves against attempts to grapple them.

spell->Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
spell->Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

spell->Thunderstrike.name: Thunderstrike
spell->Thunderstrike.description:
You call down a tendril of lightning that cracks with thunder, dealing 1d12 electricity damage and 1d4 sonic damage to the target with a basic Reflex save. A target wearing metal armor or made of metal takes a –1 circumstance bonus to its save, and if damaged by the spell is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d12 electricity and 1d4 sonic.

action->Kneecapper.name: Kneecapper
action->Kneecapper.description:
Trigger A Medium or smaller creature within the nuglub's reach leaves a square during its move action

Effect The nuglub lashes out at the triggering creature's knees and tries to knock it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. The nuglub attempts an @Check[acrobatics|against:reflex] check against the creature's Reflex DC. On a success, the target falls and lands prone.

action->Vicious Attack.name: Vicious Attack
action->Vicious Attack.description: A nuglub's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} targets, or 1d10 precision damage if the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Nyktera.name: Nyktera
Nyktera.publicNotes:
Nykteras, or bat sprites, are gentle fey known for their affectionate nature and incredible hospitality. Nykteras share features with bats, but the type of bat varies by location. A nyktera's sense of hospitality is such that they're willing to share with any who need it, even bitter foes. Violating a nyktera's hospitality is one of their greatest taboos, inviting rare anger and retribution from the nyktera who was wronged, as well as their large extended family.

Elusive, flighty, and ebullient, sprites are what many villagers first imagine when they hear the terms "fey" or "fairy."

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Heal.name: Heal
spell->Heal.description:
You channel vital energy to heal the living or damage the undead. If the target is a willing living creature, you restore 1d8 Hit Points. If the target is undead, you deal that amount of vitality damage to it, and it gets a basic Fortitude save. The number of actions you spend when Casting this Spell determines its targets, range, area, and other parameters.

1 The spell has a range of touch.

2 (concentrate) The spell has a range of 30 feet. If you're healing a living creature, increase the Hit Points restored by 8.

3 (concentrate) You disperse vital energy in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. This targets all living and undead creatures in the burst.

Heightened (+1) The amount of healing or damage increases by 1d8, and the extra healing for the 2-action version increases by 8.

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

action->+2 Bonus on Perception to Seek c.name: +2 Bonus on Perception to Seek creatures using hearing

action->Speak with Bats.name: Speak with Bats
action->Speak with Bats.description: A nyktera can communicate with bats and use Diplomacy to [[/act make-an-impression]] on bats and [[/act request]] things from bats.

action->Wrath of Spurned Hospitality.name: Wrath of Spurned Hospitality
action->Wrath of Spurned Hospitality.description:
A nyktera whose hospitality is betrayed becomes enraged at the violation of a fundamental aspect of their fey nature. They must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:20] save or begin involuntarily attacking the traitor. At the end of each of their turns, if they choose, they can attempt another Will save to end the effect; otherwise, the effect lasts until the traitor is subdued or leaves the nyktera's presence. As long as their righteous fury lasts, the nyktera gains a +2 status bonus to attack and damage rolls for their fist Strikes.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.he0QiJSgJWNeIoxt]{Effect: Wrath of Spurned Hospitality}

Oceanid.name: Oceanid
Oceanid.publicNotes:
Where naiads are bound to their freshwater springs and nereids walk as they will between wave and shore, oceanid nymphs are, to their cores, creatures of the seas. They ride the open waves as naturally as dolphins and live among the deepest depths without care for cold, darkness, or pressure. As such, they're a rare and mysterious sight for those mortals who dwell on land but well-known to denizens of the sea, such as merfolk, for whom they're often confused.

Oceanids can be as tempestuous as their watery home, with moods that change on a whim. They're quick to love and even quicker to anger. At heart, however, they're nurturing guardians, especially to the young, the elderly, the injured, and the desperate. It's not unheard of for oceanids to take in and raise children who've been abandoned near the shore, and sailors who speak of them with respect often miraculously survive storms and sinkings that otherwise leave no survivors.

spell->Hydraulic Torrent.name: Hydraulic Torrent
spell->Hydraulic Torrent.description:
A swirling torrent of water manifests along a straight line, battering creatures and unattended objects in its path and possibly pushing them away from you. The torrent deals 8d6 bludgeoning damage. Each creature in the area must attempt a basic Fortitude save; unattended objects automatically fail. Creatures and objects that fail are also knocked back 5 feet (10 feet on a critical failure).

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Crashing Wave.name: Crashing Wave
spell->Crashing Wave.description:
You summon a crashing wave that sweeps away from you. You deal 6d6 bludgeoning damage to creatures in the area. The water also extinguishes non-magical fires in the area.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Animal Messenger (Sea Life only).name: Animal Messenger (Sea Life only)
spell->Animal Messenger (Sea Life only).description:
You offer food, and an ordinary Tiny animal within range approaches to eat it. You imprint the image, direction, and distance of an obvious place or landmark well known to you within the animal. You can also attach a small object or note up to light Bulk to it. The animal does its best to reach the destination; if it makes it there, it waits nearby and allows nonhostile creatures to approach and remove the attached object. The spell ends after the message is delivered or after 24 hours, whichever comes first.

If there are no Tiny wild animals in range, the spell is lost.

spell->Mist.name: Mist
spell->Mist.description: You call forth a cloud of mist. All creatures within the mist become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, and all creatures outside the mist become concealed to creatures within it. You can Dismiss the cloud.

spell->Water Breathing.name: Water Breathing
spell->Water Breathing.description:
The targets can breathe underwater.

Heightened (3rd) The duration increases to 8 hours.

Heightened (4th) The duration increases to until your next daily preparations.

spell->Hydraulic Push.name: Hydraulic Push
spell->Hydraulic Push.description:
You call forth a powerful blast of pressurized water that bludgeons the target and knocks it back. Make a ranged spell attack roll.

Critical Success The target takes 6d6 bludgeoning damage and is knocked back 10 feet.

Success The target takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage and is knocked back 5 feet.

Heightened (+1) The bludgeoning damage increases by 2d6.

action->Animal Empathy.name: Animal Empathy
action->Animal Empathy.description: An oceanid can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals, and gets a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to influence sea life.

action->Ocean Dependency.name: Ocean Dependency
action->Ocean Dependency.description: An oceanid who moves more than 500 feet away from access to a saltwater sea for 24 hours gains the weak adjustments until they return and submerge themself for at least 10 minutes.

action->Waveshaper.name: Waveshaper
action->Waveshaper.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The oceanid takes 1 minute to create waves and currents to double or halve the speed of creatures, objects, or vehicles traveling along the surface of the water within 1,000 feet, affecting up to 100 contiguous 5-foot squares in a shapable area (typically enough to affect 1 galley, 2 longships, or 3 cutters). This ability requires a line of sight to some part of the area and can be Sustained for up to 10 minutes. An unwilling creature can resist the effect by succeeding at a @Check[fortitude|dc:25] save, which must be repeated once per minute for as long as it remains within the affected area.

Oceanid Queen.name: Oceanid Queen
Oceanid Queen.publicNotes:
While one oceanid queen may rule over an entire inland sea, the majority define their territories in the vast, wide-open ocean by the flow of currents, the edges of continental shelves, and the curves of recurring weather patterns. As such, the boundaries between oceanid queendoms are both literally and figuratively fluid, making them difficult for land-born creatures to comprehend. Wise sailors know to avoid offending any oceanid queen, as those who do are forced to retire lest they accidentally stumble into the domain of the ruler they insulted, who will not hesitate to capsize entire fleets in revenge.

Where naiads are bound to their freshwater springs and nereids walk as they will between wave and shore, oceanid nymphs are, to their cores, creatures of the seas. They ride the open waves as naturally as dolphins and live among the deepest depths without care for cold, darkness, or pressure. As such, they're a rare and mysterious sight for those mortals who dwell on land but well-known to denizens of the sea, such as merfolk, for whom they're often confused.

Oceanids can be as tempestuous as their watery home, with moods that change on a whim. They're quick to love and even quicker to anger. At heart, however, they're nurturing guardians, especially to the young, the elderly, the injured, and the desperate. It's not unheard of for oceanids to take in and raise children who've been abandoned near the shore, and sailors who speak of them with respect often miraculously survive storms and sinkings that otherwise leave no survivors.

spell->Control Water.name: Control Water
spell->Control Water.description:
Area 50 feet long by 50 feet wide

By imposing your will upon the water, you can raise or lower the level of water in the chosen area by 10 feet. Creatures that have the water trait and that are in the area when you Cast the Spell must attempt a Fortitude save, with the effects of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WsUwpfmhKrKwoIe3]{Slow} spell.

spell->Hydraulic Torrent.name: Hydraulic Torrent
spell->Hydraulic Torrent.description:

Each creature in the area must attempt a basic Fortitude save; unattended objects automatically fail. Creatures and objects that fail are also knocked back 5 feet (10 feet on a critical failure).

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Hydraulic Push.description:

action->Animal Empathy.description: An oceanid queen can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals, and gets a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to influence sea life.

action->Tied to the Sea.name: Tied to the Sea
action->Tied to the Sea.description: An oceanid queen is intrinsically tied to a dominion of the sea, which may include some solid boundaries around or above the surface, such as shorelines, islands, or coral reefs, but is more prominently defined by currents and weather patterns. This otherwise acts as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.UHuA1hue5xrRM6KK]{Tied to the Land}.

action->(Nymph Queen) Nymph's Beauty.name: (Nymph Queen) Nymph's Beauty
action->(Nymph Queen) Nymph's Beauty.description: 30 feet. Creatures that start their turn in the emanation must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:35] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

action->Waveshaper.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The oceanid takes 1 minute to create waves and currents to double or halve the speed of creatures, objects, or vehicles traveling along the surface of the water within 1,000 feet, affecting up to 100 contiguous 5-foot squares in a shapable area (typically enough to affect 1 galley, 2 longships, or 3 cutters). This ability requires a line of sight to some part of the area and can be Sustained for up to 1 hour. An unwilling creature can resist the effect by succeeding at a @Check[fortitude|dc:35] save, which must be repeated once per minute for as long as it remains within the affected area.

action->(Nymph Queen) Change Shape.name: (Nymph Queen) Change Shape
action->(Nymph Queen) Change Shape.description:
Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a more humanoid-looking version of their natural form.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

action->(Nymph Queen) Focus Beauty.name: (Nymph Queen) Focus Beauty
action->(Nymph Queen) Focus Beauty.description:
Requirements The target creature is affected by the oceanid queen's nymph's beauty aura

Effect The required creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 hour and is blown 120 feet away from the queen by a punctuating wave of water.

action->(Nymph Queen) Inspiration.name: (Nymph Queen) Inspiration
action->(Nymph Queen) Inspiration.description:
The nymph queen inspires a single intelligent creature by giving that creature a token of her favor, typically a lock of her hair, though it can be some other significant object as well. As long as the creature carries her token and remains in good standing with her, the creature gains a +1 status bonus to all Crafting checks, Performance checks, and Will saves.

If the nymph grants her token to a bard, and she's the bard's muse, the queen chooses one additional benefit granted by her token: a +1 status bonus to all Lore checks, a +2 status bonus to Performance checks when determining the effects of compositions, a +4 status bonus to untrained skill checks, or a +2 status bonus to Will saves against fey.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.iSyyR4QVOaY6mxtg]{Effect: Nymph Queen's Inspiration}

action->Ocean's Grasp.name: Ocean's Grasp
action->Ocean's Grasp.description:
Effect Water surrounds one creature within 60 feet. The target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:38] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes @Damage[3d10[bludgeoning]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 1 round or until it Escapes.

Failure As success, but @Damage[6d10[bludgeoning]] damage and immobilized for 1 minute.

Critical Failure As success, but @Damage[9d10[bludgeoning]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} for 1 minute.

Orphne.name: Orphne
Orphne.publicNotes: Orphnes are cruel and enigmatic fey courtiers obsessed with exploring the artistry of decay. They're unnervingly beautiful, yet leave behind slow rot wherever they linger. Though interested in all forms of decomposition, orphnes are particularly enamored with mortal death as a canvas for elegance. Most have a fascination with undeath, practicing necromancy in pursuit of the aesthetics of stillness, preservation, and cruel irony. Despite their sadism, orphnes carefully follow the refined manners of high society. They expect reverence or admiration, and they often grow dangerous when denied it.

spell->Calm.name: Calm
spell->Calm.description:
You forcibly calm creatures in the area, soothing them into a nonviolent state; each creature must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success Calming urges impose a -1 status penalty to the creature's attack rolls.

Failure Any emotion effects that would affect the creature are suppressed and the creature can't use hostile actions. If the target is subject to hostility from any other creature, it ceases to be affected by calm.

Critical Failure As failure, but hostility doesn't end the effect.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.Qr5rgoZvI4KmFY0N]{Spell Effect: Calm}

spell->Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
spell->Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an invisibility potion) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Glamorize.name: Glamorize
spell->Glamorize.description:
Using simple magical gestures, you alter a minor detail of your appearance (add or remove highlights to your hair color, apply or remove cosmetics, add polish or accessories to your nails, etc.) or create a small environmental effect that's confined to your person (adjust surrounding lighting to favor your good side, cause a brief wind to make your hair blow dramatically, make a small chime occur as you smile, etc.). While the spell is active, you can Sustain it to make further adjustments. The changes persist until the spell's duration ends.

At the GM's discretion, such alterations might grant a +1 status bonus to certain tasks, such as Impersonate or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EEDElIyin4z60PXx]{Perform}.

spell->Illusory Disguise.name: Illusory Disguise
spell->Illusory Disguise.description:
You create an illusion that causes the target to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise is typically good enough to hide their identity, but not to impersonate a specific individual. The spell changes their appearance and voice, but not mannerisms. You can change the appearance of its clothing and worn items, such as making its armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item removed from the creature returns to its true appearance.

Casting illusory disguise counts as setting up a disguise for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} use of Deception; it ignores any circumstance penalties the target might take for disguising itself as a dissimilar creature, gives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through the disguise, and lets the target add its level to such Deception checks even if untrained. You can Dismiss this spell.

Heightened (3rd) The target can appear as any creature of the same size, even a specific individual. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 willing creatures. If you target multiple creatures, you can choose a different disguise for each target, but none can impersonate a specific individual. You can Dismiss each disguise individually or all collectively.

Heightened (7th) As 4th, but you can choose disguises that impersonate specific individuals. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3Ktyd5F9lOPo4myk]{Spell Effect: Illusory Disguise}

spell->Summon Undead.name: Summon Undead
spell->Summon Undead.description:
You summon a creature that has the undead trait and whose level is -1 to fight for you.

Heightened As listed in the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.8gcp880pEWZ9VPnF]{summon} trait.

spell->Void Warp.name: Void Warp
spell->Void Warp.description:
You call upon the Void to harm life force. The target takes 2d4 void damage with a basic Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} until the start of your next turn.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4.

action->Hollow Grace.name: Hollow Grace
action->Hollow Grace.description: 30 feet. Living creatures in the emanation take a –1 status penalty to saving throws against emotion and void effects, and regain half as many Hit Points from vitality and healing effects. Undead creatures in the emanation gain a +1 status bonus to attack and damage rolls and gain resistance 5 to vitality damage. This aura is suppressed while the orphne is within the area of a holy consecrate ritual or similar effect.

action->Bone Dance.name: Bone Dance
action->Bone Dance.description:
Frequency once per hour

Trigger The orphne is targeted by an attack or spell that deals damage

Effect With a graceful motion, the orphne shifts out of phase with reality, appearing as a skeletal figure surrounded by trailing mist. They gain void healing and resistance 5 to all damage (except force, ghost touch, spirit, or vitality) against the triggering attack or spell.

action->Necrotic Pulse.name: Necrotic Pulse
action->Necrotic Pulse.description:
Effect The orphne releases a focused wave of necrotic energy in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15]. Each living creature in the area takes @Damage[6d6[void]|options:area-damage] damage and must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:22] save. The orphne can't use Necrotic Pulse again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Necrotic Pulse]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} for 1 minute.

action->Withering Stare.name: Withering Stare
action->Withering Stare.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The orphne fixes their chilling gaze on a living creature within 60 feet, terrifying a potential victim and draining its will to fight. The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:22] save; if already enfeebled, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is frightened 1 and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for as long as it remains frightened.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Pech.name: Pech
Pech.publicNotes:
The riotous clamor of stone against stone in the First World often heralds the presence of a hidden pech quarry. While peches may use tools and their innate magic for mining and construction, such is the extent of their practicality. These subterranean fey are otherwise wholly committed to using their bodies alone to refine earthen bounty, crushing stone bare-handed and cutting gemstones against their muscles to create art. To chisel and polish their muscles of stone, peches pursue their crafts with near obsession, honing their skills—and physiques—to the highest possible pinnacle. Their sequestered settlements give them the privacy to pursue their ascetic lifestyles, though peches are surprisingly unperturbed by well-meaning visitors. They're aware of the great effort needed for a mortal to reach their abodes and acknowledge those who accomplish such a feat, especially outsiders who express interest in stonecraft or bodybuilding. Peches might even honor an especially skilled guest with a gift: one of their highly coveted stone crafts, created through years, if not decades, of labor. For outsiders who cause trouble, however, peches offer only the full force of their supernatural strength.

Peches are short-statured humanoids with chiseled, stony physiques that become increasingly polished as they grow more skilled in their trades. Their stony skin naturally grows patches of moss, which resembles hair, and many peches cultivate this moss in various styles to complement the presentation of their muscles.

spell->Speak with Stones (Constant).name: Speak with Stones (Constant)
spell->Speak with Stones (Constant).description:
You can ask questions of and receive answers from natural or worked stone. While stone is not intelligent, you speak with the natural spirits of the stone, which have a personality colored by the type of stone, as well as by the type of structure the stone is part of, for worked stone. A stone's perspective, perception, and knowledge give it a worldview different enough from a human's that it doesn't consider the same details important. Stones can mostly answer questions about creatures that touched them in the past and what is concealed beneath or behind them.

Heightened (6th) The duration is 8 hours.

spell->Shape Stone (At Will).name: Shape Stone (At Will)
spell->Shape Stone (At Will).description:
You shape the stone into a rough shape of your choice. The shaping process is too crude to produce intricate parts, fine details, moving pieces, or the like. Any creatures standing atop the stone when you reshape it must each attempt a Reflex save or Acrobatics check.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} atop the stone.

Critical Failure The creature falls off the stone (if applicable) and lands Prone.
spell->Shape Stone (At Will).target: cube of stone 10 feet across or smaller

action->+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Intimidating Flex.name: Intimidating Flex
action->Intimidating Flex.description:
Requirements The pech's last action was to knock a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}

Effect The pech flexes menacingly, attempting to [[/act demoralize]] a target other than the required creature. This Demoralize attempt has the visual trait instead of the auditory trait and doesn't take a penalty if the target doesn't share a language with the pech. On a success, the target also becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the pech until the start of the pech's next turn.

action->Rock Solid Stunner.name: Rock Solid Stunner
action->Rock Solid Stunner.description:
The pech drives a foe into the ground where it belongs. The pech Leaps up to 25 feet, making a melee Strike at any point during the jump. This movement doesn't trigger reactions. On a successful Strike, the target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] save.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2}.

Poludnica.name: Poludnica
Poludnica.publicNotes:
Don't go into the fields—so say the village elders—when the sun is highest and the sky is the blue of a robin's egg. That's when the poludnica, the noonday demon, walks the furrows, and to meet them is death.

Of course, some don't listen. At planting and at harvest, those few extra hours in the middle of the day can mean the difference between making it through the winter and starving to death. Desperation is a powerful force, and while it's just possible some old fireside legend might kill you, hunger most assuredly will. When need isn't at play, greed does a good impression, and pride too. Just a little more work, a little bigger harvest, that little bit extra to impress—who? Yourself? Your spouse? Parents, neighbors, or even your landlord?

So, some harvesters enter the fields while the sun beats down like a hammer: the desperate, the greedy, and the foolish alike, and if they're lucky, all they have to fear is heat exhaustion, sunstroke, and dehydration. If they're unlucky, they come across a lone stranger in the fields: a young woman dressed in a kaftan of purest white, so bright it hurts to look upon, with eyes blue as cornflowers. Sometimes it's a young man instead, sometimes their clothing is pale blue, sometimes they might appear as a young child or wizened elder. Always they hold a scythe, a sickle, or a pair of old pruning shears.

The poludnica asks questions—they're fond of riddles and trick questions, confusing nonsense—all while the sun glares and the fey twists in your sight like a mirage. Answer wrongly, or stay silent, and she'll clout you on the head, causing headaches or madness. Or perhaps they'll simply bring that sickle down and slice your head clean off. They'll bury the body then, right there in the fields, and the harvest that rises from that land will be the richest in a hundred years. The people will nod, and the village elders will have a new story to tell, and perhaps in a decade or two, some new fool will die in the fields. And in exchange for their presence, the harvest grows rich and ripe, and hunger stays at bay.

Poludnicas are proud and territorial fey—a deadly threat, but a manageable one on the whole, if you're wise and listen to those who know better. They guard their fields and their time closely, and view outsiders as trespassers to be dealt with. At the same time, poludnicas don't actually hate their mortal neighbors. A poludnica's relationship with "their" village has a parental bent, that of a shepherd to their sheep (including taking the occasional meal of mutton). A poludnica ensures the harvest is good and locals don't starve, which sometimes means culling the occasional fool who fails to show respect. No one's entirely sure what poludnicas get in the exchange, though. Mortals say that poludnicas dally with mortals, ensuring their line is continued onward. Given that, like all fey, poludnicas are immortal, this is likely just some farmhand's wishful thinking. Other fey simply think that poludnicas are all stuck-up and enjoy having someone in mortal terror of them. This is more plausible.

There's an old story that says that Poludnica—just a single fey in the story—was one of four sisters: the midday star. Beside her was the youngest, Zarya, the dawn star, the evening star, Vechernitsa, and the midnight star, Nochnitsa. Together, they oversaw the proper course of the hours and the transition from darkness to light and back. They rarely quarreled, though rarely saw eye to eye, either. Supposedly, a mortal caught out by a poludnica should suggest they're on an errand for one of their sisters, especially Nochnitsa, whom Poludnica never sees. The fey might suspect a ruse, but they're likelier to let the mortal go on their way than risk aggravating their sisters.

Another story claims that the noonday demons love dancing and are better at it than any mortal. When the sun is highest and the fields are empty, they dance, alone or in great gatherings. If they meet a mortal during this time, perhaps some farmer dozing the day away, they'll wake them and implore them to dance—on pain of death. A poludnica will dance from noon till dusk, but if the mortal can keep up with them through heat and exhaustion, the impressed fey will reward them richly, with blessings of good fortune, protection, and a purse of gold for good measure.

spell->Nature's Pathway (Fields of Grain.name: Nature's Pathway (Fields of Grain instead of Trees)
spell->Nature's Pathway (Fields of Grain.description:
You step into a living tree with a trunk big enough for you to fit inside it and instantly teleport to any tree within 5 miles that also has a sufficiently large trunk. Once you enter the first tree, you instantly know the rough locations of other sufficiently large trees within range and can exit from the original tree, if you prefer. You can't carry extradimensional spaces with you; if you attempt to do so, the spell fails.

Heightened (6th) The tree you exit can be up to 50 miles away.

Heightened (8th) The tree you exit can be up to 500 miles away.

Heightened (9th) The tree you exit can be anywhere on the same planet.

spell->Confusion.name: Confusion
spell->Confusion.description:
You befuddle your target with strange impulses, causing it to act randomly. The effects are determined by the target's Will save. You can Dismiss the spell.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target babbles incoherently and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 minute. It can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns to end the confusion.

Critical Failure The target is Confused for 1 minute, with no save to end early.

Heightened (8th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

spell->Wall of Fire.name: Wall of Fire
spell->Wall of Fire.description:
You raise a blazing wall that burns creatures passing through it. You create either a 5-foot-thick wall of flame in a straight line up to 60 feet long and 10 feet high, or a 5-foot-thick, 10-foot-radius ring of flame with the same height.
