Heightened (5th) The instrument is instead a virtuoso handheld instrument.

spell->Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
spell->Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

equipment->Tortoiseshell Lyre.name: Tortoiseshell Lyre
equipment->Tortoiseshell Lyre.description:
A maestro's instrument can be crafted in the form of any variety of handheld musical instruments. A maestro's instrument grants you a +3 item bonus to Performance checks while playing music with the instrument.

Activate—Charming Performance 2 (manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect You play the instrument, causing it to cast a 8th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm} spell with DC 38.

Craft Requirements You must supply a casting of charm of the appropriate rank.

action->+2 Status to All Saves vs. Fear.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Fear

action->Been A Long Time.name: Been A Long Time
action->Been A Long Time.description: It's been so long since the seilenos has been sick or felt fear that it shocks them. The first time each day that they fail a save against a fear effect or take poison damage (after resistances), they also become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

action->That's New!.name: That's New!
action->That's New!.description: The seilenos is compelled by a truly novel performance, even if it's an old song performed in a unique way. A creature that succeeds on a Performance check to [[/act perform]] against the seilenos's Will DC earns their grudging respect and encouragement, granting the performer a +2 status bonus to Performance checks for 1 minute.

action->Dancing Figments.name: Dancing Figments
action->Dancing Figments.description: When the seilenos casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Ucf8eynbZMfUucjE]{Illusory Scene}, they can channel the spell through their music or storytelling. If they do, they cast it with 2 actions, it gains the auditory and subtle traits, and its duration becomes sustained up to 1 hour. In addition, the creatures in their scene can cause damage, as 10th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.f8SBoXiXQjlCKqly]{illusory creatures} which are all Sustained whenever the seilenos Sustains illusory scene.

action->Strum the Lyre.name: Strum the Lyre
action->Strum the Lyre.description:
Requirements The seilenos is holding a musical instrument

Effect The seilenos prances about while playing a melody infused with enchanting primal magic. The seilenos Casts charm, fear, sleep, or suggestion, expending the spell normally. A spell cast this way gains the auditory trait and targets all creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60] instead of its usual targets. A creature that succeeds at its Will save against any spell cast this way becomes temporarily immune to all spells cast with Strum the Lyre for 1 minute.

Selkie.name: Selkie
Selkie.publicNotes:
The haunting songs that sometimes accompany pods of seals are from selkies, fey who freely shift between human and seal forms. Their natural forms belong fully to neither world, sporting a mix of human and seal features.

Selkies move through the water and on the shore with equal ease, and seaside communities often talk of them as though they were the tide itself. Despite these poetic associations, however, the life of a selkie exists far beyond the imagination of land-bound mortals. For selkies, losing either the land or the sea is to lose a part of themselves. They eagerly seek kinship with others who exist in multiple worlds and are often found as surprise guests at the celebrations of azarketis or merfolk.

spell->Noise Blast.name: Noise Blast
spell->Noise Blast.description:
A cacophonous noise blasts out, dealing 2d10 sonic damage. Each creature must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage, is deafened for 1 minute, and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10.

spell->Silence.name: Silence
spell->Silence.description:
The target makes no sound, preventing creatures from noticing it using hearing alone. The target can't use sonic attacks, nor can it use actions with the auditory trait. This prevents it from casting spells due to the magical words involved in casting, with the exception of subtle spells.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.mmJNE57hC7G3SPae]{Spell Effect: Silence}

Heightened (4th) The spell creates an aura in a 10-foot emanation around the touched creature, silencing all sound in or passing through it. While within the aura, creatures are subject to the same effects as the target. Depending upon the position of the effect, a creature might notice the lack of sound reaching it (blocking off the noise coming from a party, for example).

spell->Water Breathing.name: Water Breathing
spell->Water Breathing.description:
The targets can breathe underwater.

Heightened (3rd) The duration increases to 8 hours.

Heightened (4th) The duration increases to until your next daily preparations.

spell->Haunting Hymn.name: Haunting Hymn
spell->Haunting Hymn.description:
You echo a jarring hymn that only creatures in the area can hear. The hymn deals 1d8 sonic damage, with a basic Fortitude save. If a target critically fails the save, it's also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 minute.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d8.

weapon->Sealbone Dagger.name: Sealbone Dagger
weapon->Sealbone Dagger.description: This small, bladed weapon is held in one hand and used to stab a creature in close combat. It can also be thrown.

armor->Sealskin Coat.name: Sealskin Coat
armor->Sealskin Coat.description: A mix of furs, sturdy hide, and sometimes molded boiled leather, this armor provides protection due to its layers of leather, though its bulkiness slows the wearer down and decreases mobility.

action->Sealskin Coat.name: Sealskin Coat
action->Sealskin Coat.description:
A selkie can slip their seal pelt on and off as a sealskin coat. They're permanently bound to it and can sense its location if separated (as the locate spell). While wearing their sealskin coat, the selkie is immune to mild, severe, and extreme cold, and treats incredible cold as severe cold. They can also speak with seals (as speak with animals). When the selkie uses Change Shape, they must draw their sealskin coat around themself to become a seal or fully remove it to become a human. They can't leave their human form if their sealskin coat isn't in their possession.

If their sealskin coat is destroyed, the selkie feels its loss as an ever-present wound. They take a −1 status penalty to all attacks and saving throws, but they gain a +1 status bonus to seaborn yearning's DC and their edge of mourning deals @Damage[2d6[mental]] damage instead of 1d6.

action->Change Shape.name: Change Shape
action->Change Shape.description:
Selkies can transform between their original seal-like form and a human form. In human form, they have a land Speed of 25 feet and lose their swim Speed and jaws Strike. They gain the following unarmed attack:

Melee 1 fist +14 (agile, finesse, nonlethal, unarmed)

Damage 1d4+6 bludgeoning

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

action->Deep Breath.name: Deep Breath
action->Deep Breath.description: A selkie can hold their breath for 1 hour.

action->Edge of Mourning.name: Edge of Mourning
action->Edge of Mourning.description: A selkie's sealbone dagger Strikes deal an additional 1d6 mental damage.

action->Seaborn Yearning.name: Seaborn Yearning
action->Seaborn Yearning.description: 30 feet. When a selkie is outside of their home waters, their yearning for home radiates from them. A creature that enters or starts its turn in the aura must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:22] save or become unable to benefit from emotion effects for 1 minute (though they can still take penalties or damage from emotion effects); on a critical failure, the duration is 24 hours. Regardless of the result, the creature is temporarily immune to seaborn yearning for 24 hours.

Shadow Collector.name: Shadow Collector
Shadow Collector.publicNotes:
When the traitor Count Ranalc was banished to the Netherworld, loyal sprites, gnomes, and nymphs of his court were exiled alongside him. Millennia in the shadows changed these courtiers into shadow collectors—mirrials in their own tongue. These small fey prowl the Netherworld and its borderlands, searching out wayward shadows to add to their vast collections.

According to legend, when the fey who would become mirrials first arrived in the Netherworld, their new shadowy home's lack of light meant they no longer cast the same twisting shadows they'd had in the First World. Despairing, the fey crept into the Universe, stalking midnight forests and dreary foothills to steal the shadows of unsuspecting mortals. When these first few stolen shadows cast barely a single foot of darkness, they took more and more, weaving their treasures together until they had terrifying shadows the size of dragons and giants.

spell->Umbral Journey.name: Umbral Journey
spell->Umbral Journey.description: You move partially into the Netherworld, using its warped nature to speed your travels. Each hour, you cover roughly as much ground as you normally would in 3 days. The landmarks are vague and symbolic rather than concrete, leaving you within a mile of your intended destination when you Dismiss the spell or its duration ends.
spell->Umbral Journey.target: you and up to 10 willing creatures touched

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

spell->Illusory Disguise.name: Illusory Disguise
spell->Illusory Disguise.description:
You create an illusion that causes the target to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise is typically good enough to hide their identity, but not to impersonate a specific individual. The spell changes their appearance and voice, but not mannerisms. You can change the appearance of its clothing and worn items, such as making its armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item removed from the creature returns to its true appearance.

Casting illusory disguise counts as setting up a disguise for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} use of Deception; it ignores any circumstance penalties the target might take for disguising itself as a dissimilar creature, gives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through the disguise, and lets the target add its level to such Deception checks even if untrained. You can Dismiss this spell.

Heightened (3rd) The target can appear as any creature of the same size, even a specific individual. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 willing creatures. If you target multiple creatures, you can choose a different disguise for each target, but none can impersonate a specific individual. You can Dismiss each disguise individually or all collectively.

Heightened (7th) As 4th, but you can choose disguises that impersonate specific individuals. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3Ktyd5F9lOPo4myk]{Spell Effect: Illusory Disguise}

spell->Illusory Object.name: Illusory Object
spell->Illusory Object.description:
You create an illusory visual image of a stationary object. The entire image must fit within the spell's area. The object appears to animate naturally, but it doesn't make sounds or generate smells. For example, water would appear to pour down an illusory waterfall, but it would be silent.

Any creature that touches the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) Your image makes appropriate sounds, generates normal smells, and feels right to the touch. The spell gains the auditory and olfactory traits. The duration increases to 1 hour.

Heightened (5th) As the 2nd-rank version, but the duration is unlimited.

action->Steal Shadow.name: Steal Shadow
action->Steal Shadow.description:
Requirements The shadow collector is adjacent to an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} living creature

Effect The shadow collector attempts to pull the creature's shadow from its body. The target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:26] save.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The collector steals a scrap of the shadow, increasing the size of their shadow menagerie aura by 5 feet for 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, but the aura is increased by 10 feet and the collector steals the target's shadow permanently. The shadow is returned if the shadow collector dies or takes a Dismiss action to release the shadow.

action->Slip Behind.name: Slip Behind
action->Slip Behind.description: The shadow collector slips into a creature's shadow, teleporting to a space adjacent to that creature within 15 feet. The target or its items can't be emitting magical light, and if the target is within an area of magical light the shadow collector must choose a destination that puts the target between them and the light's source.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: The shadow collector's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

action->Umbral Detonation.name: Umbral Detonation
action->Umbral Detonation.description:
Requirements The radius of shadow menagerie is 20 feet or higher

Effect A long shadow yawns out from the menagerie, withering everything it touches. Each creature in a @Template[type:line|distance:60] takes @Damage[8d6[void]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:26|basic] save. A creature who critically fails is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round. The shadow collector's aura decreases by 10 feet.

Sluagh Reaper.name: Sluagh Reaper
Sluagh Reaper.publicNotes:
Most sluagh are reapers: powerful killers subservient to their queen. After they collect souls on a hunt, they dutifully return their plunder to the queen. Though quite clever, they're inscrutable, lacking the whimsy and sociability that characterize many living fey. They do show merriment on occasion though, giggling as their claws draw closer to their quarry's throat.

A soul about to leave its physical body gives off a peculiar scent, usually unnoticed by mortal creatures. But the undead fey called sluagh can smell and track down its location with frightening ease. Unlike most fey, sluagh are undead, possessing strong connections to void energy and mortal souls. Sluagh collect the souls of those close to death and bring them to feed their queen.

Most sluagh appear bald-headed, with rounded ears, sharp teeth, glossy black eyes, and scrawny bodies. Their rib cages show through their skin, which is translucent and soft as velvet.

Sluagh can become ghostly and incorporeal for brief periods. They use this power to stalk their prey to great effect. Sometimes the glimpse of a sluagh is mistaken for a ghost sighting.

spell->Invisibility.name: Invisibility
spell->Invisibility.description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

spell->Figment.name: Figment
spell->Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

action->Soulscent (Imprecise) 100 feet.name: Soulscent (Imprecise) 100 feet
action->Soulscent (Imprecise) 100 feet.description: The sluagh is aware of all @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed} creatures, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yZRUzMqrMmfLu0V1]{Dying} creatures, and creatures that died within the last hour within the listed range.

action->Ghostly Swoop.name: Ghostly Swoop
action->Ghostly Swoop.description: The sluagh reaper becomes incorporeal until the start of their next turn and Flies up to their fly Speed. While incorporeal, they are immune to precision damage and have resistance 10 to all damage (except force, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JQdwHECogcTzdd8R]{Ghost Touch}, or vitality); this resistance is doubled against non-magical damage. The sluagh reaper can't use Ghostly Swoop again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Ghostly Swoop]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: The sluagh reaper deals an additional 3d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

action->Steal Soul.name: Steal Soul
action->Steal Soul.description:
The sluagh reaper touches a dying creature or a creature that died within the past hour. If the target is a dying creature, it must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:28] save; on a failure, its dying value increases by 1 (2 on a critical failure). If the target is dead, the sluagh automatically imprisons its soul in a small, grimy sack that keeps stolen souls fresh.

The sack is magically locked. Any sluagh can open it without difficulty, but any others must [[/act pick-a-lock dc=35]]{Pick the Lock} or use @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (5th level; counteract DC 32). A creature can Interact to empty an unlocked sack, which frees the souls but doesn't return them to life. While a soul is imprisoned, it can't be brought back to life by any means short of a wish ritual or similar magic. The sack can hold 12 souls at a time. Sluagh reapers typically attempt to deliver the souls to a queen sluagh so she can devour them.

Sorrow Stitcher.name: Sorrow Stitcher
Sorrow Stitcher.publicNotes:
Sorrow stitchers, as their name suggests, are beings of intense sadness. Ages ago, their forebears transgressed against one of the great powers of the First World, and as a result, their entire people were exiled to the Universe, barred from returning in perpetuity. So severe is the denial of the joy and mirth of the First World that sorrow stitchers have lost the ability to experience any feeling beyond fear and sorrow.

Most sorrow stitchers spend their time seeking out things that might bring happiness, even though nothing can ever restore that emotion to them. They're especially drawn to areas of concentrated joy—parks, fairgrounds, parades and the like. Their proximity to mortal population centers can be troublesome, as their frustration over being unable to experience happiness often leads them to lash out at the very displays of joy that entice them.

Sorrow stitchers are pale, sallow folk. They shroud themselves in colorful patchwork cloaks, fruitlessly hoping the garish colors will bring them some measure of joy. Each sorrow stitcher also carries a magical needle that can briefly capture threads of fate. They use these needles to sew a mortal's happiness onto their own heart, hoping to steal it for themselves. Lacking the true power to weave fate, however, these threads quickly fray, leaving the sorrow stitcher more forlorn than ever.

spell->Wave of Despair.name: Wave of Despair
spell->Wave of Despair.description:
You inflict despair on creatures in the area. The effects for each creature are determined by its Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success For 1 round, the creature can't use reactions and must attempt another save at the start of its turn; on a failure, it is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for that turn as it sobs uncontrollably.

Failure As success, but the duration is 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, and the creature is automatically slowed 1 for 1 minute.

Heightened (7th) The area increases to a 60-foot cone.

spell->Translocate.name: Translocate
spell->Translocate.description:
You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

spell->Vision of Death.name: Vision of Death
spell->Vision of Death.description:
You force the target to see a vision of its own death. It takes 8d6 mental damage with a Will save. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by this spell, its vision becomes reality and kills it instantly.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for as long as it's frightened.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

spell->Fear (At Will).name: Fear (At Will)
spell->Fear (At Will).description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

weapon->Shadow Scissors.name: Shadow Scissors
weapon->Shadow Scissors.description: These blades come in a variety of shapes and styles, but they are typically 2 feet long.

action->First World Exile.name: First World Exile
action->First World Exile.description: A sorrow stitcher can't enter the First World. An effect that would transport them to that plane fails to affect them. They can't enter any planar gate or similar effect that would take them to the First World, voluntarily or involuntarily.

action->Hollow Heart Curse.name: Hollow Heart Curse
action->Hollow Heart Curse.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:26]

Effect The victim becomes immune to emotion effects, except those that cause fear or sorrow and this curse. In addition, the victim is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to sorrow stitchers and takes a –2 status penalty to attack rolls if they can see a sorrow stitcher.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: The sorrow stitcher's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

action->Sorrowful Gaze.name: Sorrowful Gaze
action->Sorrowful Gaze.description:
The shadow stitcher focuses their sorrow and anguish into their gaze, forcing another to feel what they feel, if even for a moment. A creature the shadow stitcher can see must attempt a @Check[will|dc:26] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round as tears well up in their eyes.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 minute as their eyes fill with tears. At the end of each of its turns, they can attempt a @Check[will|dc:26] save to end the condition early.

Critical Failure The target is blinded and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 minute while lost in sorrow.

Sporgout.name: Sporgout
Sporgout.languages: Can't speak, Speak with plants, Telepathy 100 feet (infected creatures only)
Sporgout.publicNotes:
Countless myths warn about the dangers of stepping into a ring of mushrooms, but few extend this caution to the hidden threat that often lurks beneath them. Sporgouts are born when mushroom colonies aiding in the decay of a corpse consume vast amounts of primal energy, whether because the body was a being of primal magic (like a leshy or arboreal) or because it died in an area of strong fey influence. These colonies become so infused with magic that they attain their own sentience as a singular sporgout, lying in wait underground to ambush those who carelessly draw near. Though once believed to be undead, sporgouts are not reanimated corpses; while they absorb the nutrients and magic of their host body, they are wholly new creatures.

Sporgouts resemble unnatural humanoids with bodies like rotting logs or burned or petrified wood, covered in a colorful riot of strange fungi and lichens. They have no eyes or mouths, though they turn their heads as if mimicking beings who use such features to communicate. They have little interest in interacting with strangers and are often mistaken for solitary creatures, but like mundane mushrooms, sporgouts can and do communicate with each other across long distances through a mycorrhizal network.

spell->Dominate (Mycosome-Infected creat.name: Dominate (Mycosome-Infected creatures only)
spell->Dominate (Mycosome-Infected creat.description:
You take command of the target, forcing it to obey your orders. If you issue an obviously self-destructive order, the target doesn't act until you issue a new order. The effect depends on its Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} as it fights off your commands.

Failure You control the target. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9qGBRpbX9NEwtAAr]{Controlled} condition, but it can attempt a Will save at the end of each of its turns. On a success, the spell ends.

Critical Failure As a failure, but the target receives a new save only if you give it a new order that is against its nature, such as killing its allies.

Heightened (10th) The duration is unlimited.

spell->Lignify.name: Lignify
spell->Lignify.description:
You turn the target's flesh slowly into wood. The target must attempt a Fortitude save. Creatures with the plant trait have a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against this spell.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Failure The target is slowed 1 and must attempt a Fortitude save at the end of each of its turns; this ongoing save has the incapacitation trait. On a failed save, the slowed condition increases by 1 (or 2 on a critical failure). A successful save reduces the slowed condition by 1. When a creature is unable to act due to the slowed condition from lignify, the creature is permanently non-magically petrified, though it's turned to wood instead of stone. The spell ends if the creature is magically petrified or the slowed condition is removed.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target is initially @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2}.

spell->Speak with Plants (Constant).name: Speak with Plants (Constant)
spell->Speak with Plants (Constant).description:
You can ask questions of and receive answers from plants and fungi, but the spell doesn't make them more friendly or intelligent than normal. Most normal plants and fungi have a distinctive view of the world around them, so they don't recognize details about creatures or know anything about the world beyond their immediate vicinity. Cunning plant or fungus monsters are likely to be terse and evasive, while less intelligent ones often make inane comments.

Heightened (4th) The duration is 8 hours.

spell->One with Plants.name: One with Plants
spell->One with Plants.description:
You can either transform into a plant or merge with plant matter. While transformed, you can't move or affect anything outside the plant, but you can cast spells as long as they don't require line of effect beyond the plant. You can Dismiss this spell.

  • Merge with Plants The spell's duration is 10 minutes. While casting the spell, you must touch a plant with enough volume to fit you and your possessions or the spell is disrupted. While merged, you can hear, but not see, what's going on outside the plant. If the plant takes damage while you're inside it, you're expelled from the plant and take 10d6 damage. Magic passage expels you without dealing damage. The spell ends if you're ever outside the plant.
  • Turn into a Plant The spell's duration is 8 hours. You become a Large plant—typically a tree. Perception checks don't reveal your true nature, but a successful Nature or Survival check against your spell DC reveals that you appear to be a plant that is strangely new to the area. While in this form, you can observe everything around you, using your normal senses. As a plant, your AC is 20, and only status bonuses, status penalties, circumstance bonuses, and circumstance penalties affect you. Any successes and critical successes you roll on Reflex saves are failures

spell->Vanishing Tracks.name: Vanishing Tracks
spell->Vanishing Tracks.description:
You obscure the tracks you leave behind. The DC of checks to Track you gains a +4 status bonus or is equal to your spell DC, whichever results in a higher DC.

Heightened (2nd) The duration increases to 8 hours.

Heightened (4th) The duration increases to 8 hours. The spell has a range of 20 feet and targets up to 10 creatures.

action->Sporesense.name: Sporesense
action->Sporesense.description: The sporgout can detect mycosome-infected creatures as a precise sense within the listed range.

action->Hidden Roots.name: Hidden Roots
action->Hidden Roots.description:
Trigger A creature within the sporgout's reach uses a move action or leaves a square during a move action it's using

Effect The sporgout infects the triggering creature with their mycosomes, then attempts to [[/act trip]] it.

action->Shimmer Spores.name: Shimmer Spores
action->Shimmer Spores.description: 30 feet. The sporgout constantly disperses mind-addling spores. A creature that enters or begins their turn in the emanation becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round unless it succeeds at a @Check[will|dc:31] save. Regardless of the result, the creature is temporarily immune for 1 minute unless it later becomes infected with mycosomes, at which point it must save against shimmer spores again the next time it enters the emanation.

action->Fungal Decomposition.name: Fungal Decomposition
action->Fungal Decomposition.description: The sporgout activates the spores inside a mycosome-infected creature within 60 feet, dealing @Damage[4d12[poison]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:34|basic] save). On a successful save, the creature is no longer infected.

action->Mycosomes.name: Mycosomes
action->Mycosomes.description: A creature hit by a sporgout's Strikes is infected with their fungal mycosomes for 1 minute if it isn't already. Infected creatures are more susceptible to some of the sporgout's abilities. An infected creature is considered infected by all sporgouts. This is a poison effect.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
action->Sneak Attack.description: The sporgout's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Spriggan Bully.name: Spriggan Bully
Spriggan Bully.publicNotes:
The typical spriggan is a bully who prefers to take live prisoners in fights, but only to ensure that they have a large stock of living victims to torment, tease, and abuse. They train to use their weapons in nonlethal, but still painful, ways.

When gnomes left the First World, many embraced and adapted to life in the Universe, but not all were so resilient. Those who instead hardened their hearts in this time formed insular communities that prioritized survival by any means necessary. Over generations, these communities lost their interest in joy and beauty, diverging into sour creatures called spriggans. In exchange for this loss, they gained an immunity to the Bleaching and the ability to grow in size for short periods of time to increase their odds of survival—or better menace their victims. Over time, spriggans' culture of ruthless pragmatism has become one of sadistic cruelty, their only joy derived from visiting harm upon others.

spell->Shatter.name: Shatter
spell->Shatter.description:
A high-frequency sonic attack shatters a nearby object. You deal 2d10 sonic damage to the object, ignoring the object's Hardness if it is 4 or lower.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10, and the Hardness the spell ignores increases by 2.

spell->Fear.name: Fear
spell->Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

spell->Light.name: Light
spell->Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

action->Enraged Growth.name: Enraged Growth
action->Enraged Growth.description:
Trigger The spriggan bully takes damage

Effect The spriggan bully grows to Large size, along with their equipment (which returns to natural size if removed). The spriggan bully's reach increases by 5 feet. They regain @Damage[5[healing]] Hit Points and gain a +2 status bonus to melee attacks and damage rolls. This effect continues until the end of the spriggan bully's next turn, but on any turn in which the spriggan bully deals damage to another creature and is not @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued}, the effect extends until the end of the following turn.

When Enraged Growth ends, the spriggan bully is fatigued for 1 hour.

action->Bully's Bludgeon.name: Bully's Bludgeon
action->Bully's Bludgeon.description: The spriggan bully makes a morningstar Strike with a +2 circumstance bonus to its attack roll. This attack is nonlethal.

action->Sneak Attack.description: The spriggan bully's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

weapon->Spiked Rings.name: Spiked Rings
weapon->Spiked Rings.description: Providing the same defensive function as a standard gauntlet, this version has a group of spikes protruding from the knuckles.

equipment->Barbed Net.name: Barbed Net
equipment->Barbed Net.description:
You can use a net either on its own or attached to a rope. When attached to a rope, you can use the net to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.PMbdMWc2QroouFGD]{Grapple} a Medium or smaller creature up to 10 feet away (instead of only adjacent creatures). You can continue to Grapple to keep your hold on the target so long as the target remains within 10 feet and you continue to hold the net. The grabbed creature gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Escape unless you are adjacent to them, and it can attempt a @Check[athletics|dc:16|traits:action:force-open] check to Force Open the net entirely. Once the target is no longer grabbed, the net is unwieldy until refolded with an Interact action with the concentrate trait that requires two hands; if used without being refolded, Grapple checks made with the net take a -2 penalty.

When the net is unattached, you can attempt a ranged attack roll using your simple weapon proficiency against a Medium or smaller creature within 20 feet. On a hit, the target is off-guard and takes a -10- foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it Escapes, and on a critical hit, it's also immobilized until it Escapes. The Escape DC is 16 ([[/act escape dc=16]]). A creature adjacent to the target can Interact to remove the net.

action->Spoilsport.name: Spoilsport
action->Spoilsport.description:
Trigger A creature targets an ally with an attack and the spriggan stooge can see both creatures

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.K8gT1KR7T8ypcAkp]{Effect: Spoilsport}

action->Bully's Bludgeon.name: Bully's Bludgeon
action->Bully's Bludgeon.description: The spriggan stooge makes a ringed fist Strike with a +2 circumstance bonus to its attack roll. This attack is nonlethal.

action->Cruel Net.name: Cruel Net
action->Cruel Net.description: On a successful barbed net Strike, the stooge's target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} and takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds. On a critical hit, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} instead. Each time a creature attempts to Escape or Interact to remove the net, it takes @Damage[1d6[piercing]] damage from the net's barbs, regardless of whether the attempt succeeds.

action->Obvious Flattery.name: Obvious Flattery
action->Obvious Flattery.description:
Requirements An ally succeeded at a Strike against an opponent within the last round

Effect The spriggan stooge croons unctuous praise to the required ally, granting them a +1 circumstance bonus to the next saving throw they attempt before the end of their next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.eyexFwHFWpEFxAZo]{Effect: Obvious Flattery}

Spriggan warlords often serve as sub-commanders in large groups, filling roles in spriggan society akin to captains of the guard or bodyguards to spriggan royalty. In smaller groups or remote outposts, a single spriggan warlord is typically in charge of a band of spriggan bullies.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.MuRBCiZn5IKeaoxi]{Spell Effect: Fly}

Heightened (7th) The duration increases to 1 hour.

spell->Blur.name: Blur
spell->Blur.description: The target's form appears blurry. It becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}. As the nature of this effect still leaves the target's location obvious, the target can't use this concealment to Hide or Sneak.

spell->Dispel Magic.name: Dispel Magic
